title: Mechanical adaptation drives out-of-equilibrium network reorganization and self-strengthening in adapt-ring networks
abstract: Synthetic polymer networks typically lack the ability to autonomously remodel and strengthen under mechanical stress, a capability commonly observed in natural materials. Here we introduce adapt-ring networks (ARNs) that establish a general design principle for adaptive polymer materials. ARNs couple a covalent polyethylene glycol network with reconfigurable α-cyclodextrin crystalline domains whose strain-directed fragmentation, translocation and alignment form kinetically trapped architectures encoding local mechanical history. Mechanical training enhances Young's modulus, tensile strength, fracture energy and fatigue threshold by up to an order of magnitude, with full reversibility through solvent-induced crystalline-domain reformation. Spatially resolved adaptation and 3D printability enable gradient materials and customized architectures. Incorporating polyethylene glycol side chains to form dangling-chain ARNs enables strain-controlled out-of-equilibrium growth through threading and crystallization of external α-cyclodextrins. These hydrogels autonomously generate spatially self-organized, strain-dependent reinforcement, including non-local, environment-fed stiffening conceptually analogous to biological reinforcement. These features establish a general approach to bio-inspired, non-equilibrium soft materials that adapt, remember, regrow and readapt.

title: Aptamers enable a distinct mode of conformational DNA recognition
abstract:
Abstract
                  Watson–Crick base-pairing defines the classical paradigm of nucleic-acid interactions, but growing research reveals noncanonical modes beyond this framework. Here we uncover a mode of interactions by which two DNA strands associate through a ligand-induced conformational rearrangement. Upon binding a small molecule, a structure-switching primary aptamer folds into a conformation that exposes a previously inaccessible docking interface. An independently evolved secondary aptamer recognizes this interface primarily through noncanonical interactions rather than sequence complementarity, reporting the ligand-bound state of the primary aptamer. This interaction is conformation-sensitive: single base-pair changes in the primary aptamer modulate secondary aptamer recognition. Across four chemically distinct small-molecule targets—serotonin, dopamine, testosterone and deoxycorticosterone 21-glucoside—secondary aptamers were identified for three, and the serotonin system was translated into surface-based sandwich assays. These results demonstrate that a ligand-induced conformational state, rather than sequence complementarity or the chemical identity of the ligand, can serve as the epitope for nucleic-acid recognition, expanding the molecular features that DNA can be evolved to detect.

title: A binuclear copper enzyme platform for enantioconvergent radical (pseudo)halogenation
abstract: Despite their intriguing native metalloenzymology, naturally occurring copper enzymes remain underexploited for new-to-nature biocatalytic reactions. Here we report the systematic investigation and reprogramming of natural copper enzymes to catalyse unnatural free-radical (pseudo)halogenation reactions with high enantioselectivity. Evaluation of Cu enzymes in the decarboxylative azidation of redox-active esters revealed activity across multiple copper enzyme families, with type III binuclear copper enzymes, particularly Bacillus megaterium tyrosinase (BmTyr), exhibiting superior activity and enantioselectivity towards both stabilized and unstabilized alkyl radicals after further engineering. The strong halide binding affinity of the binuclear copper system also enabled challenging enantioconvergent bromination, chlorination and isothiocyanation reactions that remained inaccessible to repurposed non-haem iron enzymes. Electron paramagnetic resonance and ultraviolet-visible spectroscopic analyses confirmed the coupled binuclear nature of wild-type and engineered bacterial tyrosinases and provided insight into the origin of their enhanced activity. Collectively, this study establishes binuclear copper enzymes as a powerful platform for new-to-nature stereoselective radical reactions, expanding the scope of metalloenzyme catalysis beyond mononuclear systems. The image explains the catalytic activity of the binuclear copper enzyme tyrosinase from Bacillus megaterium with mutations V218A and N205M. The enzyme contains two copper ions each coordinated by three histidine residues. The enzyme acts on a substrate with two chiral centers labeled R superscript L and R superscript S. On the left, the substrate with an azide group (N3) attached to the R superscript S center is shown as a reactant. On the right, the product has a substituent labeled X, which can be chlorine, bromine, or thiocyanate, attached to the R superscript S center. The enzyme catalyzes the substitution of the azide group by X at the R superscript S position.

title: Endogenous virus-like extracellular vesicles enhance the efficacy of cancer vaccines

title: Repurposed endogenous virus-like vesicles mediate dendritic cell long-range antigen presentation and T cell activation for enhanced cancer vaccination
abstract: Dendritic cells release extracellular vesicles (DEVs) that amplify antigen presentation while incorporating patient-derived, rapidly evolving antigens. By enriching peptide-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) and co-stimulatory ligands orders of magnitude above donor-cell levels, DEVs emerge as potent vesicle-vaccines, although efficacy remains limited by unclear mechanisms. Here we show that dendritic cells repurpose the virus-like retrotransposon-derived Arc gene to generate endogenous virus-like vesicles (VLVs) that predominantly carry peptide-MHC and high-density co-stimulatory ligands, intensifying and extending antigen presentation. Upon antigen exposure, Arc partners with endogenous envelope proteins to assemble VLVs that directly engage T cells and trigger intrinsic adjuvanticity via viral mimicry. DEVs lacking Arc failed to prime antigen-specific T cell responses, whereas Arc overexpression shifted DEVs toward VLVs that trafficked to lymphoid organs, drove rapid CD4-assisted priming and durable CD8-biased memory, suppressed melanoma, and prolonged survival. Our data reveal a viral-mimicry mechanism enabling long-range immune activation and support Arc+ VLVs as an antigen-agnostic vaccine for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Atomically resolved exciton emission from single defects in MoS2
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Excitons, bound electron–hole pairs, govern the optical response of semiconductors and underpin technologies ranging from photovoltaics to quantum light sources. In nanoscale systems, the spatial extent of excitons approaches atomic dimensions, yet direct imaging of excitonic processes in real space has remained elusive. Two-dimensional semiconductors such as transition metal dichalcogenides provide a platform where reduced screening, high light extraction and atomically defined defect sites enable the exploration of exciton physics at atomic length scales. However, the microscopic origin of defect-related emission and its variability across samples have remained debated. Here we show that scanning tunnelling microscopy-induced luminescence reveals the atomic and optical fingerprints of individual defects in monolayer MoS
                    2
                    . Decoupling the material from its substrate using bilayer hexagonal boron nitride enables the detection of sharp excitonic emission and spatially localized defect emission, which we attribute to free-to-bound recombination (
                    e
                    ,A
                    0
                    ), and map its distribution with subnanometre-resolved fluorescence imaging. We identify negatively charged carbon–hydrogen complexes as the defect species responsible for a ubiquitous defect emission band in MoS
                    2
                    . These results provide atomically resolved images of exciton emission in a solid-state material, linking atomic defect structure to its optical fingerprint and establishing a microscopic basis for deterministic quantum emitter engineering in two-dimensional materials.

title: In situ CAR engineering and nanoparticle-mediated TREM2 degradation for macrophage reprogramming in malignant ascites
abstract: Peritoneal metastasis (PM) and the resulting malignant tumour ascites characterize advanced gastrointestinal cancers, often leading to poor prognosis and limited response to current therapies. Single-cell analysis of patient-derived PM and malignant tumour ascites reveals an approximately 90% enrichment of TREM2+-tumour-associated macrophages, which drive CD8+ T cell dysfunction and tumour growth. Here we develop lipid nanoparticles encapsulating mRNA to reprogram these tumour-associated macrophages into chimeric antigen receptor macrophages targeting Claudin18.2-positive tumour ascites. The lipid nanoparticles incorporate a TREM2+ ligand to enhance the targeting of TREM2 macrophages. The piperazine-containing phosphoramide ionizable lipid synergizes with the TREM2 ligand to inhibit ligand dissociation, promoting TREM2 internalization and degradation via lysosomal and autophagosomal pathways. This inhibits AKT signalling and reprograms tumour-associated macrophages towards an antitumour phenotype, enhancing progenitor exhausted and effector memory CD8+ T cell responses, altering the PM transcriptome, and reducing immunosuppression in both malignant tumour ascites and tumours. Combined with PD-1 blockade, this therapy suppresses tumour growth and extends survival in mice, and with matching immunological effects in clinical samples, demonstrates its translational potential for PM immunotherapy.

title: Spatiotemporal intensity-cycling microscopy unveils many-body interactions and correlated transport in van der Waals semiconductors
abstract: Spatiotemporal optical microscopies are powerful tools to image the propagation of energy carriers in materials, including electrons, excitons, magnons and polaritons, providing key functional metrics inaccessible to contact-based transport measurements. Nevertheless, these approaches do not distinguish single-particle from multi-particle quantum states, hindering the study of many-body correlations that underlie the complex phase diagrams at the heart of contemporary materials research. Here we extend a concept derived from multidimensional spectroscopy, called intensity cycling, to the spatiotemporal domain using transient scattering microscopy. We leverage this approach to selectively image single-particle and multi-particle transport in van der Waals semiconductors. We demonstrate a series of sought-after capabilities, including clean isolation of single-particle charge transport with high signal-to-noise ratio, spatiotemporal tracking of exciton-exciton annihilation, high-throughput mapping of dielectric disorder, and imaging the emergence of a polaronic Mott transition and correlated transport in a superatomic solid. This work delivers a precision tool capable of visualizing how many-body interactions shape material function.

title: A socio-economic resilience metric shifts disaster risk priorities
abstract: Using microsimulations, we quantify disaster-related decreases in material well-being, capturing not only what is damaged, but also how damage affects the population. We calculate socio-economic resilience — a population’s capacity to maintain well-being despite asset damages — and find that global well-being losses exceed US$1 trillion annually, representing about double the monetary asset damages.

title: The carbon at risk measure for managing carbon removal risk and guiding portfolio construction
abstract:
Abstract
                  Carbon removal markets lack a standardized, quantitative measure of permanence risk. Inspired by value at risk in financial markets, we propose carbon at risk (CaR): a probabilistic measure of the shortfall between contracted removals and realized storage at a given confidence level and time horizon. We calibrate CaR in two proof-of-concept applications: forest carbon, where Monte Carlo simulations driven by satellite fire data yield a single-project 95% CaR of more than 70% over 200 years for California, and geological storage, where simulations using the Storage Security Calculator show that the 95% CaR ranges from 0.15% (well-regulated offshore) to 17% (poorly regulated onshore). Combining technologies in a portfolio can help manage tail risk cost-effectively. The minimum cost of meeting a permanence target depends on the magnitude and correlation structure of key risk factors. CaR provides a technology-agnostic basis for risk-calibrated buffer sizing, insurance pricing and reserve-fund design, over both policy- and climate-relevant horizons.

title: Programming supramolecular polymer network topology via homochiral self-sorting
abstract: While stereochemistry has a strong influence on polymer structure and assembly, its use as a design handle to regulate polymer network topology remains unexplored. Here we demonstrate that homochiral self-sorting can be harnessed to suppress primary loops in end-linked polymer networks. We synthesized linear polymers terminated with heterochiral bi-2-naphthol-based ligands that cross-link via palladium(II)-mediated Pd2L4 metal-organic cage (MOC) assembly. This design exploits a thermodynamic preference for homochiral MOCs, enforcing a bias against intramolecular cyclization. Compared with networks formed from homochiral polymers, which can form primary loops through MOC formation, networks formed from heterochiral polymers exhibit lower primary loop densities and enhanced mechanical properties. The presence of sacrificial loops at low concentrations also enables topology editing by adding functionalized free ligands with minimal impact on network integrity. This work establishes chiral self-sorting as a versatile approach to controlling polymer topology and provides a generalizable strategy for designing robust and functional polymer networks.

title: Dynamic electrical control of on-chip second-harmonic generation with ferroelectric NbOBr2
abstract: Niobium oxide dihalide films show a second-harmonic generation (SHG) efficiency scaling with their thickness, owing to their weak interlayer electronic coupling, but their use in integrated nonlinear photonics has been limited by the lack of robust electrical tuneability. Here we integrate ferroelectric NbOBr2, of thicknesses ranging from 20 nm to 40 nm, with a silicon nitride microring resonator to realize electrically reconfigurable SHG on a photonic chip. NbOBr2 combines strong second-order susceptibility from intrinsic inversion-symmetry breaking with electrically switchable in-plane ferroelectric polarisation. By modulating the Schottky barrier at the NbOBr2-metal interface, ferroelectric switching controls carrier injection, free carrier absorption and dispersion, thereby tuning the cavity-enhanced nonlinear response. The device achieves an SHG conversion efficiency of 158% W-1 under continuous-wave excitation and a 53% electrical modulation depth. The polarisation states can also be programmed over multiple levels and retained after switching, enabling non-volatile control of the optical response. Using the fundamental and frequency-converted outputs as complementary channels, we further demonstrate dual-channel edge detection.

title: All IPCC AR6 regions are close to their 1.5 °C- and 2 °C-equivalent warming limits
abstract: Global temperatures have averaged 1.2 °C above pre-industrial levels over the past decade, yet regional warming patterns and remaining warming budgets under Paris Agreement limits remain uncertain owing to insufficient historical observations. Here we quantify and attribute warming across all IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) regions since pre-industrial times using a Bayesian framework combining multi-model simulations with observations, enabling robust estimates in data-sparse regions. Regional warming is already pronounced. By 2025, attributed regional warming had reached about 90–94% of the levels expected at 1.5 °C global warming and 65–76% of those expected at 2 °C. Attribution confidence is the highest in tropical regions, including much of Africa, where low internal variability enables robust results. Attributed warming is the greatest in northern high-latitude regions, exceeding 2.5 °C. Greenhouse gases dominate, partially offset by aerosol cooling. These results reveal that current warming is already indistinguishable from a 1.5 °C world, highlighting the shared urgency of adaptation across all regions. Climate targets are set for global temperatures, but what they mean regionally is less clear. Here the authors quantify the amount of human-induced warming in individual IPCC regions and find that, by 2025, they had reached 90–94% (65–76%) of their expected warming levels at the 1.5 °C (2 °C) global warming thresholds.

title: In Situ Displacement Reaction Enables a Conductive Metallized Hydrogel Interface for Smart Underwater Flexible Electronics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Underwater wearable sensing is severely hampered by the intrinsic drawbacks of conventional materials, including water absorption, swelling, and electrical drift during long-term immersion. Here, we develop an anti-swelling hydrogel with a surface-metallized layer, which achieves strong stability of both mechanical structure and electrical conductivity during long-term underwater immersion. The precise regulation of hydrophilic acrylamide and hydrophobic butyl acrylate enables anti-swelling performance, while an in-situ displacement reaction conveniently and readily constructs an interfacial silver layer on the hydrogel. The hydrogel exhibits remarkable mechanical sensing performance, including high pressure sensitivity, fast response/recovery times, and a broad tensile sensing range. The sensor is integrated into an electronic skin for motion and physiological monitoring (joint bending, respiration, electromyography, and electrocardiography). With AI assistance, this electronic skin achieves 93.75% accuracy in handwriting recognition via a ProbSparse Transformer model. More importantly, a waterproof multichannel sensing system is constructed for real-time monitoring of underwater finger movements and gesture-associated resistance responses. This hydrogel sensor thus serves as a simple, robust, and amphibious platform for healthcare and human-machine interfaces in both air and water.

title: Reconfigurable Exchange Bias Enabled by Photoresponsive Liquid Crystal Networks in FeGa/IrMn Magnetic Heterostructures
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Post-fabrication tunability of magnetic properties remains a key challenge for next-generation spintronic and adaptive magneto-electronic devices. Here, we report on a fully electrically contactless strategy to reversibly manipulate the magnetic response of an exchange-biased Ta/Fe80Ga20/Ir20Mn80/Ta multilayer stack through external light stimuli. A photoresponsive azobenzene-doped liquid crystal network (LCN) substrate is employed as an active support for the heterostructure capable of transferring controllable stress to the magnetostrictive FeGa layer under ultraviolet irradiation. This strain-mediated coupling induces a tunable uniaxial magnetic anisotropy in the device, enabling continuous, angular-dependent modulation of key magnetic parameters, including exchange bias and coercivity. Their variation reaches about 11% with respect to the unstressed state. Owing to the slow thermal relaxation kinetics of the LCN, the UV-induced magnetic state is retained after the illumination is switched off over timescales relevant for device operation and can be fully erased by subsequent green-light irradiation. Notably, both the magnitude and sign of the modulation are strongly angle-dependent, reflecting the interplay among stress-induced, magnetocrystalline, and interfacial (i.e., exchange coupling) anisotropies. This approach demonstrates a pathway toward reconfigurable, energy-efficient magnetic systems with remotely tunable functionality, offering significant advantages for miniaturized devices adaptable to dynamic, multi-stimuli environments.

title: Faster global mid-depth ocean connectivity in observations
abstract: Ocean circulation redistributes heat, carbon, and biogeochemical tracers through transport pathways connecting distant ocean regions, yet global connectivity of mid-depth transport pathways remains poorly constrained by observations. Here we establish an observational benchmark of global mid-depth water-mass connectivity, using more than 1.3 million displacements recorded by 9,920 Argo floats over the past two decades. The benchmark reveals that observed connectivity is generally faster than simulated, with mean connectivity timescales 23-29% shorter in the real ocean. This systematic discrepancy between observed and simulated mid-depth ocean connectivity arises from overestimated turnover timescales within subtropical gyre interiors and underrepresentation of rapid inter-basin exchanges along equatorial and western boundary pathways in the simulation-derived networks, particularly in the South Pacific and South Atlantic. These findings provide quantitative constraints on ocean interior transport, with broad implications for estimates of climate memory, tracer age, carbon sequestration, and marine biogeographic connectivity.

title: Promoting photocatalytic methane oxidative coupling via gradient oxidation field engineering
abstract: The efficient and selective photocatalytic oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) into valuable chemicals remains an unresolved challenge in modern science. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of a robust photocatalyst by constructing photocatalytic gradient oxidation field on mesoporous TiO2, which demonstrates exceptional OCM performance and outperforms other benchmark photocatalysts. The optimized photocatalytic system exhibits a high CH4 conversion rate of 1.2 mmol h−1, a high C2 hydrocarbon space-time yield of 82.7 mmol g−1 h−1 and 90.1% C2 selectivity, accompanied by a remarkable apparent quantum efficiency of over 11.6%. Mechanism analyses reveal that the gradient oxidation field introduced by the Au nanoislands and Pd atomic satellites can optimize the oxidation activity and selectivity with hydroxide and superoxide radicals, respectively. The synergistic interaction between the Au and Pd sites facilitates favorable adsorption of O2/CH4 reactants and promotes fast desorption of the C2H6 product, thereby accelerating the overall OCM process. This work demonstrates the critical role of photocatalytic oxidation field, and opens a new avenue for developing efficient and selective catalysts for various photocatalytic applications.

title: Rippled graphene pores as fluidic memristive devices with synaptic and neuromorphic functionalities
abstract: Nanofluidic memristive devices work with nanoscale pores (or channels) and ions dissolved in water, which harness the ionic memory effect aiming to store and process information. These devices share the same charge carriers as biological systems and bring hope for better emulating the neural functions and developing ionic circuits for neuromorphic applications. Specifically, theory and experiments suggest that nanoconfinement is essential for inducing a memory effect, which places a limit on the pore size to nm-scale or smaller. Such devices are, however, difficult to scale up with precision and operate with long-term stability. Here, we show that a micrometer size pore, generally expected to exhibit a linear ion transport, can display a pronounced memory effect, if its rim is wrapped by strongly curved and tightly stacked graphene. We attribute the observation to slow ion dynamics confined in the rippled graphene edges. The devices are easy to scale up and integrate into fluidic circuits. The memory effect is ion-selective and, crucially, exhibits long endurance, which enables reversible modification of the conductance states using programmable voltage spikes and various electrolytes over a long time, akin to biological synaptic plasticity. Thanks to this plasticity, our devices and their integrated circuits enable storing, transmitting and processing information with exceptionally high reliability, fidelity and accuracy, as evidenced by the effective processing of largescale and event-based information in the identification of both grayscale and color images, and in the real-time analysis of emulated neural signals. Our results highlight nanoscale morphology of the pore wall as an important parameter regulating ion transport, in addition to the well-documented pore’s charge and size, and indicate that the stringent nanoconfinement for ionic memory can be lifted from restricting the pore size to designing its rim structure. The devices and their integrated circuits may find use in ionic neuromorphic applications.

title: Conformational inversion mediated organic crystal actuator with extended stroke, self-healing, and optical switching
abstract: Dynamic molecular crystals with the capability to effectively convert thermal energy into mechanical work offer a compelling platform for microactuators. However, developing crystalline actuation materials that simultaneously achieve large and reversible deformation, rapid response, robust cyclability, and integrated optoelectronic functionality remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we take advantage of the conformational inversion of cyclohexyl groups and have rationally developed a dynamic organic crystal based on a dibenzothiophene sulfone derivative, BcDT, which exhibits exceptionally large, rapid, and reversible elongation. The thermally induced chair-to-boat conformational inversion of the introduced cyclohexyl moieties drives a cooperative phase transition that yields a linear elongation of ~14.3% along the crystal long axis, which delivers a work density of ~6.8 × 102 J m−3 and an efficiency of ~0.014%. Notably, the crystal features an uncommon self-healing capability, autonomously repairing macroscopic cracks during heating/cooling stages, ensuring its structural integrity and reliable actuation over multiple thermal cycles. The phase transition also enables reversible switching of linear and nonlinear optical properties, including a 4.2-fold modulation of two-photon excited fluorescence and tunable polarization anisotropy. Leveraging these properties, we demonstrate that BcDT crystals can function as microactuator devices to propel a heavy object and cooperatively lift a platform. This work establishes a molecular design strategy that integrates rapid, high-stroke actuation, self-healing, and optical switching within a single crystalline system, overcoming key functional limitations of current microactuators based on dynamic molecular crystals.

title: Nanomechanics of MXene Flakes at Gold Interfaces
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The demand for novel self-powering and sustainable electronics requires major efforts in identifying new advanced materials for nano-applications. MXenes have gathered attention due to their electronic and mechanical properties; however, their nanomechanical compliance against a metal-like interface is still not clearly identified. In this work, we employ atomic force microscopy to characterize the nanomechanical properties of a self-assembled thin flake of titanium carbide MXene (Ti3C2Tx) against a gold probe. The investigation returns an interfacial shear stress of 399 MPa and the observation of nano-wear localized in the center of the MXene flake. Nevertheless, MXene flakes retained their crystallinity in the tribofilms, as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy and electron energy loss spectroscopy. The outcomes of this work set the basis for the use of Ti3C2Tx in novel nano harvesting systems involving metal (e.g., Au) interfaces with large scope in nanoelectronics, wearable sensing, electric vehicles, and robotics.

title: Extracellular vesicles presenting “don’t eat me” signal limit the efferocytic capacity in lung fibrosis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Efferocytosis is essential for tissue homeostasis and resolution of inflammation, yet its direct contribution to resolve organ fibrosis remains poorly understood. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive age-driven lung disease, we found profound suppression of efferocytosis coupled with robust production and release of extracellular vesicles presenting functional receptor CD47, a canonical “don’t eat me” mediator. Restoration of efferocytosis contributes to the natural resolution of fibrosis, which is accelerated by CD47 deficiency or alterations in macrophage metabolic responses. In turn, pharmacologic disruption of efferocytic receptors or signaling results in lung fibrosis development and its persistence. While sustained reduction of efferocytic capacity align with fibrosis persistence in aged mice, AMPK activation promotes fibrosis resolution via reducing inflammaging and CD47 bioavailability, thus restoring clearance of apoptotic fibroblast. Importantly, AMPK activation also reprograms macrophages engaging apoptotic fibroblasts toward a fibrosis pro-resolving phenotype by suppressing TGF-β1 and promoting secretion of pro-regenerative hepatocyte growth factor (HGF). Together, these findings link metabolism and immune efferocytic fitness in lung fibrosis resolution and suggest that an AMPK senomorphic pathway has broad therapeutic relevance for fibrotic diseases.

title: Elastic tricriticality at the collapse of magnetic order in a valence fluctuating Eu-based compound
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Spin and charge fluctuations are key for understanding the properties of materials with strongly correlated electrons, but their coupling to the atomic crystal lattice is often assumed to be weak and perturbative. In this work, we demonstrate that at tricritical points (TCPs), that are associated with electronic correlations, a coupling to crystal elasticity is generically nonperturbative. It will modify the tricritical universality class leading to elastic tricriticality , characterized by a compressibility that diverges in a universal manner with the correlation length. To test this scenario experimentally, we use single crystals of EuPd 2 (Si 1− x Ge x ) 2 where, depending on x and pressure, magnetic order collapses due to strong valence fluctuations. First, we confirm the presence of a TCP for x ≈ 0.1 by using complementary probes, in particular, measurements of relative length changes under control of temperature and He-gas pressure. Second, by studying the elastic response, we uncover clear signatures of elastic tricriticality, notably a drastically enhanced compressibility.

title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals organizational properties of the mouse spinal cord and alterations in neuropathic pain
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The spinal cord integrates diverse somatosensory inputs and executes motor outputs through anatomically and functionally distinct circuits. Here, we employed spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomic profiling of the adult mouse spinal cord to gain insights into the organizational logic of the spinal cord. Our results reveal distinct spatial and laminar distributions of neuronal subtypes, including axial level and sex-specific differences. Many neuronal subtypes exhibit lamina-specific somatic proximities, suggesting potential regionally specific connectivity. Additionally, neuronal subtypes within the dorsal horn exhibit a wide range of predicted cell-cell communication motifs, as assessed by the spatial distribution of neuropeptide- and other ligand-receptor pairs. Finally, we identified several neuronal subtypes with altered transcriptomic states and predicted cell–cell communications in a model of neuropathic pain. This spatially resolved cellular and molecular map of the spinal cord will facilitate the decoding of circuit mechanisms underlying somatosensory and motor functions in health and disease.

title: Disruption of the NTCP–EGFR receptor complex as a strategy for selective inhibition of hepatitis B and D virus entry
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) enter hepatocytes through a coordinated process mediated by a receptor complex consisting of sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP), and host entry cofactors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Here, we established an in vitro assay to evaluate the NTCP–EGFR interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupted this molecular interaction. Oxy229 selectively inhibited HBV and HDV infection to HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes. Mechanistic analysis revealed that Oxy229 impaired the relocalization of HBV–NTCP complex from the plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles. Notably, Oxy229 did not compromise the physiological functions of NTCP and EGFR, i.e., bile acid transporter and activation of downstream EGFR signaling pathways including Ras–MAPK and PI3K–Akt pathways, indicating selective inhibition of viral entry. Compound derivative analysis identified Oxy283, which acquired dual inhibitory activity against both NTCP–EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization, resulting in enhanced anti-HBV potency. These findings establish the functional significance of NTCP–receptor complex formation in the HBV/HDV entry and highlight this machinery as a potential target for antiviral intervention.

title: Homeostatic control of stem cell activity during intestinal regeneration
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Stem cells proliferate rapidly to maintain tissue turnover during regeneration, yet the mechanisms preventing hyperproliferation remain unclear. Here, we identified nuclear factor Y (NF-Y) as a transcriptional repressor that maintains intestinal stem cell (ISC) quiescence. NF-Y restricts ISC proliferation by occupying the promoters of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling components, including Egfr , Mkp3 , Raf , Ras , and pnt , through regulation dependent on the histone acetyltransferase Nejire (Nej)/p300. Loss of NF-Y enhances ISC proliferation and accelerates tumor progression. NF-Y acts with Nej to restrict Egfr expression and suppress hyperproliferation. Together, these results demonstrate that NF-Y, acting with Nej, serves as a key transcriptional repressive brake that restrains growth-signaling to control stem cell activity under homeostatic and disease conditions.

title: VAMP725 and VAMP726 interact with cellulose synthase to support secondary cell wall formation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The formation of plant cell walls underpins morphogenesis, growth, and development of all plants. Cellulose is an essential and load-bearing cell wall polymer that is synthesized by Cellulose Synthase (CESA) protein complexes at the plasma membrane. In this study, we reveal that SNARE proteins Vesicle Associated Membrane Protein 726 (VAMP726) and VAMP725 associate with multiple CESA proteins. Consistent with these results, the VAMP726 is codelivered with the CESA proteins to the plasma membrane, and the proteins colocalize at intracellular compartments. We further show that the VAMPs, especially VAMP726, are important for CESA trafficking and sustenance of cellulose synthesis both in growing tissues and in secondary wall producing maturing tissues. Taken together, our study outlines an important intracellular process whereby VAMP proteins facilitate trafficking of CESA complexes during cellulose synthesis.

title: Host infection selects for sRNA variants that drive bacterial social cheating
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Single-nucleotide mutations in regulatory small RNAs (sRNAs) represent a largely unexplored route to social cheating during bacterial infection. Here we show that arcZ , encoding a conserved Hfq-dependent sRNA in the plant pathogen Dickeya solani , undergoes recurrent single-nucleotide mutations during potato tuber infection. Five distinct arcZ alleles define a graded series of ArcZ functional impairment in which antifungal and protease activities are progressively reduced while virulence is compromised only in a subset of alleles. All five variants gain a fitness advantage exclusively during coinfection with wild-type arcZ 1 cells. This advantage is strongest when variants are rare and declines as cheater frequency increases, ultimately correlating with reduced total bacterial productivity, the canonical signature of social cheating and a tragedy of the commons. No fitness benefit is detected in vitro . Transcriptomic profiling of five arcZ variants identifies a conserved core of 186 downregulated genes enriched in secreted and diffusible functions. Systematic genetic dissection, supported by quantitative proteomics, establishes BudAB-dependent limitation of tissue acidification as the dominant cooperative public good exploited during infection. Wild-type arcZ 1 cells divert pyruvate flux toward acetoin via the BudAB pathway, maintaining a less acidic tissue environment that sustains disease progression; arcZ variants, which show reduced expression of this pathway, benefit from the less acidic environment maintained by wild-type cells without contributing to it. These results establish pleiotropic regulatory sRNAs as a previously unrecognized class of mutational targets for the emergence of social cheaters during host infection.

title: RNA and proteins joined up at the origins of life: Persistence is the point
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: What drove nucleic acids (NA) into functional associations with proteins (PR) at the origins of life? We reason from polymer physics and the Central Dogma that the fitness value of cooperating through a division of labor—NA for replication fidelity and PR for functional fitness—is much higher than for either polymer alone. Our model shows a Pareto Front, where NA and PR can bootstrap each other to achieve autocatalytic cooperativity toward biology.

title: A trefoil knot mimic and multiple pore states define the mechanism of a split-shell Tc toxin
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Toxin complex (Tc) toxins are among the largest virulence factors secreted by pathogenic bacteria, operating via a sophisticated injection mechanism that translocates cytotoxic effectors into host cells. While most structural and mechanistic studies have focused on fused-shell Tc toxins such as PTC3 from Photorhabdus luminescens , the structurally distinct split-shell toxins remain poorly understood. Here we report cryoelectron microscopy structures of the split-shell Yersinia entomophaga Tc holotoxin (YenTc) in multiple conformational states at resolutions of 2.6 to 3.7 Å. We show that the chitinase subunit YenChi2 is essential for shell expression and stabilizes the N terminus of the shell subunit YenA1 in the prepore state. Our structures also reveal the first trefoil knot mimic in Tc toxins, which serves the dual function of stabilizing the linker domain and holding the two halves of the split shell together. We further describe three distinct pore states: the conventional pore state, an inverted pore state in which the shell rotates 180° around a hinge in YenA2, and a lollipop pore state induced at alkaline pH in which the YenA1-YenChi2 subcomplex fully dissociates from the channel. Strikingly, all three pore states also manifest in the TcA pentamer of P. luminescens PTC3, indicating that they represent a general but previously undescribed feature of Tc toxin pore formation. Taken together, our results establish a mechanistic framework for split-shell Tc toxins and expose a dynamic, multilevel intoxication pathway that may apply broadly to Tc toxins.

title: The highly heat-inducible HspA6 and the thermolabile DnaJB5 are potent regulators of heat shock transcription factor 1 activity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: In response to proteotoxic stress the central regulator of the heat shock response (HSR) in mammalian cells, Hsf1, trimerizes, binds DNA, and drives transcription of heat shock genes. We previously showed that Hsc70 (HspA8) assisted by its J-domain protein (JDP) cochaperone DnaJB1 dissociates Hsf1 from DNA by monomerizing the trimeric Hsf1 and thereby attenuates the HSR. Whether this feedback mechanism is specific to the HspA8–DnaJB1 pair or instead reflects a broader, isoform- and JDP-selective Hsp70 network controlling Hsf1 remained unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that of all cytonuclear Hsp70s the highly heat-inducible HspA6 is most efficient in monomerizing Hsf1 in the presence of DnaJB1 and of all cytonuclear class A and class B JDPs, only DnaJB1, DnaJB4, and DnaJB5 assist in Hsf1 monomerization. Whereas cooperation of HspA6 and HspA8 with DnaJB1 and DnaJB4 absolutely depends on Hsp70s’ C-terminal glutamate-glutamate-valine-glutamate (EEVD)-motif, cooperation with DnaJB5 does not. Consistent with these data, overproduction of EEVD-deleted HspA8 and HspA6 down-regulate the HSR in HeLa cells. DnaJB5 knockdown reduces HspA8–Hsf1 interaction under nonstress conditions revealing DnaJB5 as major targeting factor for HspA8 binding to Hsf1. On temperature upshift DnaJB5 partially unfolds and partitions into insoluble cell fractions, suggesting it is a thermosensor that allows for increased Hsf1 activity by reducing HspA8’s ability to monomerize Hsf1. During ongoing heat shock, upregulated HspA6 and HspA8 then limit the HSR presumably targeted by heat-induced DnaJB1. HspA6 knock-down and overproduction in HeLa cells suggest that HspA6 functions in preventing an overshoot of the HSR.

title: IFITM1-mediated restriction of henipavirus entry is associated with ephrinB2 reorganization and confinement in membrane nanodomains
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Nipah (NiV) and Hendra (HeV) viruses are prototype henipaviruses (HNV) within the family of Paramyxoviridae . They are highly pathogenic zoonotic paramyxoviruses that cause fatal encephalitis in humans, with case fatality rates of 40 to 70%. These viruses use the receptor-binding protein (G) to engage host receptors ephrinB2 and/or ephrinB3, while the fusion protein (F) drives membrane fusion leading to virus entry and cell–cell fusion. Interferon-inducible transmembrane (IFITM) proteins restrict the infection of many unrelated viruses at virus entry. We show that the knockdown of IFITM1 enhances HNV entry and cell–cell fusion in both human epithelial and endothelial cells, while overexpression of IFITM1 inhibits both. Using single-molecule localization microscopy, we observed that IFITM1 forms nanoclusters on the plasma membrane that are enlarged upon interferon stimulation. IFITM1 clusters spatially co-occur with GM1-enriched, raft-like membrane domains. EphrinB2, a lipid raft resident, organizes into larger and denser clusters when associated with IFITM1, suggesting a preferential partitioning into membrane domains organized and/or influenced by IFITM1. Using single-particle tracking, we further show that lateral diffusion of ephrinB2 on the plasma membrane is confined in the presence of IFITM1. This confinement is not reversed by amphotericin B, nor is IFITM1-mediated NiV restriction. Our data show spatial reorganization and confinement of ephrinB2 within membrane domains that may be organized and/or influenced by IFITM1. These changes may contribute to HNV restriction, potentially by increasing the energy barrier for virus-cell membrane fusion and reducing productive virus-receptor encounters.

title: N-terminal integrity governs heptamer assembly and maturation in a mosquito innexin hemichannel
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Nonchordate gap junction channels are formed by innexins, yet the structures and subunit assembly mechanisms of insect innexins remain unknown. We determined cryoelectron microscopy structures of AGAP001487, an innexin from the malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae , reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs. The wild-type protein forms a rotationally symmetric heptameric hemichannel with an ordered N-terminal ring stabilized by intersubunit hydrogen bonds. Whereas deletion of a single N-terminal residue preserves channel activity, removal of two or more residues markedly impairs function. Consistent with these functional defects, the structure lacking two N-terminal residues exhibits disrupted rotational symmetry, extensive N-terminal disorder, pore collapse, and altered pore–lipid interactions. In addition, two-dimensional class averages revealed a minor population of hexameric particles, consistent with a potential assembly intermediate. Together, these structures support a stepwise assembly pathway in which intersubunit hydrogen bonding stabilizes N-terminal ring formation as a maturation step leading to a fully symmetric heptameric channel. Our findings identify N-terminal integrity as a critical determinant of oligomer maturation and channel function and provide mechanistic insight into how defined oligomeric assemblies are established in large-pore channel families.

title: A heavy molybdenum reservoir in Neoarchean seawater tracks extensive iron oxidation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The lead-up to the Great Oxidation Event (GOE; between 2.5 and 2.2 Ga) was arguably as consequential as the event itself, yet substantial uncertainties remain regarding the timing and magnitude of oxygen rise in early Earth’s oceans. Heavy molybdenum isotope compositions (δ 98 Mo) in Neoarchean marine sediments have traditionally been interpreted as evidence for adsorption of dissolved Mo onto iron oxyhydroxides [e.g., ferrihydrite; Fe(OH) 3 ] and manganese oxides (MnO 2 ) formed in oxygenated marine environments, implying at least regional surface oxygen accumulation immediately prior to the GOE. Here, we propose an alternate explanation in which these isotopic signatures arose in a largely anoxic ocean. Analyses of Neoarchean banded iron formations (BIFs) deposited at 2.57 to 2.51 Ga reveal a broad range of δ 98 Mo values, which are best explained by the combined effects of Mo adsorption onto primary ferrihydrite, followed by its diagenetic incorporation into Fe(II)-Mo(IV)-sulfides. After accounting for isotopic fractionation during adsorption, we estimate that Neoarchean seawater δ 98 Mo maintained a relatively stable composition between 1.5‰ and 1.6‰. A newly developed Mo isotope mass balance model further indicates that only a minor MnO 2 sink was required to generate these heavy δ 98 Mo values. Instead, the dominant control was likely removal of isotopically light Mo via adsorption to settling ferrihydrite particles in ferruginous seawater. Given the lack of oxygen indicators for cyanobacterial photosynthesis, we posit that anoxygenic photosynthetic bacteria (photoferrotrophs) were the primary drivers of ferrihydrite precipitation during BIF deposition. Together, these findings imply that the Neoarchean Mo isotope record reflects anaerobic biological oxidation of Fe(II) rather than pervasive surface seawater oxygenation preceding the GOE.

title: Boundary density predicts catalyst-layer utilization in membrane-electrode assemblies
abstract: Catalyst layers in membrane-electrode assemblies are often underutilized, limiting the efficiency of electrochemical devices. This work identifies the mechanism that localizes reaction near the boundaries between contacted and non-contacted regions of the catalyst layer. Based on this insight, boundary density is introduced as a geometric descriptor of the porous-transport-layer/catalyst-layer interface and a predictor of catalyst-layer utilization.

title: Dye-Sensitization Enables Visible-Light-Driven N–N Bond Cleavage in a Dinuclear Rhenium Dinitrogen Complex
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conversion of μ-N2 complexes into nitrogenous compounds is one of the most important and challenging chemical transformations in N2 fixation. Although photochemical N2 splitting has been demonstrated, existing approaches predominantly rely on high-energy ultraviolet light that generally affords low efficiency and poor selectivity. Herein, we establish a visible-light-driven molecular photosensitization strategy that enables efficient and selective N–N bond cleavage in a dinuclear rhenium dinitrogen complex. Blue light excitation of the organic photosensitizer 4DPAIPN (2,4,5,6-tetrakis(diphenylamino)isophthalonitrile) is shown to initiate N–N scission to afford the corresponding rhenium nitride in 96% yield. Kinetic analysis of nanosecond transient absorption data through the Balzani-Scandola model indicates energy transfer from the photosensitizer to an acceptor state that lies approximately 2.31 eV above the ground state of the μ-N2-bridged dirhenium complex. This photosensitization strategy decouples light harvesting from N–N bond activation, eliminates the need for UV light, and shows broad applicability across different visible-light absorbing photosensitizers, including transition metal complexes and organic chromophores with long-lived, high-energy triplet excited-states. These findings establish dye-sensitization as a powerful strategy for visible-light-driven N–N bond cleavage for mechanistic study and the future realization of a photochemical pathway for nitrogen fixation.

title: Acute degradation of Pumilio proteins reveals a biphasic posttranscriptional regulatory hierarchy in embryonic stem cell fate decision
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Posttranscriptional regulation is critical for mammalian embryogenesis yet has been underexplored. We previously showed that RNA-binding Pumilio proteins (Pum1/2) are essential for early mouse embryogenesis and embryonic stem cell (ESC) functions. Here, using acute protein degradation systems combined with time-resolved RNA sequencing and enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation, we delineate a two-phase regulatory hierarchy modulated by Pum1/2 in mouse ESCs. The first phase, occurring within 10 h of Pum1/2 depletion, is predominantly stabilization of over 100 Pum1/2-target mRNAs, while the second phase, occurring in subsequent 66 h, propagates to over 1,000 mRNAs mostly through indirect regulatory effects. Functionally, Pum1/2 depletion delays transition from naïve to formative pluripotency and alters expression trajectories of neuroectoderm and germline genes during early differentiation. Mechanistically, Pum1/2 directly repress mRNAs encoding Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 subunits, including Suz12 , thereby potentially constraining H3K27me3 deposition at neuroectodermal gene loci. These findings establish Pum1/2 as biphasic posttranscriptional regulators of pluripotency and lineage balance.

title: Programming golden triple helices
abstract: Chiral helical superstructures provide a platform to control photon polarization and electron spin, yet they are challenging to construct using inorganic materials. Now, homochiral triple helices that exhibit pronounced circularly polarized luminescence have been assembled from gold by tailoring the steric and stereochemical properties of supporting chiral cyclic ligands.

title: Stereodynamical control of a four-atom reaction: HD + OH → D + H 2 O
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: To date, studies of differential steric effect in reactive collisions have been limited to atom + molecule systems. How stereodynamics is affected when the other reactant is also a molecule remains an open question. Here, we present a combined high-resolution crossed-beam scattering and full-dimensional quantum dynamical study of the HD ( v = 1, j = 2) + OH → D + H 2 O reaction, in which the HD molecular axis was initially prepared either parallel or perpendicular to the relative velocity using the stimulated Raman pumping scheme. The OH reactant was unpolarized and in its ground vibrational state, with a rotational temperature of ~85 K in the experiment, and was restricted to the ground rovibrational state in the theory. Pronounced stereodynamic effects are observed in both the backward scattering intensity and the product angular distributions. Detailed analysis of scattering wavefunctions reveals that the initial m = ±2 states access a noncoplanar dynamical transition state, distinct from that accessed by m = 0 ( m denotes the projection of j along the direction of relative velocity). The nonzero dihedral angle, a geometric degree of freedom absent in triatomic reactions, leads to reduced reactivity and enhances sideward scattering for the perpendicular configuration, while leaving the product rovibrational state distributions essentially unchanged. In addition, the alignment of the HD rotational angular momentum is preserved in the rotational direction of the product H 2 O.

title: Design and Evolution of an Orthogonal HaloTag for Multiplexed Labeling in Cells
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The self-labeling protein HaloTag is used to install a wide variety of functional small molecules in cells and living organisms with exquisite specificity with respect to cell type and subcellular localization. HaloTag is a core part of many biotechnology-based tools for sensing, tracking, and manipulating biological systems with a high degree of spatial and temporal control. Due to the limitations of fluorescent proteins and other self-labeling proteins, most of these tools have historically been restricted to a single channel. In this work, we used structure-guided rational design and directed evolution to produce an orthogonal HaloTag protein called OrthoTag which reacts selectively with a modified chloroalkane substrate. OrthoTag retains many of HaloTag’s superior properties, and reaction rate measurements with purified proteins show OrthoTag and its substrate have 109-fold mutual orthogonality to HaloTag with respect to substrate concentration. We demonstrate the application of OrthoTag for multiplexed labeling experiments in mammalian cells with minimal optimization. Going forward, OrthoTag should be straightforward to incorporate into HaloTag-based systems to allow simultaneous measurement or manipulation of two biological targets or processes. The availability of multiple high-performance self-labeling proteins will enable the continued development of new multiplexed biotechnology methods.

title: Cell Configuration Dependent Perturbations for in Situ/Operando Raman Spectroscopy of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: In situ/operando characterization is crucial for revealing dynamic processes in electrochemical energy devices, offering key insights for mechanism elucidation and performance optimization. However, the configurations used for the observations may...

title: Multiscale insights into zinc metal anodes for aqueous zinc ion batteries
abstract: This review examines how the intrinsic properties of zinc metal influence its stability in aqueous electrolytes, highlighting multiscale correlations among morphology, microstructure, electronic structure, and electrochemical behavior. It outlines emerging strategies and future directions for enhancing zinc reversibility and utilization toward practical aqueous zinc ion batteries.

title: Ultraviolet exciton-polaritons in silver phenylthiolate
abstract: Hybridization of light and excitons can change how materials absorb and emit light, but achieving this in the ultraviolet remains challenging. We show that a layered silver phenylthiolate forms hybrid light-matter states in simple mirror structures. This material expands the options for controlling ultraviolet light and provides a foundation for exploring future light sources and light-driven chemistry.

title: Unlocking flexibility in buildings through batteries: a case study of the Netherlands
abstract: Residential buildings account for a significant share of energy consumption and emissions, and heating electrification and rooftop photovoltaic (PV) generation create new challenges for distribution grids: import peaks from heat pumps and export peaks from PV surpluses. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) can reduce peak demand and increase self-consumption. We report a multi-objective optimization of BESS sizing and dispatch in a 58-apartment positive-energy building in Utrecht, using a full year of measured smart-meter data. A linear-programming model with a Wöhler-based degradation cost trades off peak shaving and self-consumption across a capacity sweep, under two scenarios: a hypothetical configuration in which all 58 apartments and the facilities share one ± 110.4 kW connection instead of their individual connections (Scenario 1), and the current configuration, in which the BESSs serve only the facilities (Scenario 2). Consolidation rather than operational savings dominates the economics: once the BESS dispatch eliminates the 122 hours of PV export violation (the summed apartment exports exceeding the shared connection, purely from aggregation), the avoided cost of the 58 individual connections becomes accessible. The installed 70 kWh BESS crosses this threshold, with a payback of 0.55 years; the economic optimum lies near 280 kWh. Scenario 1 is notional: its economics depend on contractual and regulatory consolidation of the 58 connections, which is not addressed in this study. In Scenario 2, where peak-shaving has no value, the BESS adds modest self-consumption gains. The results show the value of measured multi-apartment data and of institutional drivers alongside technological ones in residential storage economics.

title: Porphyrin-Driven Redox Tuning in Structurally Defined De Novo Heme Proteins
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Designing redox proteins with predictable and tunable electron transfer properties is a major goal in de novo bioenergetics. Here we show that replacing heme B with a series of structurally conservative non-natural metalloporphyrins enables broad modulation of redox potentials over 400 mV in the de novo designed monoheme m4D2 and diheme 4D2 T19D. The non-natural porphyrins bind with high affinity and do not compromise either the heme binding site or global protein structure, as evidenced by X-ray crystallography and NMR spectroscopy. We also report the native-like NMR structure of m4D2 loaded with the non-natural and symmetric iron 2,4-dimethyldeuteroporphyrin IX, confirming our modular approach to tetrahelical redox protein design. This work establishes a versatile platform for constructing tunable electron carriers for engineered bioenergetic pathways and bioelectronic applications.

title: Unlocking Intrinsic Chirality in Luminescent Copper Clusters via Intramolecular Spatial Confinement
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Most luminescent clusters that exhibit pronounced chiral signals typically rely on predesigned chiral ligands; however, stimulating the intrinsic chirality of clusters in the absence of exogenous asymmetric ligands remains a significant challenge. In this study, based on a series of structure-correlated Cu2 clusters, we demonstrate that intramolecular spatial confinement effectively induces distortions in flexible ligands, thereby imparting asymmetry to the cluster framework. This molecular asymmetry further determines the orientation of cluster entities during supramolecular assembly, thus enabling the modulation of chirality across this cluster series between inactive (“off”) and active (“on”) states. In addition, these structure-correlated Cu2 clusters display bright and tunable luminescence, allowing for the fabrication of uniform thin films that function as practical scintillation materials for high-resolution X-ray imaging. Collectively, this work provides a novel perspective for regulating the chiroptical properties of metal clusters through the activation of intramolecular spatial confinement and offers valuable insights into the fabrication of cluster-based nanomaterials with tailored photophysical performances.

title: Photoresponsive Mechanically Interlocked [ a n]Daisy Chain Network
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Muscle integrates molecular-machine motion with hierarchical structural organization, enabling it to sustain large deformations under physiological loads. Mechanically interlocked molecules offer a versatile platform to mimic such molecular-level motion, but efficiently translating it into macroscopic material performance, akin to muscle, remains challenging. Herein, we report a mechanically interlocked network (MIN) with [an]daisy chain backbone which can efficiently scale up the photoresponsive behavior of mechanical bonds, exhibiting intelligently tunable mechanical properties. In specific, photoresponsive unit of arylazopyrazole (AAP) is embedded onto the axis of each mechanical bond in the [an]daisy chain backbone. Ultraviolet light triggers the trans-to-cis (E/Z) isomerization of the AAP moieties, and when amplified through the [an]daisy chain backbone, it brings about significant changes in the material’s properties. On one hand, the E/Z isomerization significantly shortens the dimension of the [an]daisy chain framework, resulting in a notable increase in the material modulus (from 1.6 to 4.0 MPa). On the other hand, the cis configuration of AAP formed after the isomerization restricts the mobility of the mechanical bonds, resulting in a shorter elongation at break (from 343% to 272%). Our work presents an efficient method for amplifying mechanical bond responsiveness, providing a fresh perspective for the development of intelligent materials.

title: Dynamic Acidic Adsorbates Govern Fast Oxygen Incorporation in Ceria through Interfacial Electrostatics
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a key heterogeneous process underpinning energy conversion, catalytic, and sensing technologies. However, reported ORR kinetics at oxide surfaces often vary widely because surface chemistry evolves under operating conditions. Ceria-based fluorites have been proposed as protective layers to stabilize perovskite electrodes, but ORR kinetics are typically considered sluggish and reported values have large variability. Herein, we demonstrate that cathodic polarization triggers an unexpected activation in Gd-doped ceria (CGO) dense thin films at 500 °C, enabling oxygen incorporation rates that surpass state-of-the-art materials such as La0.5Sr0.5FeO3−δ and approach the performance of La0.6Sr0.4CoO3−δ. Operando near-ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (NAP-XPS), supported by ex situ surface-sensitive tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS), reveals that CGO surface activation coincides with a reversible, overpotential-dependent modulation of sulfate adsorbates. Integration of these measurements with nondilute space-charge modeling suggests that charged adsorbates dynamically tune the near-surface electrostatic potential and electron concentration, thereby controlling oxygen incorporation kinetics. These results support adsorbate-induced electrostatic effects as a key mechanism in ceria and show that ORR kinetics are dynamically set by surface chemistry under operation, rather than by intrinsic bulk defect chemistry alone.

title: Efficient Long-Wavelength Through-Space Charge-Transfer Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence in Conformationally Adaptive Emitters without Conformational Locking
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Through-space charge-transfer thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TSCT-TADF) emitters often employ conformationally constrained donor–acceptor architectures to control through-space electronic coupling, particularly for long-wavelength emission. Here, we report conformationally adaptive orange-to-red TSCT-TADF emitters based on an S-shaped donor−π–acceptor−π–donor framework composed of phenoxazine donors, xanthene linkers, and a dibenzo[a,j]phenazine acceptor. Structural and NMR analyses reveal substantial conformational mobility, while systematic conformational searches and excited-state calculations identify thermally accessible conformers with distinct donor–acceptor geometries and excited-state characteristics. Comparative studies with reference compounds and fragment-resolved transition-density analysis show that the xanthene linker primarily acts as a conformational regulator and that the low-energy CT states have predominant TSCT character with only minor linker involvement. Temperature-dependent early-time photoluminescence measurements reveal continuous spectral relaxation in fluid toluene that slows upon cooling and is absent in rigid Zeonex and mCBP hosts, providing strong evidence for structural relaxation following photoexcitation within a pre-existing conformational ensemble. The emitters exhibit orange-to-red TADF with reverse intersystem crossing rates on the order of 105–106 s–1. Organic light-emitting diodes employing these emitters show electroluminescence at 598–624 nm, external quantum efficiencies up to 14.9%, and limited efficiency roll-off over a broad luminance range. These results demonstrate that efficient long-wavelength TSCT-TADF can be realized without permanent conformational locking and establish a framework for understanding the interplay between ground-state conformational heterogeneity and excited-state structural relaxation.

title: Dynamic Metal Encapsulation in a Pt/TiO x system Regulated by Pt-Assisted TiO2 Amorphization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Strong metal–support interaction (SMSI) plays an important role in heterogeneous catalysis, but remains poorly understood, particularly on the origin of SMSI under an oxidative atmosphere. Hereby grand canonical structure exploration of over 4 million bulk PtTi alloys and Pt or PtTi-supported Ti oxide (TiOx) surface structure candidates, we resolve the Pt/TiOx system, a text-book example of SMSI, under both reductive and oxidative conditions: it experiences an encapsulation─deep encapsulation─decapsulation dynamic reconstruction under a sequence of H2 reduction─O2 oxidation─H2 plus O2 redox thermal treatment. The whole process was kinetically simulated by long-time (69 ns) molecular dynamics simulations, revealing in detail how a 3 nm Pt nanoparticle undergoes nonclassical SMSI under an oxidative and redox atmosphere. We find that Pt-assisted TiO2 amorphization is the key to the transition of various SMSI states at different conditions, which elevates Ti chemical potential via amorphization toward low-coordinated [TiO4]. Finally, explainable machine learning models were developed to predict nonclassical SMSI cases and clarify their rarity in nature.

title: Hydration-Dependent Working-Surface Chemistry in Photocatalytic Methane Coupling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Selective photocatalytic methane coupling requires directing methane-derived intermediates toward C–C bond formation while limiting their oxidation to CO2, yet how the reaction environment controls this competition through surface chemistry remains unclear. Water is ubiquitous in photocatalytic methane conversion, but its influence is commonly interpreted through specific chemical functions rather than through its broader effects on working-surface chemistry. Here, Au/ZnO is used as a compositionally defined, coupling-competent model catalyst to reveal how hydration regulates carbon transformation pathways by reshaping the working-surface chemistry. Systematic variation of water availability reveals three hydration-dependent catalytic regimes with markedly different product distributions. Moderate hydration increases the ethane production rate from 1590 to 8407 μmol g–1 h–1 and enables ethylene formation, whereas excessive hydration increases CO2 production and lowers C2 selectivity. In situ spectroscopies show that these catalytic regimes are accompanied by hydration-dependent changes in methane adsorption, methane-derived and coupling-related surface intermediates, and oxygen-deficient surface states within a reaction network involving both carbon- and oxygen-centered radical chemistry. Moderate hydration establishes surface conditions that favor C–C coupling and C2 hydrocarbon accumulation, whereas excessive hydration favors oxidized surface species and carbonate formation. These results identify hydration as a key determinant of the steady-state surface chemistry governing carbon partitioning between C–C coupling and oxidation during photocatalytic methane conversion.

title: Tailoring Solid-State Reaction Pathways for Bulk Fluorination of Mn-Rich Rock-Salt Cathodes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Manganese-based cation-disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes offer high capacities without relying on cobalt and nickel, but maintaining that capacity over extended cycling often requires bulk fluorination. The challenge is that incorporating fluorine into Mn-rich DRX host structures is hindered by unfavorable thermodynamics and the stability of LiF, often necessitating elevated synthesis temperatures that promote severe lithium and fluorine volatilization. This study overcomes that limitation by manipulating the solid-state reaction pathway using unconventional Li6MnO4 and MnF2 precursors in a challenging Mn-rich model system (Li1.2Mn0.6Ti0.2O2–xFx). This precursor engineering strategy reshapes the thermodynamic landscape. Computational modeling and in situ X-ray diffraction reveal that by using reactive starting materials, we suppress the crystallization of less reactive intermediates, enabling bulk fluorination at a lower temperature. The resulting DRX retains both a high fluorine content and the lithium excess required for three-dimensional percolation, delivering improved electrochemical performance relative to material synthesized from conventional precursors.

title: Multiphase Inorganic-Rich Interphases with Integrated Li-Ion Capture-Transport Ability for High-Rate Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lithium metal batteries promise high-energy-density storage but are limited by unstable solid–electrolyte interphases, which couple poor passivation, sluggish Li+ transport, dendritic deposition, and safety risks. Herein, we report a multiphase inorganic-rich solid–electrolyte interphase (m-SEI) containing P- and Al-derived species including Li3P, LiAl5O8, Li3PO4, and Li2Al, which is formed from the in situ reaction between a flame-retardant aluminum diethyl hypophosphite (ADP) interlayer and lithium metal. This multicomponent inorganic SEI enables an integrated capture-transport mechanism by combining high Li+ affinity, facilitated desolvation, and low-barrier Li+ migration pathways in individual inorganic phases and their heterophase interfaces, thereby facilitating rapid Li+ interfacial migration. Its chemical inertness and high Young’s modulus of 17.14 GPa further suppress electrolyte decomposition and Li dendrite growth. As a result, the Li-metal batteries with m-SEI deliver an extended lifespan of 1000 h at a high current density of 4 mA cm–2. Li||NCM811 full cells with a high cathode loading (20 mg cm–2) and ultrathin Li foil (50 μm) retain 80% capacity after 250 cycles, while Li||NCM811 pouch cells retain 90% capacity after 500 cycles. This work establishes the capture-transport mechanism as an effective design principle for regulating Li+ interfacial dynamics and offers a practical interphase-engineering strategy for constructing ion-conductive and chemically protective interphases in durable lithium metal batteries.

title: Synthesis and Crystal Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol C(OH)4
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Methanetetrol, C(OH)4 (orthocarbonic acid), is an elusive tethrahydroxymethane that, due to its rapid dissociation under ambient conditions, has never been synthesized in bulk. A recent study detected the formation of C(OH)4 molecules in the gas phase. Here, we show that C(OH)4 can be synthesized in a diamond anvil cell through the reaction between H2O and CO2 at 45(3) GPa and 50(3) GPa and temperatures <1200(200) K. The crystal structure of C(OH)4 was determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and corroborated by density-functional theory calculations together with Raman spectroscopy. It is composed of isolated [C(OH)4]-molecules linked by strong hydrogen bonds. Under high-pressure conditions, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids are denser than coexisting water ice phases, allowing them to segregate gravitationally and form stable reservoirs of oxidized carbon. These phases incorporate large amounts of carbon into their crystal structures as part of [CO4]4–- or [CO3]2–-building blocks. Because the amount of carbon that can be stored as CO2 in clathrates or filled-ices is significantly smaller, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids may provide a host mechanism for sequestering large carbon inventories in the icy mantles of water-rich exoplanets.

title: Programming Oxygen Reduction Selectivity via Peroxo Basicity: Acid-Controlled 2e–/4e– Reduction Switching at a Dicobalt Platform
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving switchable 2e–/4e– oxygen reduction selectivity within a single molecular catalyst remains an unmet challenge because the key metal–oxygen intermediate typically commits to one pathway. Herein, we demonstrate that this limitation can be overcome by elevating the basicity of the peroxo intermediate to a level where both proton-transfer (PT) and proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) manifolds become accessible, with the dominant pathway dictated solely by the external acid strength. A dicobalt μ-1,2-peroxo complex supported by an electron-rich macrocyclic poly-NHC ligand exhibits a computed pKa1 of ∼8.8, placing it in a unique thermodynamic window. Stoichiometric protonation bifurcates cleanly: strong acids (HClO4) trigger rapid diprotonation to release H2O2, whereas weak acids (Et3NHOTf) promote O–O bond cleavage to afford a μ-hydroxo complex. Under catalytic conditions, this dichotomy translates into complete selectivity switching─100% H2O2 with HClO4 versus 90% H2O with Et3NHOTf, accompanied by a switch in the rate-determining step from O2 binding to PCET (KIE = 1.60). Crucially, a structurally analogous but less basic peroxo complex predictably inverts the selectivity to H2O under identical conditions, providing a closed-loop validation of the basicity-selectivity relationship. These results establish intermediate basicity as a general, tunable design parameter for programming product selectivity in multielectron catalysis.

title: Programmable multistable structures via bioinspired, mechanically guided 4D printing
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Multistable structures, characterized by rapid shape morphing, instantaneous force amplification, and zero standby power, are pivotal for soft robotics and energy harvesting. However, achieving multistability while systematically controlling the accessible deformation modes remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a bioinspired, mechanically guided 4D printing approach to design and fabricate programmable multistable structures, including octastable and various bistable units, mimicking the growth-induced morphing of plant leaves and fruits. The stability landscapes of these units can be tuned by varying dimensionless geometric parameters and validated through buckling analysis. By integrating multiple octastable units, we demonstrate a compact, 10-cm-scale strip and a shape-morphing metasurface with configuration spaces of over one billion and four sextillion stable states. Furthermore, by modulating the dimensionless geometric parameters of multiunit structures, we identify a transition from bending to folding, enabling the creation of bistable hinges. As proof-of-concept demonstrations, we developed devices for directional droplet routing and mixing, reconfigurable electrical switching, conforming grasping of irregular objects, and programmable mechanical display. This work establishes a versatile framework for the design and fabrication of next-generation reconfigurable morphing systems and programmable flexible devices.

title: Structural Dynamics of a COF-Based Soft Actuator: Molecular Motion and Macroscopic Response
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Translating molecular-level dynamics of crystalline frameworks into macroscopic function remains a central challenge in the design of responsive materials. Here, we report that the intrinsic flexibility of COF-300 can be systematically characterized in the bulk powder and then harnessed in a processable composite film to achieve coupled optical and mechanical actuation. In powder form, COF-300 exhibits distinct responses to applied stimuli, including solvent vapors, acid-base environments, and temperature changes. Variable-temperature solid-state NMR reveals the thermally activated coalescence of the phenylene ring signals, and variable-temperature powder X-ray diffraction uncovers colossal anisotropic thermal expansion. Periodic TDA-DFT calculations trace the acid-induced chromism to both geometric distortion and protonation of framework. Embedding COF-300 into a poly(vinylidene fluoride) matrix produces a PVDF@COF film in which solvent vapors drive reversible bending–unbending motion synchronized with a visible color shift, and heating drives the same reversible motion. Exposure to HCl turns the film orange and locks both responses through imine protonation, while thermal deprotonation unlocks them, establishing a reversible chemical switch over framework dynamics. These findings show how molecular flexibility in a crystalline framework can translate into programmable macroscopic actuation, advancing the design of multifunctional solid-state actuators with integrated optical and mechanical output.

title: The public trusts scientists with AI — more than it does anyone else
abstract: Public confidence in scientists’ use of generative artificial intelligence remains high, but that trust comes with conditions.

title: SERS-Active Nanocomposite Contact Lenses for Label-Free Multiplexed Biosensing of Tear Analytes
