source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Continuous monitoring remains limited by the fact that most wearable biosensors are built around single-analyte recognition chemistries, even though many physiological states are defined by changes across multiple metabolites. Tear fluid is one of the most biochemically informative biofluids accessible non-invasively, but contact lens biosensors have largely relied on enzymatic or electrochemical techniques that are difficult to extend beyond one target marker at a time. Here, we report a label-free surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS)-active contact lens in which gold nanostars are grown in situ on commercial hydrogel contact lenses. The resulting gold nanostar-loaded contact lens (AuNS-CL) introduces a plasmonic sensing layer directly onto the wearable substrate, with a substrate-averaged SERS enhancement factor of ∼105, while preserving the lens’ physiochemical properties. Quantitative biosensing was demonstrated using a digital thresholding method to account for variable hotspot distributions. Metabolites such as lactate and urea were quantified through their diagnostic bands in several solutions, including artificial tears and a mixture of tear analytes. The AuNS-CLs showed a strong linear response in the physiological range and recovery errors below 10%. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a wearable contact lens for label-free SERS quantification of tear metabolites.

title: Porosity Tunable Silk Fibroin Microspheres Enhance Cartilage Repair in Rabbit Model
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Repairing articular cartilage defects is particularly challenging due to the tissue's hypovascularity and limited intrinsic healing capacity, which pose significant clinical challenges. Biomaterial-based scaffolds have shown promising outcomes in terms of repair capacity; however, finding a robust scaffold system remains challenging in cartilage tissue engineering. In this study, silk fibroin porous microspheres were fabricated using the co-axial electrospraying technique, followed by ethanol treatment to induce crosslinking and enhance microsphere stability. Interestingly, we observed that while changing the ethanol concentration from 100% to 75% to crosslink the silk microsphere resulted in the formation of tunable micropores, with pore sizes up to 87 μm in nonporous microspheres and ranging from 80–200 μm in porous microspheres. Then, we seeded human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hAdMSCs) onto microspheres to evaluate cell adhesion and proliferation over time. The microspheres exhibited enhanced cell adhesion during in vitro cytocompatibility assessments. Notably, porous microspheres displayed superior cell migration compared to nonporous microspheres, attributed to their interconnected pore architecture. Additionally, hAdMSCs-laden microspheres were further studied for their chondrogenic potential under induction conditions, demonstrating cartilage-specific marker expression. Moreover, macroscopic observations and histological staining images showed cartilage regeneration in a rabbit cartilage-defect model, in which porous microspheres outperformed nonporous counterparts due to their enhanced nutrient transfer and host-scaffold integration. Together, these results suggest that silk fibroin microspheres can mimic the extracellular matrix microenvironment, support cell growth, and promote matrix accumulation for effective cartilage repair.

title: Waterborne-Polyurethane as High-Performance Binder for Cathodes of Lithium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In lithium-ion batteries, the electrodes are strongly influenced by the polymer binder swelling in liquid electrolytes, which governs electrode integrity, adhesion, flexibility and Li+ transport. Herein, a series of polyacrylate-terminated waterborne polyurethanes (WPUAs) are designed by systematically varying the proportions of nonionic, anionic, and zwitterionic monomers to regulate swelling behavior in liquid electrolytes. The compositional modulation influences the polymer polarity, polymer entanglement, polymer mechanical property and their swelling in electrolytes, and finally the final electrochemical performance of WPUAs. The optimized WPUA exhibits a balanced swelling ratio, strong adhesion, and significantly enhanced Li+ diffusion. Density functional theory calculation reveals that the molecular configuration is rational and conducive to the Li+ transport, which are supported by its superior Li+ conductivity and diffusion coefficient of lithium ions much higher than those of the polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder. The calculated diffusion coefficient of lithium ions in WPUA is 2.43 × 10–12 cm2 s–1, which is twice times higher than that in PVDF. Employing the synthesized WPUA binder, the assembled LiFePO4@Li half cells show improved electrochemical performance of 110.8 mAh g–1 at 3C for over 800 cycles with 80.4% capacity retention and the high-loading LiFePO4@artificial graphite full cells also show improved performance of 135.0 mAh g–1 after 340 cycles with 87.1% capacity retention, both of which exhibit better electrochemical performance than PVDF. This work highlights controlled binder swelling as a key design parameter for balancing electrolyte accessibility, Li+ transport, and electrode integrity, offering useful guidance for the development of high-performance waterborne binders for lithium-ion batteries.

title: Poly-γ-Glutamic Acid-Modified Carbon Dots as an Enhanced Immune-Activating and Antigen-Delivering Nano-adjuvant for Improved Influenza Vaccine Efficacy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Vaccine adjuvants are essential components that enhance immune responses to antigens with limited intrinsic immunogenicity and shape the magnitude and quality of adaptive immunity. Although conventional adjuvants effectively stimulate innate immunity, their use is often limited by safety concerns or inefficient antigen delivery. Consequently, biologically derived and biodegradable biomaterials have gained attention as potent vaccine adjuvants. Among them, poly-γ-glutamic acid (γ-PGA) is a naturally derived biopolymer with intrinsic immunostimulatory activity that activates innate immune signaling and promotes cellular immune responses. However, γ-PGA alone shows limited antigen delivery efficiency, which can restrict formulation reproducibility and immune potency. Here, we report γ-PGA-modified carbon dots (PGA-CDs) as a rationally designed nano-adjuvant integrating γ-PGA-mediated immune activation with efficient antigen delivery. Compared with γ-PGA, PGA-CDs exhibited faster and more sustained cellular association, thereby inducing stronger dendritic cell maturation and proinflammatory cytokine production. They readily formed stable nanocomplexes with protein antigens, enhancing cellular uptake and antigen cross-presentation. In vivo, PGA-CDs formulated with ovalbumin elicited strong antigen-specific humoral and cellular immune responses. When combined with hemagglutinin (HA) from pandemic influenza A/California/04/2009 (pH1N1), PGA-CDs induced HA-specific humoral responses comparable to alum, while eliciting significantly stronger antibody and T cell responses than γ-PGA alone, resulting in complete protection against lethal viral challenge. Notably, HA/PGA-CDs also elicited more robust homosubtypic cross-reactive immunity than alum against influenza A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1), conferring complete protection. Furthermore, PGA-CDs were well tolerated in vivo, with no detectable hematological or histopathological abnormalities. Collectively, these findings establish PGA-CDs as a promising vaccine adjuvant platform that enhances antigen delivery, amplifies immune activation, and broadens protective efficacy.

title: Decoupling Metal Deposition from Contact Formation Enables Polarity Transformation in WSe2 Transistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polarity control in two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor field-effect transistors (FETs) is essential for their integration into complementary logic circuits. However, existing polarity-engineering approaches often fail to preserve high-quality contact interfaces because atomically thin 2D semiconductors are highly sensitive to fabrication processes. Here, we introduce an effective buffer-layer removal process that enables polarity transformation while preserving a high-quality contact interface. A thin semimetal layer (Bi or Sb) is deposited prior to high-work-function metal evaporation and subsequently removed by a wet chemical treatment that preserves a high-quality metal/semiconductor interface. Minimizing the contact angle of the rinsing solution suppresses wrinkle and bubble formations and reduces Fermi-level pinning. The same WSe2 transistors transform from semimetal-dominated n-type transport before treatment to high-work-function-metal-dominated p-type transport afterward. Monolayer devices exhibit a maximum two-terminal hole field-effect mobility of 313 cm2 V–1 s–1 after treatment, while also supporting a maximum electron mobility of 41 cm2 V–1 s–1 before treatment. These results demonstrate n-to-p polarity transformation in WSe2 transistors enabled by a removable semimetal layer, providing a potential doping-free route toward complementary 2D electronics.

title: Epoxy-Functionalized Polysilsesquioxane Coatings for Rear-Side Impact Protection of Thin Functional Ceramics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-performance protective coatings capable of preventing catastrophic impact fracture of thin brittle inorganic substrates are urgently demanded for next-generation 5G/6G consumer electronics; however rational design strategies that simultaneously retain pristine surface aesthetics and achieve prominent shock resistance are still lacking. Herein, a rigid epoxy-functionalized polysilsesquioxane hybrid resin is synthesized, followed by cross-linking with various amine curing agents through a high-efficiency synchronous thermal-moisture dual-curing route. The optimized EGSI coating crosslinked by isophorone diamine (IPDA) achieves a pencil scratch hardness of 9H and a nanoindentation modulus of 2.66 GPa. Viscoelastic characterization confirms a distinctive filler-free self-reinforcement effect originating from the siloxane skeleton; the glass transition becomes indistinct, and the optimized coating preserved ∼40% of its initial glassy storage modulus, corresponding to a remarkably high rubbery plateau modulus of ∼750 MPa up to 300 °C. Ball-drop impact tests support the effectiveness of the proposed rigid backing structural constraint mechanism. When coated on the rear face of 300 μm structural ceramic sheets, the EGSI layer elevates the maximum crack-free nominal drop energy to 63.9 mJ, representing a 233% enhancement compared with bare ceramics. Different from conventional front-side energy-absorbing coatings, this noninvasive rear-side reinforcement scheme avoids damaging the decorative exterior of ceramic components and enables low-cost upgrading of ordinary sintered ceramics to high shock-resistant grade. This study establishes a design approach for the tested systems and coating configuration optimization methodology for reinforcing brittle substrates, showing great application prospects in smartphone ceramic back covers, ultrathin glass panels, and other electronic protective components.

title: Polymer–Two-Dimensional Filler Composites for Hydrogen Barrier Materials: Transport Theory, Design Strategies, and Experimental Advances
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen energy is widely regarded as one of the most promising pathways toward sustainable, low-carbon energy systems. However, hydrogen permeation remains a critical challenges for pipelines, storage vessels, and other hydrogen-related equipment. These issues not only reduce structural reliability but also raise significant safety concerns during long-term service. To mitigate hydrogen permeation, various hydrogen barrier materials, including metals, ceramics, and polymers, have been extensively investigated. Recently, incorporating two-dimensional (2D) materials used as fillers into polymer matrices has emerged as an effective strategy for enhancing hydrogen barrier performance by increasing diffusion tortuosity and suppressing hydrogen transport pathways. As a result, layered silicates (e.g., montmorillonite, MMT), graphene-based materials, MXenes (e.g., Ti3C2Tx), molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN), and layered double hydroxides (LDHs) have attracted increasing attention for advanced hydrogen barrier applications. Despite rapid progress in polymer/2D filler composite barrier materials, which can be implemented as surface coatings, bulk liners, or free-standing films, enhancement of barrier properties through the optimization of nanosheet alignment, interfacial stability, oxidation resistance as well as scalable fabrication and long-term durability remain major challenges. Moreover, a mechanistic understanding of hydrogen transport and the structure–property relationships that determine barrier performance remains also insufficient, limiting their practical employment in hydrogen-energy systems. Therefore, this review systematically summarizes recent advances in polymer/2D filler composite hydrogen barrier materials, with a particular focus on theoretical aspects related to gas permeability in 2D nanocomposites, hydrogen transport mechanisms, structure–property relationships, fabrication strategies, durability, and engineering applications. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives for next-generation multifunctional hydrogen barrier materials are discussed, aiming to provide guidance for the rational design and industrial implementation of advanced hydrogen barrier systems.

title: Crystalline NiO:N Templating of Uniformly Anchored Self-Assembled Monolayers for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The buried hole-selective contact in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is expected to transport holes through its bulk while also templating a defect-free self-assembled monolayer (SAM). A crystalline, vacuum-deposited nitrogen-doped NiO (NiO:N) film deterministically templates a uniformly anchored SAM, while the reactive-atmosphere N2/O2 ratio used during pulsed laser deposition (PLD) simultaneously programs bulk hole density and interfacial anchoring chemistry. Nitrogen incorporation is proposed to act as a shallow acceptor that generates Ni3+ states and raises p-type conductivity, whereas the dense, pinhole-free template enforces uniform SAM coverage, fully suppressing the underlying substrate signal and minimizing surface hydroxyl groups relative to discontinuous nanoparticle films. Consequently, NiO:N/SAM-based PSCs achieve a 6.2% relative increase in power conversion efficiency (PCE) over pristine NiO nanoparticles, reaching one of the highest reported performances for vacuum-deposited NiO-based PSCs, with improved thermal and operational stability. These results establish reactive-atmosphere NiO:N as a general, scalable platform for hole-selective contacts in inverted perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Follicle-Targeted Deep Eutectic Solvent-Lipid Hybrid Nanocarriers for Phloretin against Androgenetic Alopecia
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) represents the most prevalent form of hair loss globally. Currently, minoxidil (MNX) is the only FDA-approved topical medication for AGA, but its use is limited by suboptimal efficacy and noticeable side effects. These limitations underscore an urgent demand for safer and more effective treatment options. Phloretin (PHL), a natural flavonoid, offers anti-inflammatory and antioxidant benefits that make it a promising candidate for AGA therapy. However, its practical application is restricted by poor water solubility and low skin permeability. To overcome these challenges, this study used a betaine-mandelic acid deep eutectic solvent (BMDES) to considerably improve the solubility and skin penetration of PHL. Due to the high viscosity of pure BMDES, which can compromise patient comfort, we developed a hybrid nanoparticle system, called BMDES-Lip@PHL, by combining 50% BMDES with liposomes. This strategy effectively harnesses the high drug-loading capacity of BMDES and the follicular targeting and retention properties of liposomes, thereby overcoming the limitations associated with each individual system. In vitro experiments BMDES-Lip@PHL significantly boosted the proliferation and migration of human dermal papilla cells and reduced oxidative stress. It also encouraged follicular angiogenesis and lowered the levels of pro-inflammatory factors. In AGA models, BMDES-Lip@PHL significantly stimulated hair regrowth and prevented collagen degradation induced by oxidative stress and inflammation. Furthermore, the system efficiently eliminated reactive oxygen species, suppressed the inflammatory cytokine TNF-α, reduced lipopolysaccharide-induced nitric oxide production, down-regulated interleukin-6, and promoted angiogenesis, all contributing to a healthier follicular microenvironment. Mechanistic analysis revealed that BMDES-Lip@PHL is associated with Wnt/β-catenin and mTOR signaling, alongside marked Sox9 and phosphorylated S6 up-regulation. Overall, BMDES-Lip@PHL showed outstanding safety and successfully delivered multiple functions including solubilization, penetration enhancement, retention, and targeting, indicating its strong potential as a treatment for AGA.

title: Electrostatically Integrated Cationic Antimicrobials Modulate Hydrogel Stability, Release, and Antibacterial Activity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrogel platforms for antimicrobial medical devices requiring sustained function must maintain bactericidal activity without compromising mechanical stability or cytocompatibility. Conventional systems often rely on passive antimicrobial loading, which can lead to burst release, rapid payload depletion, and dose-dependent toxicity. Here, we developed an ionic-covalent hydrogel platform in which cationic antimicrobial agents (CAAs) were post-loaded into a sulfonate-rich anionic network designed to provide electrostatic retention. A citrate-cross-linked chitosan–polyacrylamide network was coupled with poly(3-sulfopropyl acrylate) (polySPA) and subsequently loaded with benzalkonium chloride (BAK) or poly(hexamethylene biguanide) (PHMB). CAA loading reduced swelling and dry-mass loss while converting the anionic phase into a regulated antimicrobial reservoir. Compared with physically loaded controls, BAK- and PHMB-containing polySPA hydrogels sustained antimicrobial release over 28 days, retained direct antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli after 28 days of release aging, reduced viable bacteria in established biofilms by up to 99%, and showed lower hemolysis after 2 h and higher L929 cell viability after 24 h than physically loaded controls. BAK also reinforced the hydrogel network, with CPMSB-3 reaching nearly 13 MPa dry tensile strength and retaining approximately 2.5 MPa wet tensile strength. In a catheter demonstration, the optimized BAK-containing hydrogel improved lubrication and retained antibacterial activity and restricted Proteus mirabilis catheter-surface migration. A subsequent 7-day pilot rat catheter challenge provided exploratory macroscopic observations but was not used as definitive evidence of in vivo anti-infective efficacy. These findings support electrostatic CAA integration as a structure–property–function strategy for antimicrobial hydrogel interfaces with sustained function.

title: Electrospun Perforated Carbon Spheres with an Ultramicropore-Rich Architecture for Sodium-Ion Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hard carbon (HC) is a promising anode material for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) because its disordered structure and relatively large interlayer spacing facilitate reversible Na+ storage. Polyacrylonitrile (PAN) is an attractive carbon precursor with high carbon yield and in situ nitrogen doping. However, conventional PAN-derived HC often suffers from sluggish ion transport and limited reversible capacity. Herein, electrospun perforated carbon spheres (PCS) with an ultramicropore-rich architecture were fabricated via coaxial electrospinning, sacrificial templating, and high-temperature carbonization. The optimized PCS exhibits a CO2-derived apparent specific surface area of 362.5 m2 g–1 and deliver a reversible capacity of 312.9 mAh g–1 at 20 mA g–1, including a plateau capacity of 180.2 mAh g–1. It also delivers a rate capability of 145.6 mAh g–1 at 2 A g–1 and retains 88.0% of its capacity after 400 cycles at 50 mA g–1. Ex situ XRD, in situ Raman spectroscopy and electrochemical analyses are consistent with an adsorption–intercalation/pore-filling sodium-storage mechanism. A full cell paired with a Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 (NFPP) cathode delivers an energy density of 209 Wh kg–1 based on the total mass of active materials. These results demonstrate that electrospun carbon spheres with tailored pore structures are promising anodes for advanced SIBs.

title: Stimuli-Responsive Copper Modified Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles as Smart Antimicrobial Delivery System for Antimicrobial Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The emergence of multidrug-resistant pathogens poses a significant challenge to conventional antimicrobial therapies and underscores the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies using highly efficacious and less toxic antimicrobial compounds, as well as more targeted antimicrobial delivery strategies to prevent uncontrolled release, which contributes to the rise of drug resistance. In this study, the design and synthesis of copper-modified mesoporous silica nanoparticles (Cu-MSNs) were described as a stimuli-responsive, smart antimicrobial delivery system incorporating carvacrol as a bioactive alternative to conventional antibiotics. The Cu-MSNs exhibit high surface area, tunable pore size, and efficient carvacrol loading. Copper ions embedded within the silica matrix provide intrinsic antimicrobial activity and may enhance the antimicrobial effect of carvacrol. Poly(2-(dimethylamino) ethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) brushes were anchored on Cu-MSNs via surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP). The PDMAEMA brushes provided stimuli-responsive behavior, enabling pH- and temperature-dependent modulation of carvacrol release. The successful synthesis of Cu-MSN-PDMAEMA has been confirmed by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), elemental analysis (EA), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Moreover, stimuli-responsive behavior was confirmed using dynamic light scattering (DLS) experiments, demonstrating the pH- and temperature-dependent response of the PDMAEMA brushes. Finally, the carvacrol release behavior was studied at different pH values by using a sensitive paper-based electrochemical sensor. The multifunctional nanoplatform exhibited antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria as well as antiviral activity against representative enveloped and non-enveloped viral models. This synergistic design combines the benefits of a natural antimicrobial agent, intrinsic metallic activity, and smart polymer regulation, offering an strategy to enhance efficacy while minimizing off-target effects. Release studies demonstrated pH-triggered carvacrol delivery, with enhanced release under acidic conditions, confirming the gating function of the PDMAEMA brushes, highlighting the potential of these particles as an antibiotic-free alternative for preventing microbial infections while mitigating the development of antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

title: Automated shape optimization of stellarator divertor targets via Chebyshev parameterization and differential evolution
abstract: Managing extreme heat fluxes in the form of strike lines on divertor target plates is a central challenge that hinders the progression of reactor-relevant stellarators. We present an automated, fast, non-gradient-based optimization framework for shaping open stellarator divertor targets, applied to the Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) island divertor as a test case. The target surface geometry is parameterized using a Chebyshev spectral basis whose low-order modes naturally encode the physics motivated deformations, namely: translation, tilting and higher-order bending, which have an influence on the incidence angle and flux tube connection-length distributions at the target surface. The heat flux distribution on a target surface is evaluated by EMC3-Lite, a fast three-dimensional Monte Carlo edge-plasma transport code that self-consistently solves an energy transport equation with a sheath boundary condition, thereby avoiding the fixed-velocity limitations of simpler field-line-diffusion proxies. A parallelized Differential Evolution algorithm explores the Chebyshev coefficient space, minimizing a composite objective that simultaneously reduces peak heat flux, promotes uniform heat spreading, and maximizes the fraction of scrape-off-layer power intercepted by the target. Truncating the Chebyshev polynomials to the first three toroidal modes in and holding the coordinates constant, reduces the entire shape of the target surface to a single function . This function governs how quickly the surface drains the flux tubes it intersects and the radial width of the footprint. The optimized surface yielded a improvement in intercepted power, reduction in peak heat flux and a increase in the power weighted effective area.

title: Nanosecond-LIBS-induced deuterium outgassing, diffusion, and surface modification in tungsten coatings
abstract: Tritium retention in plasma-facing components (PFCs) must be strictly controlled to ensure the safe operation of fusion devices. In ITER, compliance with the tritium inventory limit and assessment of fuel-removal strategies require in situ monitoring of fuel retention in PFCs. Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) is a diagnostic technique that can be implemented via remote handling to investigate fuel retention during maintenance shutdowns at ITER. In LIBS diagnostics, the selection of laser parameters plays a critical role in determining the ablation characteristics and thermal perturbation of the target. Used nanosecond (ns) laser pulses deliver energy on timescales that allow substantial thermal diffusion into the target, which could result in surface heating and melting. Under multi-pulse LIBS operation, these cumulative thermal effects can alter deuterium quantification, as deuterium may diffuse or outgas due to heating induced by earlier pulses. Such laser-induced perturbations can compromise accuracy of quantitative deuterium measurements if they are not properly accounted for in modelling. In this study, subsequent in situ ns-LIBS and in situ nuclear reaction analysis (NRA) measurements were performed in Magnum-PSI on compact and porous tungsten coatings using a defocused, millimetre-scale laser spot ( ). Deuterium retention and depth profiles were determined in and outside the LIBS crater. Under the investigated laser conditions, NRA measurements indicated a 66%–79% reduction in retained deuterium within the sampled region of the LIBS crater, whereas pure material removal by ablation would account for only 21%–42%, demonstrating additional laser-induced outgassing. Compact coatings further exhibited melting and intermixing with the underlying substrate. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for defocused ns-LIBS-induced perturbations in retention measurements. Further experimental and modelling studies are needed to assess the dependence of these effects on laser spot geometry and to determine whether picosecond (ps) LIBS, together with consideration of cumulative multi-pulse effects, could improve the reliability of fuel-retention diagnostics in future fusion devices.

title: Numerical investigation of helium leakage and transport from in-vessel cooling-circuit in fusion reactor using DSMC method
abstract: Early detection of micro-leaks is essential for fusion reactors because such leaks precede a large-break loss-of-coolant accident (LOCA), which can seriously threaten vacuum-vessel structural integrity and reactor safety. In high-vacuum vessels, micro-leak identification depends on the transport characteristics of the plume released from the leak, making plume simulation and feature analysis important for leak detection. However, micro-leak plumes evolve across transitional and free-molecular regimes, where conventional continuum methods become limited. The direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method provides a promising approach for resolving cross-regime rarefied plume transport. In this work, DSMC is used to investigate helium leak plumes in the CFEDR vacuum vessel. Representative leak locations at the inboard blanket, outboard blanket and lower divertor, together with different leak intensities, are analyzed in terms of plume morphology, pressure distribution, affected volume and probe response. The results show that the plume evolves within 1–100 ms from a directional jet into a vessel-scale diffusive field, while pressure decays by approximately two to three orders of magnitude across the chamber. The pressure responses differ among the three representative leak locations, indicating that poloidally distributed probes can provide location-dependent signal features for the future development of leak-localization methods. At a leak intensity of , representative window probes reach the threshold within 4.35–8.50 ms, whereas lower-intensity leaks remain confined near the source and require more sensitive or cumulative detection. These findings provide preliminary guidance for multi-probe, multi-threshold monitoring strategies for early in-vessel LOCA warning in fusion reactors.

title: Tritium release and defect evolution in neutron-irradiated Li2Pb x Ti1−x O3 ceramic pebbles
abstract: Achieving tritium self-sufficiency remains a key challenge for future fusion reactors, creating a strong need for breeder materials with efficient tritium release. In this study, neutron-irradiated Li2PbxTi1−xO3 (x = 0, 0.05, and 0.1) ceramic pebbles were investigated by tritium thermal desorption spectroscopy (T-TDS) and electron spin resonance (ESR). Tritium release was examined at different heating rates and under isothermal conditions, and the corresponding kinetic parameters were determined. All samples exhibited a single tritium desorption peak that shifted to higher temperatures with increasing heating rate, confirming a thermally activated release process. Pb introduction broadened the desorption peak and lowered the apparent activation energy for tritium release. Under isothermal heating, the tritium diffusion activation energy (Ed) and pre-exponential factor (D0) increased simultaneously, following the compensation effect and suggesting multiple migration pathways. ESR isochronal and isothermal annealing showed that irradiation-defect annihilation occurs in two stages: a fast stage associated with electron migration and a slower stage governed by oxygen diffusion. The defect-annihilation range overlaps strongly with the main tritium-release range, indicating that tritium release is jointly controlled by diffusion and defect evolution. Increasing Pb content modifies irradiation-defect annealing behavior and influences tritium-release kinetics.

title: Cross-machine profile prediction and differentiable optimization by learning multi-tokamak databases
abstract: The development of high-performance plasma regimes is becoming increasingly important for tokamak operation and scenario design. Conventional operation-space exploration relies on computationally expensive iterative simulations and experimental trial and error. Although machine-learning methods have recently been applied to this problem, many optimization approaches treat the predictive model as a black box. They can therefore require a large number of model evaluations and must be retrained when the objective or operational constraints change. In this work, we develop a neural-network surrogate for multi-tokamak profile prediction using public databases. Device-dependent dimensional input and output variables are transformed into appropriate normalized quantities. These normalizations of input and output variables enable the prediction model to be applied to new devices such as ITER. The surrogate forms a fully differentiable mapping from engineering parameters to plasma profiles and derived performance metrics. Automatic differentiation provides the exact Jacobian of this mapping and enables gradient-based optimization without treating the model as a black box. Under identical objectives and bounds, the proposed method requires substantially fewer model evaluations than other machine-learning approaches. The proposed framework offers an efficient route from multi-machine data to interpretable plasma optimization and reactor scenario design.

title: Investigation of the inverse plasma sheath via BIT1 PIC modelling
abstract: In a classical plasma sheath, the potential decreases from the upstream towards the wall. The absolute value of the potential drop depends on a number of parameters, such as the electron temperature and the flux of electrons emitted from the surface. The question then is whether the wall potential can ever exceed the plasma potential—whether there is a realistic access to the so-called inverse sheath in tokamaks. We start our investigation from the work of Campanell and Umansky, reproduce their regime, and determine whether it is applicable to fusion-relevant conditions. Afterwards, we explore the theoretical conditions for accessing the inverse sheath.

title: Hydrogen borrowing with heterogeneous catalysis
abstract: Hydrogen borrowing (HB) enables sustainable C–N, C–C, and C–S bond formation using alcohols as alkylating agents. Heterogeneous HB catalysts offer improved recyclability and scalability (continuous production).

title: Electrochemical conversion of low-concentration carbon dioxide to multicarbon products: advances, challenges, and perspectives
abstract: This review highlights advances in electrochemical conversion of low-concentration CO 2 to multicarbon products, covering dilute and impurity-containing CO 2 , capture-solution electrolysis, bioelectrocatalysis, and techno-economic analysis.

title: A louder kind of belonging
abstract: In a Beijing park, a dispute over square dancing versus basketball changed how Haiyun Xu heard the music of women dancers — and revealed unwritten rules that govern whose movements belong in public space.

title: Benchmarking mechanistic credibility in electrocatalysis through data-driven evaluation
abstract: The performance of electrocatalytic reactions has rapidly advanced in recent years, yet there remain numerous controversies in the underlying mechanistic understanding of these systems. This Perspective proposes a framework for rating the strength of evidence and cross-community validation of mechanistic claims for the most-studied electrocatalytic reactions.

title: Diffuse Fabry-Pérot Cavities from a Bifunctional Metal Mesh for Angle-Invariant Electrochromic Camouflage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tungsten trioxide (WO3) is a widely studied electrochromic material, yet its monochromatic switching behavior limits its applicability in scenarios requiring dynamic color modulation. To address this limitation, integration with a Fabry-Pérot (F-P) optical cavity has emerged as an effective strategy for expanding color tunability while reducing viewing-angle dependence. In this work, a simplified F-P cavity is constructed using stainless-steel mesh (SSM) as a bifunctional reflector and electrode, with a sputtered WO3 film serving as the electrochromic spacer. This design enables continuous full-spectrum color modulation across the visible range through precise regulation of the WO3 layer thickness. Meanwhile, the microscale topological roughness of the SSM introduces diffuse light scattering, which synergistically couples with F-P interference to compensate for optical path variations at different viewing angles. As a result, angle-independent structural coloration is achieved over a broad viewing-angle range from 15 to 90°. Furthermore, benefiting from the high electrical conductivity and unique porous structure of the SSM, a 14 cm × 14 cm inverted flexible electrochromic device was successfully fabricated. The resulting device exhibits fast switching kinetics, excellent mechanical durability under repeated bending, and stable reversible multicolor performance, demonstrating a scalable and cost-effective platform for adaptive visible-light camouflage and energy-efficient reflective display applications.

title: High-entropy alloy aerogels promote selective glycerol oxidation to tartronate at industrial current densities
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The highly selective electrosynthesis of tartronate (TA) from glycerol oxidation reaction (GOR) at industrial current densities remains a grand challenge, as it necessitates the concurrent oxidation of two primary hydroxyl groups while suppressing C-C cleavage. Herein, we engineer a PtCuCoCeSn high-entropy alloy aerogel electrocatalyst for efficient glycerol-to-TA electrooxidation under industrially relevant conditions. This catalyst delivers a high current density of 461 mA cm−2 at 1.0 VRHE, alongside a TA selectivity of 81.4%. In situ characterization and theoretical calculations reveal that Ce modulates the glycerol adsorption conformation, enhances the adsorption of glycerate intermediates, and promotes its conversion to TA. Meanwhile, Sn facilitates TA desorption and suppresses the C-C cleavage, thereby ensuring high selectivity at elevated current. Furthermore, in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer configured with Pt1.5CuCoCeSn | | PtCuCoCeSn, the system achieves a stable TA selectivity of 78.9% at a cell voltage of 1.6 V with a TA production rate of 4.9 mmol h−1, and maintains stable operation for over 240 h. This work provides fundamental insights into the design of high-entropy alloys for the sustainable electrosynthesis of value-added chemicals at scale.

title: Genesis of Nucleation Sites Dictates the Fate of 2D MoS2 Growth
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Scalable synthesis of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) with atomic precision is critical for next-generation flexible electronics. Chemical vapor deposition is a primary strategy for the growth of 2D TMD films. The process, however, is difficult to control at large scales due to the strong interplay between time-dependent concentration gradients of the precursors, setup-specific fluid dynamics, and surface energetics. Here, we present a dual-channel reactor system that allows independent dynamic control over transition metal and chalcogen precursor dosages. This enables preprogrammed delivery of precursor partial pressures, effectively decoupling the chemical potentials governing nucleation and subsequent growth phases. This was demonstrated using molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) synthesis as an archetypical model system. By combining experiments and time-dependent fluid dynamics simulations, we have revealed that the genesis of nucleation sites, the local Mo/S ratio established during the fleeting initial nucleation event, decisively dictates the ultimate growth morphology. We demonstrate that near-stoichiometric S-rich conditions during both nucleation and growth stages favor 2D lateral expansion via heterogeneous surface reactions, whereas excessively S-rich conditions promote 3D growth through homogeneous gas-phase reactions. Furthermore, we show that the spatial limitations of traditional horizontal configurations, such as inherent concentration gradients and mass transport bottlenecks, are effectively bypassed using an optimized vertical substrate orientation. By thinning the boundary layer and stabilizing the chemical potential, this configuration shifts the rate-limiting step toward surface reaction kinetics. This dual approach of temporal precursor modulation and spatial substrate optimization provides a robust protocol for the deterministic synthesis of 2D TMDs.

title: Conserved molecular properties of dissolved organic matter during Weddell Sea Deep Water formation
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) is decreasing in volume due to climate change with potential consequences for abyssal carbon storage, where carbon is locked away from the atmosphere for centuries. Understanding the formation and export of dissolved organic matter (DOM) on the Antarctic shelf is therefore essential to determine how organic carbon enters this deep-sea reservoir. Here, we investigate solid-phase extractable DOM (SPE-DOM) transformations in the Weddell Sea, where half of AABW forms. Molecular and structural properties of SPE-DOM remain unchanged during dense-water formation. Shelf processes minimally affect exported organics into the deep-sea, likely due to remineralization to inorganic carbon enhanced by long residence times on the shelf. Consequently, the dominant SPE-DOM signature in Weddell Sea Deep Water (WSDW) is established before dense shelf waters mix with warmer off-shelf waters. We estimate that 0.155 ± 0.03 PgC are transferred annually from the Weddell Sea to AABW, and that its molecular composition is expected to remain conserved despite ongoing climate-driven weakening of AABW.

title: Hydrogen-Bond-Regulated PAN/PTFBZ Nanofibrous Composite Barriers for Flame-Resistant Thermal Runaway Protection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrospun polymer barriers are attractive for lightweight thermal protection in compact lithium–ion battery (LIB) devices, but their limited flame resistance and structural stability under thermal abuse restrict their practical use. Herein, a hydrogen-bond-regulated nanofibrous composite barrier was developed by incorporating trifluoromethyl-modified benzoxazine (TFBZ)-derived components into a polyacrylonitrile (PAN) matrix. The benzoxazine-derived phenolic hydroxyl groups could interact with the nitrile groups of PAN through O–H···N≡C hydrogen bonding, contributing to improved interfacial compatibility and fibrous-network stabilization while retaining the processability of PAN. Thermogravimetric analysis showed that PAN/PTFBZ retained 96.1% of its mass at 300 °C, compared with 75.8% for pure PAN. Cone calorimetry showed that the total heat release and total smoke production were reduced by 64.9% and 45.1%, respectively, and the limiting oxygen index (LOI) increased from 18% to 31%. In battery-level thermal abuse tests, the time to complete thermal runaway (TR) increased from 1068.7 ± 14.6 s to 1884.7 ± 44.2 s, corresponding to 76.4% delay. These results suggest that interfacial hydrogen-bonding regulation, together with the ─CF3-modified benzoxazine-derived structure and compact char formation, contributes to improved flame resistance, structural retention, and battery-level thermal-abuse protection.

title: A Keratin and Polyacrylamide Dual Network Hydrogel Based on Dynamic Coordination between Polydopamine and Mg2+ for Infected Wound Repair
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Exogenous bacterial infection severely impairs skin wound repair and creates a complex therapeutic challenge that requires simultaneous infection control, oxidative stress regulation, and tissue regeneration. In this study, a PAM/HK/PDANP-Mg2+ multifunctional hydrogel (HPPM) was developed as a cascade therapeutic dressing for infected wounds. In this system, polyacrylamide (PAM) provided a flexible covalently cross-linked framework. Hydrolyzed keratin (HK) offered bioactive and cytocompatible interfaces. Polydopamine nanoparticles (PDANPs) endowed the hydrogel with adhesiveness, photothermal antibacterial activity, and radical scavenging capacity. Coordination between Mg2+ and PDA, together with intermolecular hydrogen bonding, contributed to reversible physical cross-linking within the PAM framework. The optimized HPPM (0.012) hydrogel exhibited a porous structure, high swelling ratio (∼1277%), strong adhesion properties (31.00 kPa), and large tensile elongation (∼560%). Under 808 nm near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, HPPM achieved mild photothermal heating and over 99% antibacterial efficiency against Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus). It also showed favorable antioxidant activity, cytocompatibility, and pro-migratory effects. In an S. aureus-infected rat wound model, HPPM (0.012) + NIR accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammation, enhanced collagen deposition and re-epithelialization, and regulated IL-10/TNF-α expression. These results suggest that HPPM promotes infected wound healing through dynamic coordination-driven cascade remodeling of the infected wound microenvironment.

title: Prospective and genetic analyses implicate lower immunosurveillance in the aetiology of prostate cancer
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Tumour-promoting inflammation and immune evasion are key features of cancer, but prospective evidence linking specific immune pathways to prostate cancer risk remains limited. Here we show that circulating proteins involved in immune regulation may influence prostate cancer development. We analyse 368 immune- and inflammation-related proteins measured in blood samples from men in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC), including 1434 cases and matched controls, and combine these results with data from UK Biobank. While no proteins are associated with risk in EPIC alone after multiple testing correction, meta-analysis identifies several proteins linked to prostate cancer risk, including IL15 and FLT3LG, in particular, in blood taken long before diagnosis. Higher levels of immune surveillance-related proteins, particularly those involved in natural killer and T cell activity, are associated with lower prostate cancer risk, whereas genetic evidence implicates PARP1, SPINT2 and NME3 in increased risk. These findings suggest that immune pathways play a role in prostate cancer development and highlight potential targets for prevention.

title: Temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder revealed through predictive symptom networks
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Temporal dynamics of psychiatric symptoms challenge researchers and clinicians due to their inherent unpredictability. The cyclical on–off nature of symptoms linked to physiological rhythms, such as the menstrual cycle, provides a unique window to apply temporal and dynamic modeling of psychiatric symptoms. This can be studied in premenstrual dysphoric disorder, a female hormone-triggered condition characterized by cyclical symptoms. Yet intra-individual temporal patterns and dynamics of these symptoms remain unknown. Here we show that individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder differ widely in symptom timing, severity, and persistence, clustering into distinct temporal symptom profiles. Dynamic modelling uncovers temporal order among core psychiatric symptoms, with anxiety emerging as a central symptom in the unfolding of affective dysregulation. Depression shows the strongest predictive associations with subsequent severity of the other core symptoms, while irritability predicts the severity of depression at the longest time-interval. These temporal symptom dynamics reveal mechanistic psychoneuroendocrine pathways and inform precision, time-sensitive interventions for the mental health of individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder.

title: Diffusion Models for Small-Molecule Design
abstract: Abstract Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

title: The representational geometry of cognitive maps under cognitive control
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Recent work has shown that the brain abstracts non-spatial relationships between entities or task states into representations called cognitive maps. Here, we investigate how cognitive control enables flexible top-down selection of goal-relevant information from multidimensional cognitive maps retrieved from memory. We examine the relationship between cognitive control and representational geometry by conducting parallel analyses of functional magnetic resonance imaging data and recurrent neural network models trained to perform the same task. We find both stable map-like representations in a medial temporal lobe and orbitofrontal cortical network that reflect both task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions and context-dependent, orthogonal representations of only task-relevant dimensions in a frontoparietal network. These representational motifs also emerge with distinct temporal profiles over the course of training in the recurrent neural network, with map-like representations appearing first. We further show that increasing control demands due to incongruence (conflicting responses) between current task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions impact the geometry of subjective representations, and the degree of this effect further accounts for individual differences in cognitive control. Taken together, our findings show how complementary representational geometries balance stability and behavioral flexibility, and reveal an intricate relationship between cognitive control and cognitive map geometry.

title: A lactate-fatty acid loop drives prostate cancer bone colonization by mediating metabolic interplay between tumor cells and osteoblasts
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bone metastasis is the major cause of morbidity and mortality in advanced prostate cancer, yet current therapies provide only limited clinical benefit. Here, we show that prostate cancer cells metabolically adapt to the bone microenvironment by utilizing bone-cell-derived lactate as an alternative nutrient source. Beyond fueling oxidative phosphorylation, lactate serves as carbon source for fatty acid synthesis. Among the resulting lipid products, oleic acid is secreted to reward osteoblast, establishing a reciprocal metabolic interplay that supports both tumor progression and pathological bone formation. Mechanistically, we identify MCT1 as the essential transporter mediating lactate uptake in bone-colonizing tumor cells. MCT1 expression is coordinately regulated by NFAT signaling and extracellular glucose availability at both transcriptional and post-translational levels. Genetic deletion and pharmacological inhibition of MCT1 markedly suppresses prostate tumor growth in bone. Together, these findings uncover a lactate-driven metabolic crosstalk, identifying MCT1 as a promising therapeutic target for prostate cancer bone metastasis.

title: Global environmental genomics reveals vast uncultivated protist diversity and taxonomic blind spots
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Protists, defined as eukaryotes distinct from plants, animals and fungi, comprise much of eukaryotic phylogenetic diversity and perform key ecological functions, yet most lineages remain uncultivated and poorly represented in reference databases. Amplicon-based 18S rRNA gene surveys have transformed protist ecology, but primer bias, PCR bias and marker length can limit recovery of divergent lineages. Here, we conduct a cultivation-independent, rDNA operon-centered survey of over 30,000 assembled metagenomes, protist single-cell genomes and 21 long-amplicon datasets spanning marine, freshwater and soil-associated environments. We recover 157,956 long 18S rRNA gene sequences (≥800 bp), which together with reference sequences cluster into 103,338 OTUs at 97% identity and 24,438 OTUs at 85% identity. After excluding non-protist groups and singletons, 81% of the remaining 9543 protist 85%-OTUs consist exclusively of environmental sequences with no described representative. A concatenated 18S-28S rRNA framework reveals strong underrepresentation of Amoebozoa, Discoba, and Rhizaria in current references and identifies 13 candidate deeply divergent lineages with little or no database representation, some of which we link to partial genomes recovered by single-cell genomics. We further characterize their ecosystem distributions and predict associations with bacteria and other eukaryotes. This study provides a global, cultivation-independent resource for targeted sampling and downstream genomic, ecological and experimental characterization.

title: Pico-X: a 24.9 nanowatt microcontroller for long-duration autonomous operation in flexible landing-pad sensor networks
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Flexible landing-pad sensor networks require local intelligence that can remain dormant for long periods yet respond rapidly to sparse mechanical events. General-purpose microcontrollers incur substantial retained-state and control overhead under such workloads, whereas hardwired controllers sacrifice programmability. Here we present Pico-X, a state-minimized eight-bit programmable processor designed for patch-level wake-up, sensing, event classification and reporting. A compact multi-cycle architecture, unified retentive memory and workload-constrained instruction framework reduce retained state and standby leakage. Fabricated in a 28-nanometre fully depleted silicon-on-insulator process, Pico-X consumes 728.2 nanowatts during active operation at 25 kilohertz and 24.9 nanowatts in state-retentive deep sleep without body bias, while preserving deterministic state recovery after wake-up. We further integrate Pico-X into a 4 × 4 flexible landing-pad demonstrator that records 12,842 events and achieves class-wise detection rates (recall) of 96.3% for occupancy, 92.1% for load imbalance, and 94.6% for deformation. Mean event-to-report latency is 38 milliseconds, packet delivery reaches 99.12%, and operation remains stable for more than 72 hours. These results establish a low-overhead programmable architecture for distributed, long-duration sensing.

title: Rational Selection of Hole Contacts with an Organic Light-Emitting Diode Industry p-Dopant for Fully Vacuum-Processed Perovskite/Silicon Tandems
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Translating perovskite/silicon tandems to fully vacuum-based manufacturing requires vacuum-compatible p-doped hole contacts, yet clear selection criteria for doped hole-transport materials (HTMs) remain underdeveloped compared with C60-based electron contacts. Here, we report a fully vacuum-processed perovskite/silicon tandem reaching 29.1% power conversion efficiency, among the highest reported for tandems with fully vacuum-deposited perovskite top cells, enabled by transferring the organic light-emitting diode (OLED)-industry p-dopant NDP-9 and an evaporable arylamine HTM into the perovskite stack. Comparing TaTm, Spiro-TTB, and TAPC shows that contact selection does not follow apparent host–dopant interaction strength derived from theoretical calculations or conventional optical, vibrational, and photoemission spectroscopies. Instead, device-level charge extraction and recombination metrics identify NDP-9-doped TaTm as the most effective contact, also yielding 20.0% in a single-junction 1.70 eV wide-bandgap cell. These results point to transport-based screening as a practical route to selecting vacuum-compatible doped hole contacts.

title: Operando Time-of-Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry Reveals Iodine-Mediated Redox Chemistry in Solid-State Li–S Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Understanding dynamic reaction pathways in all-solid-state batteries remains challenging because electrochemical processes occur at buried solid–solid interfaces and transient intermediates are difficult to detect with conventional analytical techniques. While operando techniques typically probe structural or macroscopic changes, direct detection of reactive species during operation remains experimentally demanding. Here, we introduce a dynamic operando time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry platform that enables continuous chemical analysis of processes in a solid-state battery under electrochemical bias. Using this approach, we directly observe a pronounced increase of the I2– signal during charging of a Li–S composite cathode containing LiI, indicating the formation of elemental iodine. Concurrent changes in the sulfur-containing ion signals suggest the involvement of iodine species in the ongoing redox processes. These results reveal transient, low-concentration species at buried interfaces undetectable by other operando techniques, offering a pathway for identifying reactive intermediates in conversion-type solid-state batteries and related electrochemical systems.

title: Mesoscale Chiroptical Order in Achiral Metal-Halide Nanoplatelet Assemblies
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract This viewpoint presents the circular dichroism emerging directly from the self-assembly of achiral metal-halide perovskite nanoplatelets such as Cs3Cd2Cl7, Rb3Cd2Cl7, and CsPbBr3. Specifically, even when they form only short-range, polydisperse assemblies rather than the long-range helical superlattices reported in prior works, these short assemblies also exhibit chiral optical properties. The effect persists across emissive and nonemissive systems; with diverse stacking morphologies, and both in solution and film forms. Thus, this viewpoint establishes mesoscale chirality as a general principle of nanoplatelet self-assemblies.

title: A further acceleration of clean energy is needed for global CO2 emissions to peak and decline
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Global fossil fuel CO
                    2
                    emissions have grown 0.8% per year on average between 2019 and 2025. Here we project a decrease of 0.4% in 2026, probably as a short-term response to the energy shock triggered by the Iran conflict. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power offset about 64–79% of increasing emissions from demand growth through 2028; acceleration in clean technology deployment is needed to guarantee emissions peak and subsequent decline.

title: Electric vehicle battery materials supply disruptions can be mitigated with chemistry changes and recycling
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Battery materials supply chains for plug-in electric vehicles face vulnerabilities to disruptions from geopolitical disputes and natural disasters. Through industry interviews, we identify scenarios that could disrupt materials supply by 2030. We estimate the impacts on US automotive production, prices, and consumer costs in an economic equilibrium model of the US automotive industry. We find year-long disruptions can have large impacts: trade restrictions that reduce processed lithium supply from China by 30% and disasters shutting down the three largest cobalt mines increase average new vehicle prices (including conventional vehicles and plug-in electric vehicles) by $1,100-1,600, costing consumers $14-17 billion. However, feasible changes in battery chemistry and materials supply by 2030 mitigate these negative impacts. If 85% of battery electric vehicle models are produced with lithium iron phosphate batteries and at least 100 kilotonnes of planned production of recycled lithium carbonate equivalent is available, disruption costs decrease by more than half.

title: A national baseline for methane sink habitats and methanotroph diversity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Methane emissions account for nearly a third of the Earth’s effective radiative forcing, with methanotrophs playing a critical role in mitigating emissions by oxidising methane in diverse environments. Despite their ecological importance, methanotrophic diversity and environmental distribution remain incompletely characterised due to cultivation challenges, incomplete or low-quality metagenome-assembled genomes, and limited taxonomic resolution in marker gene surveys. Here, we present a national study of the biogeography of novel and known methanotrophs across Denmark’s major natural, urban and agricultural habitats, using genome-resolved classification of 10,683 metagenomes and 102 new methanotrophic species. By linking metabolic potential to habitat-specific distributions, we reveal uncharacterised methanotrophs as dominant in natural ecosystems. These findings provide a comprehensive baseline of methanotroph diversity, reveal clear contrasts between natural and disturbed habitats, and highlight candidate species and habitats for future methane-mitigation strategies.

title: Early evidence links data centre exposure to coal power retirement timelines
abstract: Data centre expansion may slow the coal-fired power plants phase-out, complicating decarbonization pathways. This study finds that coal units exposed to post-2020 data centres have lower retirement risks and their potential lifetime extensions could cause large additional CO2 emissions.

title: Decoding Symmetry-Breaking Band Structures in Nanocatalysts for Kinetically Favorable Li-S Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The conventional d-band center theory represents catalyst electronic structures using an averaged energy and may therefore overlook higher-order information contained in the complex and asymmetric density of states of alloy catalysts (ACs). Here, combining quantum chemistry with interpretable machine learning, we identify the transformed d-band peak position (Epp) as an alternative electronic descriptor for alloy–polysulfide interactions in lithium-sulfur batteries. Epp integrates information related to the d-band position, bandwidth, and band shape, and correlates with the electron occupation of S3p–Md (M = metal) antibonding states and the calculated polysulfide adsorption strength. A series of bimetallic ACs recovered from spent lithium-ion batteries was employed to experimentally evaluate the descriptor. Within this series, CoFe shows favorable electrochemical performance, enabling an ampere-hour-level pouch cell with an energy density of 426 Wh kg–1 under a sulfur loading of 12.5 mg cm–2 and an electrolyte-to-sulfur ratio of 3.6 mL g–1.

title: Higher warming leads to a larger zero-emissions commitment
abstract: Scientific grounds for a net-zero policy assume near-zero committed warming over a few decades after CO2 emissions cease. A modelling study suggests that if prior peak temperatures rise above 2 °C before cessation of CO2 emissions, committed warming increases, making it harder to stabilize global warming.

title: Coal power lives longer next to data centres
abstract: Data centres are among the world’s fastest growing electricity consumers. An analysis of more than 9,000 facilities worldwide links the artificial intelligence-era expansion of data centres to delayed coal plant retirements and around 2 Gt of additional carbon dioxide emissions.

title: Soft polymer coatings form hard directional bonding
abstract: Soft polymer coatings spontaneously rearrange on nanosphere surfaces to form directional bonds, unlocking an alternative route to delicate nanoparticle superlattices.

title: Widespread North American pollution and health impacts from early twentieth century copper production
abstract: Mining and industrial emissions can be substantially reduced by technological interventions. The historical case of copper production in Anaconda, Montana shows the widespread health burdens that can result when lax regulation delays such interventions.

title: Cryo-EM reveals conserved baseplate-architecture and distinct accessory-protein assemblies in mycobacteriophages Claus, Corndog and Mysterious
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mycobacteriophages, viruses infecting mycobacteria, hold therapeutic promise against antibiotic-resistant mycobacterial infections. Although thousands of mycobacteriophages have been isolated, high-resolution baseplate structures have been reported for only two, highlighting a gap in understanding phage–host interactions. Most mycobacteriophages are siphophages with four structural components: capsid, connector, non-contractile tail, and baseplate. The baseplate plays a critical role in host recognition, adsorption, and genome delivery. Here, we present atomic-resolution cryo-EM baseplate structures of three mycobacteriophages, Claus, Corndog, and Mysterious. These exhibit distinct inverted crown-, barrel-, and cage-like architectures, respectively, yet share a conserved architecture with a 6:6:3 stoichiometry of homohexameric tail tube proteins (TTPs), distal tail proteins (DTPs), and homotrimeric baseplate hub proteins (BHPs). The baseplate core is formed by DTPs and BHPs, with terminal TTPs making direct proximal contacts with DTPs and contributing to overall structure. While the central core is conserved, the exterior domains diverge across the phages. Surrounding the conserved cores are diverse baseplate accessory proteins (BAPs), including upper baseplate proteins (BppUs), central fiber proteins (CFPs), and others, which assemble into distinct peripheral architectures and give rise to two baseplate-opening mechanisms. These structures reveal a conserved baseplate core complex diversified by BAPs, a feature potentially shared across mycobacteriophage siphophage families.

title: Agricultural data source choice as a dominant control on nitrogen surplus uncertainty
abstract:
Abstract
                  Agricultural nitrogen (N) surplus (the residual of total N inputs after harvest removal, plant-tissue storage, runoff and atmospheric losses) is a leading cause of groundwater and other environmental contamination in intensive food-producing regions, yet N surplus estimates often depend on inconsistent fertilizer, harvest and manure datasets in an N balance. Using California’s Central Valley as a data-rich test case, we propagate expert, survey-based, regulatory and county-level datasets through a fixed crop-specific N surplus framework to generate 24 cases. Holding model structure and land use constant, we quantify the large divergence in estimated N surplus arising from data choice, especially for manure-treated field crops. The uncertainty about N surplus is consequential: it can reorder which crops, regions and pathways receive priority for groundwater protection. The resulting spread among N surplus outcomes is large enough to alter hotspot rankings, mitigation priorities and screening-level estimates of economic burden. Credible nitrogen assessment at farm to global scales therefore requires explicit propagation of agricultural data source uncertainty, which can materially affect resulting N surplus estimates. Absent specific local data, the uncertainty magnitudes reported here may guide N surplus uncertainty assessment in other regional, national and global analyses.

title: Dynamic, Wet‐Adhesive Hydrogels for Enhanced Interface Healing in Cartilage Repair
abstract: ABSTRACT Articular cartilage defects remain a major clinical challenge due to the tissue's limited self‐repair capacity. Although numerous biomaterial‐based strategies have been explored, achieving a stable and functional cartilage interface remains difficult. A critical barrier is the poor integration between grafts and native cartilage, leading to fibrocartilage formation, delamination, and repair failure. Current approaches show limited success due to inadequate wet adhesion, mechanical mismatch, and insufficient chemical bonding. Here, we report a dynamically adaptive wet‐adhesive hydrogel composed of oxidized hyaluronic acid, quaternized chitosan, and silk fibroin (OHA/QCS/SF) for enhanced cartilage interface healing. The precursor exhibited rapid underwater spreading on hydrated substrates and displaced interfacial fluid in a fluid‐covered assay. Fluorescence imaging further revealed wetting and infiltration into the PAAm hydrogel. Dynamic Schiff‐base bonding between aldehyde groups in the hydrogel and amine‐containing components at the cartilage interface further promoted wet adhesion, while the reversible network enabled self‐healing under mechanical disturbance. In a rabbit cartilage defect model, the hydrogel loaded with synovial membrane‐derived mesenchymal stem cells (SMSCs) improved defect filling, host–graft integration, and cartilage‐like regeneration. This study provides a dynamic wet‐adhesive hydrogel strategy for improving biomaterial–cartilage interface healing in fluid‐rich joint environments.

title: Pd Single‐Atom Engineered Janus BiOCl/MXene Heterostructure for Printed Self‐Decoupled Temperature‐Humidity Dual‐Mode Sensors
abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement of flexible sensing technologies is of paramount importance in biomedical engineering. However, achieving high‐fidelity multi‐modal temperature‐humidity sensing without inter‐channel cross‐talk and computational post‐processing remains a formidable challenge due to overlapping transduction mechanisms. In this study, an unprecedented electron‐ion synergistic functional material, featuring a unique inherent self‐decoupling capability, was developed based on the Janus hierarchical heterostructure. Through interfacial chemical engineering of Pd single‐atom anchoring and heterogeneous‐nucleation‐driven vertical growth of BiOCl on hollow MXene, the constructed material architecture successfully establishes fundamentally segregated electronic and ionic stimulus‐response pathways. Specifically, humidity fluctuations trigger ultra‐fast quasi‐2D proton conduction facilitated by localized potential wells and electronic redistribution generated around atomically dispersed Pd sites, while temperature gradients induce entropy‐driven carrier diffusion within the conductive MXene network. By suppressing signal cross‐talk through rigorous mechanistic orthogonality, the fabricated sensing array exhibits outstanding response characteristics (37.5/50 ms for humidity response/recovery and 25/62.5 ms for high/low‐temperature response), alongside superior oxidation resistance and robust functional durability (enduring 5000 cycles of testing). Ultimately, leveraging this multi‐modal sensing platform and machine learning algorithm, the integrated closed‐loop therapeutic system enables accurate evaluation of wound healing progression as well as on‐demand drug release, pioneering a new paradigm for next‐generation flexible electronics and adaptive healthcare modalities.

title: Liquid Luminescent Materials Based on 10 H ‐Pyrido[1,2‐ a ]‐5‐indolium Salts
abstract: ABSTRACT Next‐generation flexible optoelectronics and soft robotics require adaptive luminescent materials that withstand extreme environments while remaining deformable. However, the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of current solvent‐free ionic liquids suffers from fundamental limitations arising from aggregation‐caused quenching and rapid nonradiative decay, and these liquids degrade under thermal and chemical stress. This study presents a supramolecular locking strategy that overcomes these limitations through kinetically stabilized anion–π + interactions. Specifically, a rigid N‐doped fluorene (10 H ‐pyrido[1,2‐ a ]‐5‐indolium, PIn + ) was paired with selected anions to maintain fluidity and suppress nonradiative molecular motion by locking radiative pathways in the liquid state. This ionic tethering approach yielded an unprecedented PLQY of 80% in the liquid state while preserving the solvent‐free liquid nature of the material. These highly emissive ionic liquids exhibited extreme physicochemical robustness, withstanding thermal decomposition up to 400°C, retaining intense emission without volatilization even under reduced pressure at 250°C, and resisting strongly acidic and basic environments. Derived from a versatile and readily synthesizable fluorene platform, this system also provides broad opportunities for structural customization. These findings establish a general molecular design principle for highly robust and emissive liquid fluorophores, providing a foundation for indestructible and flexible photonic technologies operating under extreme conditions.
