title: Rate Capability of Lithium‐Rich Manganese‐Based Oxide Cathodes: Charge–Discharge Kinetics, Multiscale Bottlenecks, and Dynamic Rate‐Determining Steps
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials deliver a reversible specific capacity exceeding 250 mAh g −1 through synergistic anionic and cationic redox, promising for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries, yet their poor rate capability remains a critical barrier to practical deployment, particularly for fast‐charging applications. This review deconstructs rate‐limiting mechanisms at three levels, namely direct charge‐transport impediments, kinetic sluggishness of anionic redox, and degradation cascade of phase transformations, voltage decay, and microcracking that exacerbates kinetics. A central insight is that the rate‐determining step (RDS) shifts from electron‐transfer to ion‐diffusion dominance, governed by the exchange current density ( j 0 ) and the limiting current density ( j d ). Modification strategies are classified into two threads, kinetic enhancement by shortening diffusion paths and lowering migration barriers, and structural stabilization by reinforcing bonds and suppressing oxygen release. Importantly, the often‐overlooked charging kinetics are critically assessed, as the asymmetric nature of anionic redox imposes a more severe bottleneck for fast charging than for high‐rate discharging. Methodological limitations in cross‐study C‐rate comparisons, arising from variations in electrode loading and testing protocols, are also examined to enable more rigorous evaluation of reported performance. This review ultimately provides a theoretical foundation for rational design of high‐rate LRMO cathodes toward practical energy storage applications.

title: Ion–Electron Coupling Transport in Semiconductor Nanotubes for Retinomorphic Vision
abstract: ABSTRACT A key limitation of current artificial visual systems lies in their single‐channel signal transduction, which fundamentally departs from the parallel processing architecture of the biological retinas enabled by rod and cone cells. To bridge this gap, we developed a retinomorphic vision device by ion‐electron coupling transport based on carbon nanotube (CNT)/zinc oxide (ZnO) heterostructured nanotubes. Upon optical stimuli, this device generates two distinct ionic and electronic current signals, effectively mimicking the parallel phototransduction pathways in biological vision. This dual‐channel property enables efficient machine vision perception, achieving luminance adaptation and color discrimination accuracies of 96.5% and 98.2%, respectively. Furthermore, traffic‐light‐guided closed‐loop navigation of a mobile vehicle in a real scene has verified its application potential in embodied intelligence. This “single device enabled, distinguishable dual‐channel readouts” principle opens a new avenue toward artificial vision systems.

title: Sustainable Soft Electronic Devices by High‐Performance Recyclable Elastomers and Conductors
abstract: ABSTRACT Soft electronics have driven emerging advancements, which are expected to have wide‐range and large‐scale applications in health management, electronic skins, soft robotics, and interactive human‐machine interfaces. However, existing strategies mainly focus on isolated components, and system‐level soft electronic devices combining sustainable fabrication, robust performance, and versatile integrated functions have rarely been explored. Herein, we develop a recyclable soft electronic system enabled with multifunctional poly thioctic acid (TA) elastomer and high‐performance elastic metallic conductors. The multifunctional TA elastomer exhibits an exceptional combination of stretchability (435% strain), fracture energy (5.5 kJ/m 2 ), apparent adhesion energy on Cu (10.7 kJ/m 2 ), and thermal conductivity (0.69 W/m·K). These properties enable robust mechanical and electronic interfacing with different electronic components for sustainable soft circuits, while also endowing the electronic systems with outstanding self‐healing and recycling capabilities. Furthermore, by integrating with printable and recyclable elastic conductors based on eutectic liquid metals, the sustainable soft electronic systems can fully restore circuit functionality after complete mechanical rupture with the selfhealing capability of the composite elastomer and the elastic conductor. The system can be reprocessed to achieve full functionality restoration. The materials strategy developed in this study renders a promising solution for the development of soft and sustainable electronic devices.

title: Fluoride‐Mediated Host‐Activator Engineering in Homogeneous Lithium Glass Scintillators for Thermal‐Neutron Detection and Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Homogeneous lithium‐aluminosilicate‐glass scintillators offer transparency, scalable fabrication, and compositional flexibility, but their neutron response is limited by defect trapping and activator loading concentration. Here, fluoride‐mediated host‐activator engineering is introduced to overcome these coupled limitations in Ce 3+ ‐activated lithium aluminosilicate glasses. F − preferentially coordinates with Li + and Mg 2+ , preserving the primary Si/Al─O tetrahedral units while reorganizing inter‐tetrahedral linkages. The resulting host‐network reconfiguration suppresses electronic disorder and defect‐mediated trapping, modulates medium‐range Ce‐centered correlations, broadens the viable Ce‐concentration window, and enables efficient excitation capture at ∼9 wt% CeO 2 (twice that of GS20). After 6 Li enrichment, it delivers 8003 photons neutron −1 , an energy resolution of 6.8%, a decay time of 85.06 ns, and a neutron peak‐to‐trough ratio of 77:1. To the best of our knowledge, these values represent the highest light yield and best energy resolution reported for a homogeneous transparent 6 Li‐enriched glass scintillator, achieving single‐digit neutron energy resolution for the first time and approaching the performance of 3 He proportional counters and high‐performance crystalline scintillators. A transparent plate exceeding 2 inches further enables proof‐of‐concept two‐dimensional thermal‐neutron imaging with a system‐level spatial resolution of 1.35 mm, demonstrating the scalability of the glass for position‐sensitive neutron imaging.

title: Ultralow Loading Iridium Doped Hollandite Manganese Oxide Nanowires for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient and durable catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are critical for hydrogen production but remain limited by reliance on scarce iridium (Ir). We present an ultralow‐loading Ir catalyst (3 at%, − 2 ) integrated within a hollandite MnO 2 framework, which lowers the overpotential at 10 mA cm − 2 from 580 mV (undoped α‐MnO 2 ) to 303 mV and delivers an Ir mass activity an order of magnitude higher than commercial IrO x . Varying pH and potential, we combine ICP‐MS dissolution measurements with x‐ray absorption spectroscopy, electron energy loss spectroscopy, and 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy. Dissolution is modest, with at least 79% of the Ir and 76% of the Mn remaining after 6 h under applied potential, and Ir remains oxidized and associated with the hollandite framework. Mn, in contrast, undergoes pH‐ and potential‐dependent reduction and local structural disorder. Notably, the strongest Mn reconstruction (pH 0, 1.65 V) coincides with moderate dissolution, whereas the greatest Ir and Mn loss (pH 0, 1.60 V) occurs where the residual material is less reconstructed. Net dissolution therefore does not report on local structural change, highlighting the need to evaluate dissolution, reconstruction, and oxidation state together when designing and assessing Ir‐efficient mixed‐metal oxide catalysts.

title: pH‐Responsive Synthetic Cells for Programmable In Situ Protein Synthesis and Release
abstract: ABSTRACT Lipid membrane‐bound synthetic cells provide programmable, cell‐like compartments for on‐demand biomolecule production. However, most cell‐free gene expression systems in synthetic cells are regulated by user‐imposed cues rather than signals associated with environmental or physiological states. Here, we present an acidity‐transducing synthetic cell that converts external pH changes into nucleic acid information to drive in situ protein synthesis. The system integrates gramicidin A proton channels for pH sensing, triplex‐forming single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) that releases a trigger ssDNA upon acidification, and a toehold switch RNA that activates translation in response to the released trigger ssDNA. This work further reveals that tuning the annealing length between the pH‐responsive and trigger ssDNAs controls the trigger‐release pH, which is critical for enabling acid‐triggered protein synthesis. The synthetic cells retain their pH‐responsive activity when embedded in alginate hydrogels, creating acidity‐responsive materials that synthesize proteins in situ rather than release preloaded cargo. Cell‐penetrating peptide tagging further enables selective protein release and target‐specific binding. This work establishes a molecular transduction strategy for programming synthetic cell materials to sense environmentally relevant acidity and generates functional biomolecules on demand.

title: Upcycling Piezoelectric Single‐Crystal Debris Into High‐Performance Flexible 0–3 Composites
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐value piezoelectric single‐crystal debris remains an untapped resource for flexible electromechanical materials. Although relaxor‐based ferroelectric single crystals offer exceptional piezoelectric properties, off‐cuts inevitably generated during precision processing are typically discarded because their irregular geometries prevent direct device integration. Here, we report a recycling‐to‐device upcycling strategy that converts industrial Pb(Mg 1/3 Nb 2/3 )O 3 –PbTiO 3 (PMN–PT) single‐crystal debris into high‐performance flexible 0–3 piezoelectric composites and energy harvesters through material–structure–mechanics co‐design. A ball‐milling‐based particle refinement procedure converts the debris into dispersible particulate fillers, while dielectrophoresis (DEP)‐assisted curing reorganizes randomly dispersed particles in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrix into vertically connected quasi‐1–3‐like networks. The polymer matrix provides mechanical tunability, allowing flexibility and dynamic stress transfer to the aligned single‐crystal network to be jointly optimized. The optimized composite achieves a d 33 of 118.5 pC N −1 while retaining mechanical flexibility, placing it among the highest‐performing flexible 0–3 piezoelectric composites. Comparative experiments and finite‐element simulations reveal that single‐crystal‐derived fillers exhibit stronger DEP‐induced enhancement than polycrystalline counterparts owing to more coherent intraparticle electromechanical conversion. Integrated into flexible energy harvesters, the optimized composite delivers a peak areal power density of 284.2 µW cm − 2 . This work establishes a scalable upcycling pathway for reutilizing high‐value functional crystal waste in flexible self‐powered electromechanical systems.

title: Preserving Polymorphic Crystalline Structures in Bulk Heterojunctions for Efficient Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The crystal structure of a material profoundly influences its physical, optical, and electronic properties. However, precise control over polymorph formation of non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) in bulk heterojunction active layers remains challenging for optimizing organic solar cell (OSC) performance. Here, we employ a non‐halogenated mixed‐solvent system comprising carbon disulfide (CS 2 ) and o‐xylene (OXY) to selectively regulate the crystallization of the high‐performance acceptor BTP‐eC9. A specific polymorph (Form II) is preferentially induced and consistently identified in powder, neat‐film, and bulk heterojunction samples by correlating wide‐angle x‐ray scattering (WAXS) and grazing‐incidence wide‐angle x‐ray scattering (GIWAXS) patterns with simulations derived from the corresponding single‐crystal structures. Compared with Form I, Form II exhibits improved optoelectronic properties, including extended exciton diffusion length, balanced charge mobility, and suppressed non‐radiative recombination. Consequently, Form II‐based devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.61% with a fill factor of 82.85%, representing a 27.0% relative improvement over Form I devices (PCE = 16.23%). Moreover, this method enables scalable manufacturing, with flexible OSCs (1 cm 2 active area) fabricated by slot‐die coating achieving a PCE of 17.93%. This work establishes a practical pathway for solution‐processed polymorph control and reveals the relationship among single‐crystal packing, acceptor molecular packing, and device performance.

title: Designing a Thermochemically Active Hydrogel With In Situ‐Formed Ceramic–Carbon Hybrid Barrier for Suppressing Thermal Runaway Propagation
abstract: ABSTRACT Preventing thermal runaway propagation (TRP) is critical for the safety of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). While hydrogel interlayers actively cool through water evaporation, their mechanical reinforcement with conventional fillers dilutes the water‐rich matrix and reduces enthalpy. Here, we propose a paradigm‐shifting strategy by using boric acid (BA) as a thermochemically active cross‐linker in a poly(AMPS) hydrogel. BA reconstructs the hydrogel network through dual N─H⋯O hydrogen bonding and B⋯O═C coordination, simultaneously enhancing compressive strength by 567%. Upon thermal runaway, the composite provides dual‐mode protection: (1) synergistic heat absorption (volumetric enthalpy > 2000 J cm − 3 ) via water evaporation and BA stepwise dehydration, accompanied by flame‐inhibiting SO 2 release. (2) In situ formation of a highly insulating ceramic–carbon hybrid barrier. Post‐test analysis reveals a critical BA content of 25 wt%, where tetrahedral boron coordination (63.3% BO 4 ) maximizes covalent B─O─C bonds that chemically “weld” B 2 O 3 to carbon. This trend in BO 4 fraction with BA loading quantitatively explains the exceptional TRP suppression, reducing the adjacent cell's peak temperature by over 500°C. Beyond a high‐performance material, this work establishes a general design principle: employing reactive fillers that orchestrate both multi‐stage energy management and tailored barrier synthesis, paving the way for next‐generation battery safety materials.

title: Sensitive, Broadband, and Stable Short‐Wave Infrared Photodetection and Imaging in Mixed‐Dimensional Organic/Inorganic Heterostructures
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional short‐wave infrared (SWIR) photodetectors confront cost disadvantages and fabrication complexity, whereas two‐dimensional (2D) van der Waals devices exhibit inherent performance limitations. Mixed‐dimensional organic/inorganic heterostructures offer a promising strategy for SWIR photodetection, synergizing strong optical absorption and tunability of organic semiconductors with high charge mobility and stability of inorganics. However, critical challenges remain in architecture design, including optimal carrier‐collection geometry, material selection, and interface engineering for boosting devices’ performance. Herein, a type‐II band‐aligned PTF/WSe 2 mixed‐dimensional heterostructure is reported for high‐performance broadband SWIR photodetection via heterostructure synergy and rational Schottky barrier engineering. The Cr/ p ‐WSe 2 /PTF configuration (∼ 0.28 eV barrier) achieves superior performance, while Cr/ n ‐WSe 2 /PTF suffers from a higher barrier (∼ 1.18 eV). The optimized device achieves broad spectral photoresponsivity (∼ 10 3 A/W, 1060–1470 nm) and exceptional performance at 1310 nm: ultrahigh photoresponsivity ( R = 2894 A/W), robust specific detectivity ( D * = 1.0×10 12 Jones), and excellent long‐term ambient stability. Versus standalone PTF, it delivers 17‐fold higher photoresponsivity and 96% lower bias voltage. High‐resolution SWIR image‐pattern reconstruction, together with concurrent performance improvements after six months of controlled storage, validates this PTF/WSe 2 mixed‐dimensional heterostructure's potential for advancing next‐generation high‐performance SWIR detectors.

title: A Dual‐Locked and H 2 S‐NO Tandem‐Activatable NIR‐II Nanoagent for Colon Cancer Theranostics
abstract: ABSTRACT Dual‐locked activatable theranostics have been emerging as a promising cancer therapy platform. However, most of the reported dual‐locked systems only restricted to enzyme‐responsive probes, new molecular tools with other biomarker‐responsiveness still remain challenging. Moreover, optical manipulation in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window can potentially boost the theranostic efficacy, but having rarely been explored. In this study, we report a dual‐locked and gas tandem‐activatable NIR‐II nanoagent for colon cancer theranostics. Water‐dispersible nanoparticles containing a nitrated organic small molecule (CTBN) and an acid‐responsive NO donor (NONOate; CTBNN‐NPs) are fabricated, displaying negligible emission in visible‐NIR region. Upon uptake by colon cancer cells, CTBNN‐NPs can be tandemly activated by the overexpressed H 2 S and the in situ released NO, thus turning on NIR‐II emission extending to 1200 nm. Moreover, the activated CTBNN‐NPs also demonstrate augmented NIR absorption as well as robust photothermal and type‐I photodynamic performance, achieving NIR‐II fluorescence imaging‐guided efficient photo‐elimination of colon cancer together with NO gas therapy, while exhibiting limited efficacy in the tested cervical and breast cancer models. This work provides a new molecular design approach to dual‐locked and H 2 S‐NO tandem‐activatable nanoagents with gas‐responsive and NIR‐II active capabilities, highlighting the exciting potential for cancer theranostics.

title: Defined Matrices Reveal Epithelial‐ and Mesenchymal‐Specific Responses to Stiffness and Adhesion in Human iPSC‐Derived Intestinal Organoids
abstract: ABSTRACT Human intestinal organoids (hIOs) are powerful models for studying development and disease, yet dissecting how physical and matrix cues shape epithelial and mesenchymal responses remains challenging due to reliance on ill‐defined matrices. Here, a fully defined hIO workflow was developed in which Matrigel was replaced by recombinant human substrates during pluripotent stem cell differentiation and by polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogels during 3D culture, while maintaining organoid viability and epithelial cytodifferentiation. Transcriptomic analyses show that both PEG‐ and Matrigel‐cultured hIO epithelial cells are most similar to human duodenal reference populations, and have greater transcriptional similarity to fetal than adult duodenal references. Despite this overall similarity, PEG culture is associated with subtle shifts in epithelial differentiation‐associated gene expression, together with altered mesenchymal ECM‐remodelling and integrin‐associated programs. Increasing matrix stiffness produces modest effects in epithelial cells, including increased MUC2‐positive cells, whereas mesenchymal transcriptional responses to stiffness are limited. Together, these findings establish a fully defined hIO platform that retains responsiveness to inflammatory stimulation while enabling controlled investigation of how matrix composition and stiffness shape epithelial and mesenchymal cell states in models of intestinal development and fibrosis.

title: Skunk Cabbage‐Inspired AIEgen Photoactuators With Multiwavelength Response, Ultrafast Actuation, and Multicolor Fluorescence
abstract: ABSTRACT Near‐infrared (NIR)‐responsive polymer actuators doped with inorganic photothermal agents face trade‐offs between photothermal performance and mechanical properties due to limited compatibility. Besides, most systems remain confined to 808 nm operation, as extending to 980 nm is hindered by poor absorption. Inspired by skunk cabbage thermogenesis, we develop ultra‐fast, multicolor fluorescent NIR‐responsive actuators by integrating aggregation‐induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) with excellent compatibility and photothermal properties into Janus‐structured polyimides (PIs) at ultra‐low doping (0.25 wt%). The multi‐donor‐π structure of AIEgen achieves redshifted NIR absorption extending to 980 nm and enhanced photothermal abilities through boosted intramolecular donor–acceptor interactions and molecular motion‐facilitated nonradiative decay (MMFND). Mirroring the mitochondrial working mode, AIEgens are uniformly embedded within PIs without compromising structural integrity, preserving mechanical properties above 100 MPa. Under NIR illumination, PI actuators achieve deformation with a bending speed of 900°/s, which facilitates crawling, gripping, and rapid continuous bidirectional flipping. The combination of multiwavelength photoresponse and multicolor fluorescence endows materials with dynamic information encoding. Programmable motions are implemented under different wavelengths through sequential, penetrative, and heat‐transfer actuation. This work provides guidelines for smart materials requiring precise 980 nm actuation with maintained mechanical robustness.

title: Determining Composition–Structure–Property Relationships in Quaternary Perovskitoids Through Megalibraries
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how composition governs structure and function is essential for designing functional materials, however, establishing these relationships remains prohibitively slow for materials with massive and tunable compositional spaces, such as Bi and Sb‐based perovskitoids. Here, a novel megalibrary‐based synthetic methodology has been developed and used to rapidly identify and characterize quaternary perovskite derivatives across an expansive compositional space. Parylene templates were used to synthesize one million compositionally distinct, positionally encoded Cs 3 Sb 2−x Bi x Br 9−y I y microcrystals on 2 × 2 cm 2 chips with 20 µm periodicity. These megalibraries enabled the systematic investigation of structural and optoelectronic evolution across this compositional space using micro‐area x‐ray diffraction, position‐resolved absorbance spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and confocal fluorescence microscopy. An unusual non‐monotonic bandgap shift was observed with increasing Br content, reaching a minimum at 33% Br. This behavior is attributed to the formation of halide‐segregated heterostructures, consisting of low‐dimensional, I‐rich shells surrounding Br‐rich layered cores. Phase separation was most pronounced in Sb‐rich compositions, which were found to stabilize heterostructure formation. This study demonstrates how megalibraries enable the simultaneous evaluation of key optoelectronic parameters, including bandgap and phase purity, revealing complex, composition‐dependent structure‐function relationships in perovskitoids and providing a versatile platform for accelerating the discovery of optoelectronic‐relevant materials.

The unique Ag/CeO2||SiO2 configuration, activated hydrogen spills over from Ag/SiO2 to hydrogenate pre-polarized DMO on Ag/CeO2, achieving a 6-fold turnover frequency boost and >1000-hour stability for methyl glycolate.

title: Intrinsically Stretchable Fully π‐Conjugated Polymer Films Enabled by Supramolecular Plasticized Micro‐Crosslinking‐Network for Flexible Polymer Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable fully π‐conjugated polymers (FπCPs) films with a fantastic optoelectronic property and outstanding deformation tolerance capacity, is a promising candidate for the fabrication of flexible optoelectronics devices. However, previous reported stretchable FπCPs films undergo irreversible chain slippage and alignment upon strain release, leading to plastic deformation, and consequently severe performance degradation during cyclic‐deformation operation. Herein, we proposed a supramolecular soft‐micro‐crosslinked strategy to achieve the stretchable p ‐ n FπCPs (P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI) films with a recoverable‐deformation ability for the flexible electronics. Three‐dimensional (3D) supramolecular micro‐crosslinked network formed by oxime‐urethane and hydrogen bonds allow for the excellent elastic deformation to dissipate transient stress while fundamentally suppressing permanent chain slippage. Micro‐crosslinked p ‐ n FπCPs free‐standing films achieved an elongation at break of > 40%. Flexible PLED based on P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI showed a stable green emission with brightness of ∼3300 cd cm −2 . Meanwhile, the performance of transferred PLED based on stretchable micro‐crosslinked films are independent on the tensile ratio (>20%) with a maximum brightness of ∼2000 cd m −2 , revealed the excellent cycle‐deformation‐stability than device based on crosslinked films. Therefore, these supramolecular micro‐crosslinked networks can enhance instantaneous toughness and confer a critical resistance to long‐term stress relaxation and plastic deformation, further ensure the device excellent deformation stability.

title: Polymer‐Directed Crystal Growth Regulation: Template‐Free Synthesis of Mesoporous Single‐Crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3
abstract: ABSTRACT Transition metal borates are attractive anode candidates for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) because of their high specific capacity and environmental benignity; however, their structural collapse induced by large volume changes during cycling leads to rapid capacity degradation. In this study, we report a polymer‐directed crystal growth regulation strategy that enables the template‐free synthesis of mesoporous single‐crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3 (MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 ). Polyethyleneimine (PEI) acts as a bifunctional regulator, coordinating Mn 2+ ions and hydrogen bonding with borate ions to modulate hydrolysis and condensation, thereby yielding a hybrid precursor. Subsequent hydrothermal treatment yields single‐crystalline MnBO 2 OH nanobelts, which are converted by calcination into MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 . As an anode active material for lithium‐ion batteries, MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 delivers a reversible capacity of 1440 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 , more than twice that of bulk Mn 2 OBO 3 . Notably, this polymer‐directed strategy is readily extendable to doped MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 (e.g., Fe, V, and Mg), providing a versatile platform for the design of porous single‐crystalline materials for energy storage.

title: Efficient H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis With Valorization by X‐Packing NDI Cocrystal Catalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven photocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis offers a sustainable and green alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. However, coordinated regulation of electron‐transfer (ET) and energy‐transfer (EnT) pathways for efficient H 2 O 2 production remains challenging. Organic charge‐transfer (CT) cocrystals, which reconfigure the energy‐level structure through new intermolecular electronic states, provide a promising avenue to overcome this limitation. Herein, we report a CT cocrystal photocatalyst, DPNDI‐Py, prepared by liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) of N, N′‐bis(4‐pyridyl)‐1,4,5,8‐naphthalenediimide (DPNDI) and pyrene (Py). The cocrystal harbors an X‐packed donor‐acceptor arrangement, with a crossing angle of 52° between the long axes of DPNDI and Py. Spectroscopic measurements confirm strong intermolecular CT, and transient spectroscopy supports CT‐related excited‐state dynamics and the formation of long‐lived triplet states, while theoretical calculations indicate electronic structure favorable for intersystem crossing (ISC). Mechanistic studies indicate that both EnT and ET pathways are utilized in photocatalysis. Under LED irradiation in air, DPNDI‐Py delivers an average H 2 O 2 production rate of 18.47 ± 0.57 mmol g −1 h −1 coupled with an 83.7 ± 2.26% dehydroascorbic acid (DHA) yield from ascorbic acid (AA) oxidation. This work provides mechanistic insight into CT‐mediated photocatalysis, offering a design principle for organic photocatalysts.

title: Dual Metal Dopants Advance Near‐Room‐Temperature PbS‐based Thermoelectrics
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐cost lead sulfide (PbS) exhibits poor near‐room‐temperature (300–573 K) thermoelectric performance, limiting its practical applications. Here, Se/Te alloying coupled with dual‐metal Zn/Ge co‐doping is employed to enhance the near‐room‐temperature thermoelectric performance of n‐type PbS. Se/Te alloying forms a single‐phase PbS 0.5 Se 0.35 Te 0.15 solid solution (PbS(Se/Te)), where alloy‐induced mass and strain fluctuations enhance phonon scattering, reducing the lattice thermal conductivity from ∼2.09 W m −1 K −1 for PbS to ∼0.75 W m −1 K −1 at 300 K without compromising electrical transport. Zn/Ge co‐doping further optimizes carrier transport by regulating lattice defects and tuning carrier density, achieving a high carrier mobility of ∼522 cm 2 V −1 s −1 and an optimized carrier density of ∼1.03 × 10 19 cm −3 . The optimized PbS(Se/Te)+0.6‰Zn+5‰Ge sample exhibits an enhanced power factor of ∼20.23 µW cm −1 K −2 at 300 K, yielding a ZT of ∼0.54 at 300 K and an average ZT of ∼0.80 over 300–573 K. A seven‐pair thermoelectric module achieves a maximum temperature difference (Δ T max ) of ∼33.4 K at T h = 343 K, and a single‐leg device reaches a peak conversion efficiency of ∼7.2% under a temperature difference of 300 K. These results highlight the potential of Zn/Ge co‐doping for advancing n‐type PbS‐based materials toward near‐room‐temperature cooling and low‐grade heat recovery.

title: Nonlinear Kinetic Optimization via Strong–Weak Cosolvent Synergy in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Cosolvent engineering for aqueous Zn metal batteries has traditionally emphasized thermodynamic stabilization, whereas the kinetic dimension of Zn 2+ charge transfer—particularly in multi‐cosolvent systems—remains far less understood. Here we conduct a systematic study on a dual‐cosolvent electrolyte pairing a strong cosolvent (DMSO) with a weak cosolvent (DMC). Through spatial decoupling, the strong cosolvent directly coordinates to stabilize the primary solvation shell, while the weak cosolvent forms a dynamic outer‐shell buffer. This unique context modulates Zn–ligand binding, facilitates desolvation, and guides the formation of a regulated SEI. Consequently, this architecture preserves comparably high thermodynamic stability while unlocking a nonlinear kinetic optimization exclusive to the dual‐cosolvent regime. Using a multi‐descriptor framework, we demonstrate a ∼40% reduction in the charge‐transfer barrier relative to single‐cosolvent systems. This kinetic enhancement translates into robust practical performance, establishing strong–weak cosolvent synergy as a versatile design principle for next‐generation aqueous batteries.

title: Lumped Circuits Modeling of Dynamic Energy Transfer in Triboelectric Nanogenerators with Nonlinear Electromechanical Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT Powering autonomous electronics, sensors, and wearable systems using small‐scale daily mechanical energy is becoming increasingly important. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer a lightweight, flexible, and adaptable route for such applications, particularly when movements are involved. Here, we present a first‐of‐its‐kind unified dynamic energy‐transfer framework for TENGs, coupling their mechanical and electrical domains through a lumped element‐based equivalent circuit (LEEC) model. The framework captures time‐varying electrostatic behavior and key mechanical parameters, mass, damping, and stiffness, within a single predictive platform, enabling system‐level analysis of dynamic efficiency, impedance, resonance, and power transfer under different excitation conditions. The Thévenin equivalent model reveals that TENG performance is dynamically governed by excitation frequency, resonance, load matching, and surface charge density, approaching a time‐averaged theoretical efficiency of ∼54%. Experimental validation across devices with varied mechanical parameters shows close agreement with theory in electrical response and frequency‐dependent behavior. Furthermore, four borophene‐modified TENGs with different charge‐generation characteristics exhibit a systematic increase in electrical output and an estimated efficiency of up to 14.2% for the examined parameter space, supporting the model‐predicted dependence of energy‐conversion performance on surface charge density. The LEEC‐guided platform enables coupled energy and information harvesting through resonance‐enhanced capacitor charging and self‐powered road‐state sensing.

title: Characterizing Fill Factor Limitations in Perovskite‐Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Monolithic perovskite‐silicon tandem solar cells have achieved power conversion efficiencies approaching 35%. However, a significant gap remains to their thermodynamic limit, primarily due to fill factor ( FF ) losses. This work presents a methodology to identify the underlying mechanisms of the losses. Electroluminescence characterization reveals the potential FF without series resistance losses but cannot fully explain the observed FF limitations. An additional loss mechanism is the photoshunt, a phenomenon which the parallel shunt resistance apparently reduces under illumination in perovskite solar cells. Using an analytical model, we show that the photoshunt originates from competition between charge extraction, governed by transport‐layer properties and electric field, and recombination in the absorber and at interfaces. An equivalent circuit model quantifies its impact on subcell and tandem FF . Additionally, the two‐diode property of the Si subcell can also influence the tandem FF losses. Measurements on tandem devices under spectrally independent LED illumination show that photoshunt losses can be hidden under bottom‐cell‐limited conditions, explaining the preference for slightly bottom‐cell‐limited tandem designs. Reducing the photoshunt through improved charge transport and reduced recombination could enable operation closer to current matching while minimizing FF and efficiency losses.

title: Synergistic Surface‐Bulk Induction of Uniform Out‐of‐Plane (100) Orientation for High‐Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite thin films featuring out‐of‐plane oriented (100) crystallographic facets are pivotal for advancing the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells, owing to their superior charge transport properties and reduced deep‐level defect density. However, conventional single‐strategy modification approaches are typically constrained by limited control over crystal orientation and spatially heterogeneous orientation distribution, hindering the full exploitation of such beneficial facets. Herein, we present a surface‐bulk synergistic induction strategy that overcomes the limitations of single modification approaches, effectively promoting directional grain alignment and cooperatively guiding ordered out‐of‐plane growth during thermal annealing. Benefiting from the successful fabrication of a perovskite film with a uniform and predominant preferred orientation, the inverted perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.98% (certified 26.41%). Furthermore, the homogeneous texture and high intrinsic stability of the (100) facets enable the devices to retain 93.5% of their initial PCE after 1000 h of operational stability testing. This strategy effectively tackles the technical constraints of precursor solution regulation and solid‐state surface treatment, offering a novel research model for the precise modulation of perovskite thin film crystal facets and the secondary growth of polycrystalline thin films.

title: Competitive Solvation Structure in a Deep Eutectic Electrolyte Enables High‐Voltage LiCoO 2 ‐Based Pouch Cells With 5000‐Cycle Stability
abstract: ABSTRACT Anion‐rich solvation structures improve interfacial stability but often impede Li + desolvation, limiting fast‐charging and low‐temperature performance in high‐voltage lithium metal batteries. Unlike conventional high‐concentration or weakly solvating electrolytes, we propose a deep eutectic electrolyte (DEE) using succinonitrile (SN) and dimethyl sulfone (MSM) with competitive coordination capability. This design shifts the Li + solvation from aggregate clusters (AGGs) to a balanced AGGs/contact ion pairs (CIPs) distribution, which lowers the Li + desolvation energy barrier, enhances the transport kinetics, and endows the DEE with an ionic conductivity of 3.87 mS cm −1 and a Li + transference number of 0.81. MSM moderates excessive SN coordination, suppressing parasitic reactions on the anode, thereby enabling stable Li plating/stripping for 6800 h. A lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI)/lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiDFOB) dual‐salt system further optimizes interfacial chemistry, yielding a bilayer solid electrolyte interphase comprising an inorganic‐rich inner layer and a flexible organic outer layer. LiCoO 2 ||Li cells retain 97.1% capacity after 1000 cycles at 5C (3.0–4.5 V) and operate stably at −10°C. A 3.0 Ah LiCoO 2 ||Li pouch cell further delivers a high energy density of 417 Wh kg −1 , and LiCoO 2 ||graphite pouch cells sustain long‐term durability over 5000 cycles. This competitive solvation strategy effectively harmonizes kinetics and interfacial robustness for high‐voltage, fast‐charging DEEs.

title: Synthesis of Hetero‐Dimensional Mechanically Interlocked Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically interlocked polymer networks feature non‐covalent topological constraints between chains, in which the sliding of rings along axles allows adaptive deformation and energy dissipation. Yet these interlocking sites cannot cooperate, and the lack of direct stress transfer pathways between them leads to localized stress concentration at the chain level. Here, we report the synthesis of hetero‐dimensional mechanically interlocked networks (HDMINs), in which nanoporous two‐dimensional molecular sheets serve as multi‐threading platforms, each rigid sheet coupling its threaded chains into one cooperative network. One‐dimensional chains threaded through two‐dimensional polyaramid sheets in solution are captured by covalent crosslinking into a 2D/3D architecture. The mechanical bonds are preserved in this interlocking network, and their sheet‐coordinated sliding relieves local stress concentration and enhances energy dissipation. HDMINs are simultaneously stiffer, stronger and tougher than their non‐interlocked counterparts, showing that elevating the dimensionality of interlocking components converts discrete mechanical bonds into a cooperative network that bears load collectively.

title: Geopolitical exposure in cross-border electricity transmission: Evidence from Baltic desynchronization and interconnection disruptions
Energy poverty in an era of geopolitical instability: The role of Chinese FDI and south–south cooperation in Africa
abstract: The rising geopolitical fragmentation, driven by geopolitical tensions, conflicts and wars, has reshaped the global energy landscape, increasing uncertainty and vulnerability in energy markets. These disruptions present serious challenges for different economies in the Global South, where countries already face significant difficulties in facilitating energy transition and mitigating energy poverty. In this context, South-South cooperation may represent an important tool to address energy challenges, particularly through foreign investment. This study investigates the contribution of Chinese FDI to reducing energy poverty in Africa through different channels and whether conflict conditions influence the extent to which Chinese FDI contributes to improving energy outcomes. Our study contributes to the literature on the role of Chinese foreign capital in reducing energy poverty in Africa by examining both the underlying mechanisms and the potential role of conflict conditions in shaping these effects. To empirically explore this complex nexus, we rely on Structural Equation Modelling using a set of energy and socioeconomic variables from 2005 to 2022. The findings reveal a significant positive association between Chinese FDI and energy performance, with the prosperity channel representing the main mechanism. This association appears weaker in conflict-affected contexts, suggesting that geopolitical stability conditions the extent to which foreign investment is associated with improved energy outcomes. Policymakers in the region should consider creating a more attractive and stable investment environment to promote trade ties with Chinese companies, as these ties could be used as a tool to alleviate energy poverty.

Processing-induced self-organised triboelectric interfaces enable event-responsive cementitious composites
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Structural materials are commonly designed to bear loads passively, whereas sensing and energy-harvesting functions are typically implemented using externally attached devices that are vulnerable to damage and interfacial failure. Here we report a processing-induced strategy for forming self-organised triboelectric interfaces directly within fibre-reinforced cementitious composites during vibration-assisted casting. Through fresh-state flow, fibre migration, and grid-assisted interception, conductive and dielectric constituents assemble into local fibre-enriched contact regions, enabling intrinsic electromechanical transduction without post-fabrication assembly. Microstructural characterisation reveals local fibre enrichment and fibre-grid interweaving around the embedded coated grid, while first-principles calculations support the interfacial charge redistribution between polyvinyl alcohol and polytetrafluoroethylene. The composites retain high mechanical toughness while exhibiting stable electrical responses under low-frequency mechanical excitation, with signal amplitude scaling with load and contact configuration. After cracking, newly created internal interfaces continue to provide functional output, demonstrating damage-tolerant electromechanical activity. We further demonstrate an event-triggered sensing system in which the embedded interfaces serve as self-powered signal sources for wake-up and alert operations. This work establishes a processing-driven route for programming functional interfaces within structural materials and provides a basis for intrinsically responsive infrastructure components.

title: Pharmacological chaperone treatment with Cystadane in aspartylglucosaminuria: an open-label, phase Ib/II trial
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: This phase Ib/II investigator-initiated, open label trial aims to show the safety and efficacy of Cystadane (betaine) in aspartylglucosaminuria, a lysosomal storage disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline, in Finnish patients homozygous for the Finnish major mutation, aged between 3 and 17 years at study begin (recruited: 25, analyzed: 21). Oral Cystadane efficacy and safety were studied over 48 months. The primary endpoint of the study, reduction of glycoasparagines in the urine, was quantitatively determined using liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry and normalized to urine creatinine. Urine glycoasparagines are significantly reduced upon Cystadane treatment (by 68.6% ±10.8%; p = 0.000), and the study thus meets its primary endpoint. Our data show that Cystadane/betaine efficiently improves the main disease biomarker, and it is safe to use in aspartylglucosaminuria. Further studies should be carried out in a larger patient population over a longer time to demonstrate the effects on disease progression. EudraCT registration number 2017-000645-48.

title: Experience modifies the synaptome architecture in the developing and adult mouse brain
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Synaptome architecture describes the spatiotemporal distribution of highly diverse excitatory synapses throughout the brain. Whether and how this architecture is impacted by experience and sensory input is unknown. We found that environmental enrichment and monocular visual deprivation drive large-scale reconfiguration of excitatory synapse populations in more than one hundred regions of the mouse brain. Different experiences modify distinct subsets of synapse types and subtypes, with patterns aligned with protein turnover rates and connectome architecture. Similarity in experience-dependent reconfiguration during development and adulthood indicates shared mechanisms of synaptome adaptation across the lifespan. Our findings support a population-selection model in which experiences drive adaptation by selectively modifying synapse types and subtypes distributed across the brain. Experience-driven reconfiguration of synaptome architecture shares features with the response to aging, sleep deprivation, brain injury and genetic mutations, supporting a unifying principle of brain adaptation.

title: Frequency-tagged fMRI reveals dual mechanisms of attentional enhancement and suppression
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Selective attention biases competition between concurrent visual inputs, yet its computational implementation in the human cortex remains unclear. Using frequency-tagged fMRI (ft-fMRI), we resolve how attention shapes the spatiotemporal dynamics of competing stimulus-driven responses at fine spatial scales. Distinct cortical populations exhibit either in-phase synchronization (target enhancement) or anti-phase synchronization (surround suppression) with attended stimuli. Population receptive field mapping reveals a target–surround organization, with in-phase populations biased toward the attended target and anti-phase populations biased toward the surrounding visual field. Directed attention uniformly amplifies surround suppression across the visual hierarchy, consistent with a distributed suppressive field, whereas modulation of target-related activity increases hierarchically from V1 to hV4. Critically, modulation of surround suppression, but not target enhancement, predicts behavioral performance. These findings dissociate the mechanisms of target enhancement and surround suppression and reveal the computational architecture underlying biased competition in the human cortex, converging with recent primate electrophysiology research.

title: ATR promotes genome instability via CENP-A eviction from centromeres after prolonged exposure to genotoxic stress
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: DNA damage in interphase leads to genome instability in part by promoting missegregation of chromosomes lacking centromeres. Yet the complete molecular mechanisms linking DNA damage to centromere dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that prolonged exposure to genotoxic stress induces eviction of the histone H3 variant CENP-A. Displaced CENP-A relocalizes to nucleoli. This process depends on the DNA damage response kinase ATR and occurs in both human and mouse cells. We show that ATR promotes CENP-A eviction by promoting the nuclear localization of the AAA+ ATPase VCP through phosphorylation of Ser784, thereby destabilizing CENP-A-containing nucleosomes. Moreover, CENP-A localization to nucleoli relies on the nucleolar protein NPM1 and the canonical CENP-A chaperone HJURP, but not the H3 histone chaperones DAXX or ATRX. Importantly, ATR-dependent CENP-A eviction persists after cell-cycle re-entry and correlates with the emergence of CENP-A-deficient chromosomes, thereby linking DNA damage directly to segregation defects. Our findings identify a role for ATR in regulating centromere identity under stress and describe a mechanistic pathway that contributes to genome instability.

title: Functionally divergent RHOA mutations drive peripheral T cell lymphoma development by engaging a common neomorphic pathway
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: RHOA, a RAS superfamily member, is frequently mutated in peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL). These mutations are puzzling because variants have opposite effects on conventional RHOA signaling: some (e.g., RHOAG17V) inhibit normal RHOA function, whereas others (e.g., RHOAC16R) are constitutively active. Here we show that all PTCL-associated RHOA mutants acquire a non-canonical VAV1-like activity that activates the transcription factor NFAT. This activity is mediated by complexes between mutant RHOA and the RAP1GDS1607 isoform, is enhanced by T-cell receptor stimulation, and requires components of the T-cell receptor–VAV1 pathway, including PLCγ1 and calcineurin. Unlike canonical RAS superfamily signaling, this neomorphic activity does not require prenylation, the lipid modification anchoring RHOA to membranes. Genetic or pharmacological disruption of this pathway impairs RHOA-mutant PTCL in mouse models and patient-derived cells. These findings explain how mutations with opposing canonical effects converge on a shared oncogenic mechanism and reveal a potential therapeutic vulnerability in RHOA-mutant PTCL.

title: OsCPK17- and OsMPK6-mediated dual phosphorylation of OsPUB12 maintains OsPUB2-regulated OsPUB12 homeostasis and balances rice immunity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Numerous E3 ubiquitin ligases regulate plant immunity through mediating protein homeostasis, yet how homeostasis of E3 ligases is finely regulated per se remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal that the ubiquitin E3 ligase plant U-box 2 (OsPUB2) specifically interacts with OsPUB12 and targets it for ubiquitin-mediated degradation. In contrast to the immunity-suppressing role of OsPUB12, OsPUB2 positively regulates resistance to rice bacterial diseases and contributes to pathogen-associated molecular pattern-induced reactive oxygen burst and defense gene expression. Upon pathogen challenge, the calcium-dependent kinase OsCPK17 and mitogen-activated protein kinase OsMPK6 phosphorylate OsPUB12 at Thr154 and Ser460 in a temporally sequential manner. These two phosphorylation events oppositely regulate OsPUB12’s interaction with OsPUB2 and its subsequent ubiquitination, leading to divergent regulation of OsPUB12 stability and rice immunity. Our findings indicate that distinct phosphorylation of OsPUB12 by immune-related kinases OsCPK17 and OsMPK6 synergistically maintains OsPUB2-mediated OsPUB12 homeostasis, serving as a core mechanism to fine-tune rice immunity.

title: Pigment repression protects fungus from ferroptosis to maintain virulence
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fungal pathogens must adapt to host-derived stresses to establish infection, yet how secondary metabolite regulation contributes to this process remains poorly understood. Here, we show that Fusarium graminearum, a major cereal pathogen, suppresses the pigment aurofusarin biosynthetic gene cluster in response to host-derived iron excess, thereby preventing rubrofusarin-mediated ferroptosis and promoting invasive growth within wheat tissues. Rubrofusarin directly reacts with Fe²⁺ to form iron oxide complexes, resulting in intracellular iron accumulation, lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. Mechanistically, host-derived iron stress activates the HOG-MAPK pathway, leading to Hog1-dependent phosphorylation of the transcription factor FgSR. Phosphorylated FgSR recruits the histone deacetylase FgRpd3 to the aurofusarin biosynthetic gene cluster, establishing a repressive chromatin state that limits rubrofusarin production. Our findings reveal epigenetic repression of secondary metabolism as an adaptive strategy that enables fungal pathogens to withstand host-imposed iron stress, evade ferroptosis, and maintain virulence.

title: UMIche: a UMI-centric analysis platform for enhancing molecular quantification accuracy in bulk and single-cell sequencing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) are widely utilised in RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) technologies to eliminate polymerase chain reaction (PCR) duplicates, thereby improving the accuracy of molecular quantification. However, synthesis errors in UMIs during sequencing often compromise the reliability of UMI counting. While various computational methods have been developed for error correction, the lack of a unified benchmarking and validation framework impedes systematic evaluation and optimisation. Here, we present UMIche, an open-source, UMI-centric computational platform designed to enhance UMI-assisted molecular quantification. Its application to collapsing monomer and homotrimer UMIs across multiple bulk and single-cell sequencing protocols demonstrates effective PCR-duplicate removal. Across a broad spectrum of simulated and experimental datasets with ground truth, most UMI collapsing methods integrated into UMIche perform similarly under low-error conditions, whereas set-cover optimisation and majority voting show greater robustness as the UMI error profile becomes more pronounced. Together, these capabilities enable scalable UMI collapsing, systematic benchmarking, and method development to improve molecular quantification.

title: Nudix protein D250R promotes African swine fever virus infection by disrupting host ubiquitination machinery
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Numerous viruses have evolved diverse strategies to counteract host antiviral responses. African swine fever virus (ASFV), a large double-stranded DNA virus that threatens the global swine industry and food security, is thought to employ highly complex yet poorly understood mechanisms to facilitate infection. Here, we identify a previously uncharacterized strategy by which ASFV evades host antiviral defenses and maintains virulence. We show that ASFV infection progressively impairs the assembly of ubiquitin conjugates in host cells and that the ASFV-encoded Nudix protein D250R acts as a potent suppressor of cellular ubiquitination. Expression of D250R disrupts the host ubiquitination machinery in a manner dependent on its intact structure. Mechanistically, D250R directly binds ATP via its Nudix domain and inhibits ATP-dependent, E1-mediated ubiquitin activation, thereby suppressing ubiquitination-driven antiviral immune responses and promoting viral replication. Genetic deletion of the D250R gene markedly attenuates ASFV virulence while eliciting robust immune responses in pigs. Notably, immunization with the D250R-deficient virus confers complete protection against lethal challenge with a virulent ASFV strain. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized viral strategy to subvert host immunity and establish the D250R-deleted ASFV as a promising live-attenuated vaccine candidate for African swine fever control.
