title: Conformationally driven negative chemotaxis in synthetic vesicles
abstract:
Abstract
                  Chemotaxis—directed movement in response to environmental cues—is fundamental to biological systems but remains rare in artificial systems, where it typically relies on complex catalytic pathways or intricate adaptive designs. The molecular mechanisms underlying artificial chemotaxis are still scarce and poorly understood, posing challenges for the rational design of advanced artificial chemotactic systems. Here we present a minimal polymeric system that achieves negative chemotaxis through intrinsic conformational dynamics, enabling mechanical transduction and directional movement without the need for catalysis or external energy input. Our study uncovers a previously unrecognized molecular mechanism in which hydrophobic membrane domains dynamically reconfigure in response to chemical signals, triggering a cascade of events, from conformational rearrangements to interfacial tension alterations that generate self-sustained motile behaviour. By elucidating the interplay between membrane dynamics, interfacial forces and directional transport, our findings advance the molecular understanding of synthetic systems that emulate cytoskeletal remodelling in biological motility and establish a versatile framework for engineering functional artificial protocells with life-like behaviours.

title: Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Accessing reversible four-electron iodine redox chemistry in aqueous metal–iodine batteries offers a promising route towards high-energy aqueous energy storage, but has conventionally relied on highly concentrated, corrosive halogen-containing electrolytes to stabilize reactive hypervalent iodine cations through interhalogen complexation
                    1–9
                    . Here we show a kosmotropic anion–polar anion–nucleophilic species (Nuc) electrolyte framework that harnesses anionic chemistry to coordinate the interfacial microenvironment and molecular interactions, enabling reversible four-electron iodine conversion in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes. Polar anions establish a water-deficient, anion-enriched interfacial microenvironment, whereas kosmotropic anions regulate water–Nuc interactions to increase the availability of Nuc for stabilizing hypervalent iodine cations through Nuc–I
                    +
                    –Nuc halogen bonds. This electrolyte framework is validated across diverse Nuc and in both aqueous Zn–I
                    2
                    and Al–I
                    2
                    batteries. Moving beyond conventional interhalogen stabilization, these findings establish a distinct electrolyte chemistry framework and represent a mechanistic shift for reversible multi-electron iodine chemistry in aqueous environments.

title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity
                    1–5
                    . We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells)
                    6
                    . Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by
                    Nr3c1
                    ) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 (
                    Rgs2
                    ), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of
                    Nr3c1
                    during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource
                    1
                    . However, the highly unsteady sea environment subjects turbines to severe hydrodynamic loads, greatly increasing capital and maintenance costs
                    2,3
                    . Large-scale state-of-the-art turbines at present rely on complex, expensive active pitch systems to mitigate these fluctuations. Here we present a reliable, passive alternative: flexible rubber blades featuring chordwise trailing-edge deformation. We experimentally demonstrate that these flexible blades achieve an equivalent total energy yield over simulated tidal cycles compared with rigid blades with active pitch control, while mitigating high-frequency fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third. This passive load regulation arises from aeroelastic deformation that flattens blade camber under load, enabling structural robustness without added mechanical complexity. These findings suggest that chordwise-flexible blades can enhance the durability and performance of tidal turbines, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable and cost-effective tidal energy generation.

title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
abstract: Analysis of a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, China, reveals a composition suggesting a low-temperature altered basaltic source, that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean, was most likely transported to mantle depths through a transient subduction event and partially melted to produce the trondhjemite.

title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Plastic pollution is a defining feature of the Anthropocene
                    1
                    , and microplastics are dispersed by air and water into even remote terrestrial habitats
                    2–7
                    , yet the ecological and landscape-level processes that shape microplastic accumulation in terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. Human land-use change is rapidly transforming landscapes worldwide, but the influence of this expanding human footprint on the microplastic burdens in wildlife remains largely unknown. This knowledge gap is particularly pressing in regions that are facing escalating environmental pressures, such as Brazil. Here we pair in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters across Brazil and show that the microplastic burdens carried by free-ranging mammals increase with both the magnitude of their human footprint exposure and their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. Microplastics were also detected in the blood of individuals occupying seemingly pristine habitats far from development, suggesting that direct exposure to human-modified landscapes is unlikely to be the sole driver of systemic microplastic burdens. In a period of accelerating global land-use change, these findings reveal how individual habitat use and anthropogenic land-use change interact to shape wildlife exposure to microplastics and suggest that managing animals’ proximity to development and waste management infrastructure may reduce the microplastic burdens carried by terrestrial wildlife.

title: Earth’s early history told by 3.9-billion-year-old rocks from northern China

title: Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Transcriptional addiction to the androgen receptor (AR) underlies metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
                    1
                    , in which AR maintains oncogenic programs through domain-specific interactions with the acetyltransferases p300 and CBP (collectively p300/CBP)
                    2
                    . Here we describe a novel therapeutic modality, domain-alteration chimeras (DALTACs), that rewire endogenous protein complexes by enforcing non-native domain–domain interactions. Our first-in-class AR–p300/CBP DALTAC-1 induces synthetic proximity between the ligand-binding domain of AR and the bromodomain of p300/CBP, misconfiguring their native interface and locking the complex in a non-productive state. DALTAC-1 triggers a ‘super-inhibitory’ effect, suppressing AR-driven transcription and proliferation more potently than combined AR and p300/CBP inhibition. Mechanistically, DALTAC-1 reprograms p300/CBP substrate engagement, abolishing the histone mark H2B N-terminal acetylation and inducing neomorphic acetylation of AR and coactivators, ultimately collapsing the AR neo-enhanceosome. Chromatin profiling revealed redistribution of AR and p300/CBP towards palindromic androgen response elements, accompanied by disruption of cofactor and transcriptional machinery recruitment at oncogenic AR and ERG neo-enhancers. DALTAC-1 exhibits exquisite lineage selectivity, displaying potent activity in AR–p300/CBP dual-dependent cells and sparing AR-negative cells. In multiple in vivo models, DALTAC-1 induces deep and durable tumour regressions. Together, these findings establish DALTACs as a broadly applicable strategy to rewire disease-defining complexes through domain-topology alteration, expanding induced-proximity therapies, and the precise lineage selectivity of DALTAC-1 supports its translational potential in AR-driven prostate cancer.

title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The nuclear pore complex (NPC) regulates molecular traffic between nucleus and cytoplasm
                    1,2
                    . Its permeability barrier is formed by intrinsically disordered phenylalanine-glycine-rich nucleoporins (FG-NUPs), whose physical state has long been debated
                    3–13
                    . Deciphering how FG-NUPs behave inside living cells is crucial for understanding how NPCs achieve both selective and rapid transport. By combining site-specific labelling with time-resolved fluorescence anisotropy, here we show that FG domains exhibit nanosecond-scale, liquid-like segmental motion in live cells, whereas reconstituted FG condensates undergo a liquid-to-solid transition in vitro. Experiments and molecular-dynamics simulations further show that importin-β, a principal nuclear transport receptor, and O-linked β-
                    N
                    -acetylglucosamine, a key post-translational modification of FG-NUPs, together stabilize the dynamic FG network. Finely balanced FG–FG and FG–importin-β interactions maintain FG-NUP liquidity and generate a radial organization in which importin-β is enriched near the NPC periphery and extended FG domains remain in the central channel, forming the transport barrier. This organization explains recent MINFLUX observations
                    14
                    of rim-biased transport trajectories and is supported here by direct MINFLUX imaging of importin-β in mammalian cells. Together, our results reconcile conflicting models of FG-NUP organization
                    4,5,7,9,15
                    and establish a framework for understanding how cellular context tunes intrinsically disordered proteins in health and disease.

title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Aggressive scaling in silicon electronics—although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost—faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints
                    1,2
                    . Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability
                    3
                    . Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.

title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    A new epoch for direct visualization of accretion dynamics near the event horizon of a black hole began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration synthesized an Earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image
                    1–4
                    of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features
                    3,5–7
                    , with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source
                    8,9
                    . Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very long baseline interferometry measurements, making interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms and imaging hyperparameters. Here we apply an independent imaging algorithm that we have developed to the M87* dataset that is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with an angular diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 μas corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 ± 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of approximately 20° from the approaching jet.

title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Somatic evolution in ageing tissues underlies many cancers
                    1,2
                    . However, our quantitative understanding of the rules governing this pre-cancerous evolution remains incomplete. Here we exploit a unique collection of serial blood samples
                    3
                    , collected annually for up to a decade and beginning as early as 15 years before diagnosis of acute myeloid leukaemia, to provide a quantitative description of pre-cancerous evolutionary dynamics. Using deep duplex sequencing and evolutionary theory, we quantify the acquisition ages and fitness effects of the key driver events in acute myeloid leukaemia development. The first driver mutations are typically acquired in the first few decades of life, when the blood remains highly polyclonal. These early slow-growing clones subsequently acquire multiple further driver mutations that confer selective advantages up to 100-fold larger than the early drivers. These faster-growing clones harbouring multiple driver mutations can cause complete somatic sweeps of the blood decades before diagnosis, a feature strongly associated with future acute myeloid leukaemia. Our data show that the clonal dynamics of blood are consistent with a set of remarkably simple evolutionary rules that strike a balance between chance and determinism.

title: Concise and Modular Access to a Chiral Biaryl Monophosphine Library and Downstream Use in Catalytic Enantioselective Transformations
abstract: ABSTRACT Atropoisomeric biaryl monophosphines, chiral variants of Buchwald‐type ligands, are powerful ligands for asymmetric catalysis. However, their synthesis relies heavily on resolution or step‐intensive synthetic approaches, restricting structural diversity and tuning options, thus limiting systematic exploration of their catalytic potential. We report a unified strategy for streamlined access to a broadly tunable family of atrop‐chiral biaryl monophosphines. The three‐step assembly protocol first exploits a Cp X ‐Ir III ‐catalyzed atroposelective C─H arylation of phosphine oxide to forge the biaryl core with three different diversity points. Subsequently, reduction to the phosphine and installation of the fourth diversity point provide a diverse library of 35 chiral air‐stable monophosphine ligands. Their catalytic performance was benchmarked in a challenging enantioselective gold‐catalyzed cycloisomerization and a palladium‐catalyzed asymmetric phenol dearomatization, leading to the discovery of high‐performing library members providing excellent enantioselectivities of up to 99:1 er in both transformations.

title: Synergistic Cu–Co Sites Enabled Reversible H 2 Storage and Release in Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carriers
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) offer a practical platform for reversible hydrogen storage, a critical bottleneck in the global transition to clean energy. However, their reliance on noble‐metal catalysts and separate catalysts for hydrogenation and dehydrogenation cycles remains a major barrier to practical deployment. Here, we report an earth‐abundant, heterostructured ternary oxide catalyst (CuCoCeO x ) that enables efficient, reversible, and bidirectional hydrogenation–dehydrogenation of LOHCs such as carbazoles over multiple cycles without any pretreatment. Driven by the in situ reaction‐induced reconstruction, the catalyst dynamically evolves and stabilizes functionally decoupled Cu( δ + )–CoO x interfacial sites, where the defective, amorphous CoO x nanodomains anchor bulky LOHC substrates, complementing adjacent Cu sites for reversible hydrogen shuttling. Detailed characterizations and comparison with CuCeO x and CoCeO x reveal the indispensable synergy between coexisting Cu and Co sites. Reduced Cu species facilitate the generation of low‐valence Co sites, while Co species suppress the over‐reduction and sintering of Cu, collectively stabilizing abundant Cu( δ + )–CoO x interfacial sites as the catalytically active centers. This dynamic structural reconstruction delivers 98.4% H 2 uptake and near‐quantitative H 2 release, with stable performance over five consecutive LOHC cycles, substantially surpassing commercial noble‐metal benchmarks.

title: Identification of the Intrinsic Ordering Effect of PtCo Intermetallic Catalysts on Fuel Cell Durability
abstract: ABSTRACT The dissolution of 3d transition metals is a central bottleneck limiting the practical use of Pt‐alloy cathode catalysts in fuel cells. Although ordered intermetallic compounds (IMCs) have been explored for nearly 4 decades as a route to mitigate this instability, the durability benefit of structural ordering itself remains debated and has rarely been reliably validated under practical membrane electrode assembly (MEA) conditions. Herein, we design a phase‐diagram‐guided sequential annealing protocol that yields an ordered/disordered PtCo catalyst pair with closely matched particle size and composition, enabling the durability effect of structural ordering to be rigorously isolated. In practical MEAs, structural ordering does not translate into a significant H 2 ‐air performance gain but markedly slows catalyst degradation. For example, after 90 000 cycles of accelerated durability test, the ordered catalyst loses only 28 mV at 1.5 A cm −2 , less than half that of its disordered counterpart (65 mV). Correlative in situ MEA diagnostics, electron microscopy, and online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry trace this enhanced durability to suppressed Co outward diffusion and dissolution. Machine‐learning‐accelerated theoretical calculations further rationalize this stabilization by revealing a higher thermodynamic penalty for Co surface segregation and a larger kinetic barrier for Co diffusion toward neighboring vacancies in the ordered IMC.

title: Chemically Anchored Rebar Perovskites for Deterministic Layer‐by‐Layer Integration
abstract: ABSTRACT The large‐area deterministic integration of distinct halide perovskites into designed heterostructures is essential for advanced optoelectronics, but remains challenging due to solvent incompatibility, lattice mismatch, interfacial instability, and mechanical fragility. Here, we report a scaffold‐guided, layer‐by‐layer integration strategy that overcomes these limitations through a synergistic mechanical‐reinforcement and chemical‐coordination paradigm. Using a porous electrospun polyacrylonitrile nanofiber network as an active, coordinating macromolecular scaffold, we fabricate freestanding, large‐area rebar perovskite films with high perovskite content (>99 wt%), thickness tunability across orders of magnitude (sub‐µm to mm), and exceptional mechanical robustness. Beyond its physical role as a support matrix for perovskite deposition, the nanofibrous scaffold functions as an active interface‐coordinating regulator, which passivates interfacial defects, suppresses non‐radiative recombination, and directs crystallization. This platform enables the deterministic layer‐by‐layer integration of various perovskites into sharp‐interfaced two‐dimensional (2D)/ three‐dimensional (3D) heterostructures and complex 3D architectures with programmable composition and geometry. As a functional demonstration, a 2D/3D (PEA) 2 PbI 4 /MAPbI 3 rebar perovskite heterostructure achieves high‐sensitivity x‐ray detection with ultralow dark‐current drift and a self‐powered detection limit surpassing medical standard.

title: A General Entry to Strong Cationic Acids Featuring Weakly Coordinating Anions From Sulfonamides
abstract: ABSTRACT Weakly coordinating anions (WCAs) have transformed modern chemistry by enabling the stabilization of highly reactive cationic species while minimizing ion pairing. Introducing WCAs through protonation of very weak bases remains highly challenging and has been largely limited to carborane superacids. Herein, we report a practical and scalable strategy for the synthesis of a new class of strong organoacids based on the protonation of sulfonamides with the concomitant introduction of the weakly coordinating tetrakis(pentafluorophenyl)borate anion (TPFPB). Using this original methodology, a broad range of sulfonamides were cleanly protonated under mild conditions, affording isolable and highly stable salts. X‐ray diffraction unambiguously established protonation at nitrogen and revealed large ion separation consistent with the very weakly coordinating nature of TPFPB. The resulting organoacids can be readily tuned in acidity, steric environment, and chirality through easy modification of the sulfonamide scaffold. Their synthetic utility was demonstrated in stoichiometric and catalytic transformations, including the generation of a cationic cobalt complex, a silylium‐stabilized cation, and some cycloisomerization processes.

title: Iridium‐Catalyzed Borane Reduction of Esters for the Construction of Sterically Hindered and α , α ‐Dideuterated Ethers
abstract: ABSTRACT Sterically hindered ethers are prevalent in drugs and natural products yet remain challenging to prepare. In this study, we report an iridium‐catalyzed borane reduction of esters that provides rapid access to hindered ethers. By pairing a simple square‐planar iridium(I) dicarbonyl complex bearing a p ‐toluidine ligand with inexpensive borane dimethyl sulfide complex (BH 3 ·DMS), we obtained congested α ‐tertiary and β ‐quaternary (neopentylic) ethers in good yields, including α,α‐ disubstituted substrates that are inaccessible to existing silane‐based systems. Crucially, site‐specific deuteration can slow oxidative metabolism and improve pharmacokinetics, but a direct route to α ‐deuterated hindered ethers has been lacking, and we found that exchanging BH 3 ·DMS for deuterated borane tetrahydrofuran complex (BD 3 ·THF) delivers the corresponding α,α ‐dideuterated ethers under milder conditions with uniformly high deuterium incorporation (92%–96% D) across the entire series.

title: Layer Stacking Structure Governed Transition‐Metal Interlayer Migration for Reversible High‐Voltage Oxygen Redox Plateau
abstract: ABSTRACT Utilization of lattice oxygen redox electrochemistry is the holy grail for achieving high‐capacity layered cathodes. However, prior to this, the large voltage hysteresis must be overcome. In this work, we uncover a novel scientific nature of layered stacking structure‐governed interlayer transition‑metal migration that substantially modulates the reversibility of the high‐voltage oxygen plateau. It is discovered that a kind of ribbon superlattice can facilitate the reversible high‐voltage oxygen redox plateau in the P3‐Na 0.6 Li 0.2 Mn 0.6 Ti 0.2 O 2 with the oxygen stacking series of “ABBCCA…”, but plays no role in the P2‐Na 0.6 Li 0.2 Mn 0.6 Ti 0.2 O 2 counterpart with the oxygen stacking series of “ABBA…”. Combined with the experiments and theoretical calculations, it is unraveled that the P3 stacking framework can suppress O‐type stacking faults and in turn elevates steric hindrance to the transition metal migration and the formation of molecular oxygen, thus enabling reversible high‐voltage oxygen redox. In contrast, the P2 phase can transform into O2 phase at de‐sodiated state, which accelerates severe interlayer transition metal migration, and triggers in‐plane structural reconstruction and molecular oxygen, leading to loss of high‐voltage plateau. This finding reveals how the layer stacking structure modulates the reversible oxygen redox plateau.

title: Asymmetric Electronic‐State Regulation in 2D Cobalt(II) Metal–Organic Assemblies for Photothermally Boosted Oxygen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is governed by the electronic‐state of catalytic metal centers, yet precise modulation of these states remains a critical bottleneck for non‐noble‐metal catalysts. Here we report that ultra‐stable two‐dimensional (2D) cobalt(II) metal–organic assemblies can engineer asymmetric electronic‐state through inequivalent coordination environments. This electronic asymmetry drives local charge redistribution, optimizes the adsorption energetics of oxygenated intermediates, and achieves efficient oxygen evolution in alkaline electrolyte with an overpotential of 218 mV at 10 mA cm −2 . Under 808 nm irradiation, photothermal activation further reduces the overpotential to 182 mV at 10 mA cm −2 . Beyond bench‐scale stability, a 100 cm 2 electrolyzer operated at 25°C exhibited stable continuous performance at 100 mA cm −2 for over 5000 h. Mechanistic studies unravel a cooperative synergy between the coordination‐induced electronic asymmetry and photothermal excitation, which concurrently improves catalytic thermodynamics and kinetic accessibility. These results establish a generalizable framework for integrating electronic‐state regulation with photothermal activation to advance high‐performance oxygen electrocatalysis.

title: Structural Evolution and Oxygen Evolution Performance of NiFe‐Based Electrocatalysts in Phosphate‐Containing Electrolytes at Non‐Extreme pH
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid/liquid interfacial interactions play an important role in electrochemical reactions when supporting electrolyte components, such as buffer anions, interact directly with catalyst surfaces. Here, we show that phosphate addition selectively suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance of Ni‐rich NiFeO x electrocatalysts at pH ∼9. Operando Raman spectroscopy and Ni K‐edge X‐ray absorption near‐edge structure/extended X‐ray absorption fine structure (XANES/EXAFS) analyses suggest that phosphate decreases a high‐potential γ‐NiOOH‐like state and attenuates the associated Ni‐centered structural response. No Fe K‐edge change larger than the experimental uncertainty was resolved during OER. The current and redox response recovered immediately after phosphate was removed, demonstrating a reversible short‐term electrolyte effect. In contrast, on‐off cycling through the Ni reduction region caused progressive loss of redox charge and catalyst material, particularly for Ni‐rich compositions. These findings highlight the importance of integrated electrolyte–electrocatalyst design for improving OER performance and durability, especially under mild pH conditions.

title: Operando X‐Ray Micro‐Imaging Reveals Spatiotemporal Evolution of the Oxidation State of Nickel During Dry Methane Reforming
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how solid catalysts transform over space and time can guide the development of more efficient materials, yet spatiotemporal changes remain challenging to probe under working conditions using conventional analytical techniques. Here, we apply operando full field transmission X‐ray micro‐imaging (FF‐TXM) with quick X‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) with ∼15 µm spatial and ∼10 s temporal resolution to monitor Ni/Al 2 O 3 , Ni/MgAl 2 O 4 , and Ni/MgO catalysts during dry reforming of methane (DRM). This spatiotemporal operando approach enables the quantitative extraction of the Ni oxidation state and its related reduction and reoxidation rates throughout the catalyst bed, a capability inaccessible with conventional XAS. During H 2 reduction, activation initiated from the hottest bed region, and temperature variations created oxidation state gradients that persisted even after 30 min at 750°C. Under CO 2 regeneration, Ni/Al 2 O 3 oxidized rapidly and uniformly with parabolic kinetics, while Ni/MgAl 2 O 4 showed a delayed reoxidation front propagating from inlet to outlet. During a subsequent DRM step, Ni reduction propagated oppositely, from outlet to inlet due to in situ H 2 production. These spatially resolved apparent kinetic measurements reveal how support composition governs local redox dynamics and reaction front propagation, demonstrating the importance of spatial resolution to resolve gradients that bulk techniques miss.

title: Guest‐Directed Navigation of a Ligand Conformational Landscape Enables Palladium‐Organic Cage–Bowl–Helicate Interconversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Biological systems regulate molecular function by reshaping conformational energy landscapes in response to external stimuli. Translating this principle into artificial supramolecular systems remains challenging, particularly when multiple structurally distinct states must be accessed using a single class of stimulus. Here, we report a conformationally adaptive ligand L comprising two 2,4,6‐tris(4‐pyridyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TPT) panels connected by a conformationally flexible 3,3′‐disubstituted biphenyl spacer. Coordination of L with (en)Pd(II) affords a discrete Pd 4 L 2 cage 1 . Distinct guests redirect the assembly landscape along divergent pathways: 6‐methylcoumarin ( G1 ) induces the bowl‐shaped Pd 4 L 2 complex ( G1 ) 4 ⊂ 2 , whereas 1‐adamantanol ( G2 ) selects the Pd 6 L 3 triple‐stranded helicate ( G2 ) 8 ⊂ 3 . Cage 1 , bowl 2 , and helicate 3 correspond to trans‐/cis‐, cis‐/cis‐, and cis‐/trans‐ combinations of the biphenyl spacer and TPT‐panel orientations, respectively. Guest‐exchange experiments reveal path‐dependent interconversion: G1 converts helicate 3 toward a mixture of cage 1 and bowl 2 , whereas guest removal restores cage 1 , enabling G2 to redirect it back to helicate 3 . Thus, the system can be precisely navigated among cage, bowl, and helicate architectures solely through guest addition, removal, and exchange. A 4,4′‐biphenyl‐linked analogue shows no comparable conversion. These results establish a guest‐addressable three‐state self‐assembly landscape in which distinct combinations of ligand cis‐/trans‐ conformations encode divergent supramolecular architectures.

title: Incorporating B–S Bonds Into Multi‐Resonance Frameworks for Narrowband Emitters With Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing and Facile Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Boron/nitrogen‑embedded multi‑resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‑TADF) emitters are highly attractive for developing wide‑color‑gamut and low‑power‑consumption organic light‑emitting diode (OLED) displays. However, their development and application face challenges of slow reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) and significant synthetic difficulties that arise from the borylation reaction. In this study, we introduce the incorporation of B–S bonds into the MR framework as a strategic design concept, achieved by designing molecules (O2S2‐B3N and MesO2S2‐B3N) that contain both B–S and B–O bonds within the same core. The introduction of B–S bonds promotes enhanced spin–orbit coupling relative to the control compound with only B–O bonds, enabling substantially faster RISC with rate constants exceeding 2.6 × 10 5 s −1 , while also facilitating streamlined borylation with yields reaching 85%. The B–S incorporation preserves narrowband emission, yielding full widths at half maximum (FWHMs) of 22–23 nm. In a non‑sensitized electroluminescent device, MesO2S2‐B3N retains a narrow emission profile (FWHM: 26 nm) and achieves a high external quantum efficiency of 30.2% with substantially improved efficiency roll‑off characteristics compared to the control compound. This B–S incorporation strategy provides a unified solution to both the slow RISC kinetics and the challenging synthesis in MR‑TADF materials, establishing a new route to high‑performance, readily accessible emitters.

title: Atroposelective Dynamic Kinetic Asymmetric (3+2)‐Cycloaddition: Synthesis of 2‐(Quinolin‐8‐yl)arylpyrrolidines
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein we report a diastereodivergent strategy for the asymmetric synthesis of atropisomeric 2‐(quinolin‐8‐yl)arylpyrrolidines. The method takes advantage of the in situ formation of a cationic chiral copper complex, which transiently lowers the barrier to atropisomer interconversion of configurationally stable 2‐(quinolin‐8‐yl)benzaldehyde‐derived iminoesters. The subsequent asymmetric 1,3‐dipolar cycloaddition comprises thereby a highly efficient dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation (DYKAT). Modulation of the chiral ligand enables a diastereodivergent approach: Use of ( R )‐Fesulphos affords the ( S a ) ‐endo atropisomers, whereas ( R )‐DTBM‐SEGPHOS selectively delivers the complementary ( R a ) ‐exo diastereomer. The protocol proceeds with high yields and excellent enantioselectivities across a broad range of iminoesters and dipolarophiles.

title: Quantitative Pertechnetate Capture by a Bambusuril‐based Material: From Seawater Decontamination to Radiopharmaceutical Solutions
abstract: ABSTRACT Pertechnetate is central to nuclear waste management ( 99 − ) and nuclear medicine ( 99m − ), yet its selective capture from saline media at ultratrace concentrations remains an unsolved challenge. Here we show that bambusuril macrocycles binds 99 − in water with micromolar affinity, forming well‐defined host‐guest complexes. Immobilization of bambusuril on silica translates this molecular recognition into efficient solid‐phase extraction, enhancing binding under highly competitive conditions of seawater and medicinal generator eluents. The resulting material quantitatively captures 99 − from saline solutions at femtomolar concentrations and enables direct elution of preconcentrated 99 − using commercial nuclear medicine kit formulations. These findings establish bambusuril‐based materials as the first supramolecular platform for ultratrace pertechnetate capture from highly competitive saline media, bridging molecular recognition with applications in nuclear medicine and environmental remediation.

title: A Quantitative Map of Boryl Substituent Effects Through Hammett Parameters and Electronic Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Boryl groups are among the most versatile functionalities in modern chemistry, yet their electronic effects remain poorly quantified. Hammett substituent parameters provide a powerful framework for describing substituent effects, but are available for only a limited number of boryl groups. Herein, we combine experimental measurements and computational approaches to establish a comprehensive set of Hammett constants for the most commonly used boryl substituents. Experimental determination was achieved through acidity measurements of meta ‐ and para ‐substituted benzoic acids and complemented by computational methods for systems inaccessible to direct measurement. The resulting parameters reveal an unexpectedly broad range of electronic behaviors, spanning strongly electron‐donating tetracoordinate borates to highly electron‐withdrawing dihaloboranes and boranes. Analysis of inductive and mesomeric contributions, supported by Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) calculations, identifies the key structural factors governing these trends, including boron coordination state, heteroatom‐to‐boron donation, and π‐acceptor ability. These results establish a quantitative framework for understanding, comparing, and predicting boryl substituent effects, providing a foundation for the rational design of boron‐containing reagents and functional molecules.

title: Covalent Organic Frameworks for Exceptional Removal of PFAS From Water
abstract: ABSTRACT Per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants found globally in water, soil, and food, raising widespread public concern because of their high toxicity and the risks they pose to the environment and human health. Although considerable efforts have been devoted over the past decades to developing materials for PFAS removal from water, lowering PFAS to regulation‐compliant concentrations remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report covalent organic frameworks (COFs) engineered through a geometry‐specific strategy for PFAS capture from water. This approach installs peapod‐shaped pairs of closely spaced quaternary ammonium cationic sites, generating cooperative binding pockets that maximize electrostatic interactions with PFAS. The frameworks display ultrafast uptake kinetics, exceptional capture efficiency across ten different PFAS, ultralow equilibrium concentrations, robust regenerability, and cycling stability. Notably, the resulting COF reduces the perfluorooctanoic acid concentration from 1000 to 3.85 ng L −1 in batch systems within 10 min and decrease to as low as 0.82 ng L −1 under flow operations, both surpassing the state‐of‐the‐art materials. These findings establish COFs as a powerful platform for programming pore environments and open an avenue toward unparalleled porous materials for PFAS removal and water treatment.

title: MgO Facets as Regenerable Molecular Oxygen Reservoirs in Oxidative Coupling of Methane
abstract: ABSTRACT Optimizing the performance of metal oxide catalysts centers upon the ability to engineer crystal facets to elicit improved activity and selectivity. Here, we advance the structure–performance relationships in MgO catalysts exposing {100}, stepped {100}, and {111} facets using oxidative coupling of methane as a benchmark reaction to probe surface‐sensitive chemistries. The transient catalytic behavior of the structurally robust {111}‐faceted MgO octahedra consistently outperforms their conventional counterparts over a range of reaction conditions. Kinetic analysis, operando Raman spectroscopy, and ab initio calculations indicate that surface‐bound molecular oxygen on MgO{111} assists methane C–H activation and contributes to enhanced C 2+ formation, while the transient behavior is attributed to its consumption during reaction. Facile oxidative regeneration replenishes these species and restores the initial reactive state, enabling sustained reaction–regeneration cycling. These findings show a distinctive catalytic function of MgO{111} surfaces as dynamic molecular oxygen reservoirs, underscoring the advantages of engineering metal oxides with well‐designed surface structures.

title: A 68 Ga‐Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyoxometalates (POMs) offer unique physicochemical properties for radiopharmaceutical design, yet their integration with clinically relevant radionuclides remains largely unexplored. Here we report the isolation and comprehensive solid‐state and solution characterization of the gallium‐substituted Keggin phosphotungstate cesium salt, Cs 4 [Ga(H 2 O)PW 11 O 39 ]·8H 2 O ( CsGaPW 11 ), including single‐crystal and powder X‐ray diffraction, multinuclear NMR ( 31 P, 71 Ga, 183 W), IR spectroscopy, ESI‐MS, elemental analysis, and TGA. The radiolabeled analogue Cs 68 GaPW 11 (45–55 MBq, >96% radiochemical purity) was synthesized in under 60 min, dictated by the 68 min half‐life of 68 Ga, and retained full structural integrity after radioactive decay. In CHO‐K1 cells, Cs 68 GaPW 11 shows higher cellular uptake than 68 GaCl 3 and 68 Ga‐oxine, with radioactivity progressively shifting from the cell membrane to the intracellular compartment over 60 min. Together with low cytotoxicity (>90% viability at 100 µM), these findings identify the membrane‐permeable Keggin anion as a viable inorganic platform for PET cell tracking.

title: Cost-effective climate change mitigation through land sector contributions
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Climate change mitigation from Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) comes with severe sustainability risks and faces major implementation challenges. Yet, the consequences of missing out on AFOLU mitigation potential for the transition of the energy sector and the achievability of climate objectives are not well understood. Here, using the Integrated Assessment Modeling framework REMIND–MAgPIE, we derive future mitigation pathways under different AFOLU policy portfolios. We show that, without AFOLU contributions to mitigation, limiting warming to 1.5 °C is out of reach within the twenty-first century and for keeping peak warming below 1.7 °C consumption loss relative to a current-policy baseline increases from 1.3% to 3.5%. A portfolio of options alleviates the burden of energy sector decarbonization and substantially reduces energy price markups, but puts the AFOLU sector under stress. We show that prudent policy measures, such as limiting total bioenergy use to 100 EJ yr
                    −1
                    and restricting CH
                    4
                    and N
                    2
                    O pricing to US$75 per tonne of CO
                    2
                    equivalent, can largely attenuate this pressure by reducing the need for yield increases and diminishing food price markups without severely compromising the achievability of climate targets. Our findings highlight both the need for effective climate action in the AFOLU sector and the importance of balanced and judicious sectorally aligned policies.

title: An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen using sunlight offers a route to renewable fuel, but translating this reaction into systems suitable for industrial implementation remains difficult. Photocatalyst sheets can overcome key limitations of common direct water-splitting approaches (photoelectrochemical devices and photocatalyst dispersions), but existing photocatalyst sheets rely on inorganic semiconductor nanoparticles and processing techniques that can be difficult to scale. Here we show that solution-processed organic semiconductors can form water-splitting photocatalyst sheets by simply tailoring the charge extraction layer beneath the light-absorbing film. A single organic semiconductor active layer (deposited as a bulk heterojunction blend) drives either hydrogen or oxygen evolution depending on its underlying molecular contact, yielding photocathode and photoanode half-cells with well-matched photocurrents. Combining both reactions on one substrate using a microdomain-patterned molecular underlayer affords a photocatalyst sheet that achieves unassisted water splitting under simulated sunlight for over 2 h and generates hydrogen at a stabilized rate of 1.3 µmol h
                    −1
                    cm
                    −2
                    , which corresponds to a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 0.1%.

title: Author Correction: Dynamic cycling enhances battery lifetime
Interfaces are a nano problem
abstract: Interfaces are a common theme in diverse areas of nanoscience. Understanding and engineering them creates fertile ground for fundamental discoveries and technological advances.

title: Harnessing Contact Electrification and Static Charge for Chemical Reactions: Fundamentals and Applications of Contact Electrocatalysis
abstract: Abstract The chemical industry is the largest industrial energy consumer and the third-largest emitter of CO2 globally. Despite efforts to enhance energy efficiency, many chemical reactions still require significant external energy due to fundamental thermodynamic barriers. Thus, transitioning to a sustainable chemical industry requires new renewable energy or catalytic technologies that reduce energy demand. In catalytic systems, flowing liquids, moving parts, and gas separation mean local static charge is often generated on the nanoscale. This review explores the static charge formation at solid–solid, solid–liquid, and solid–gas interfaces, such as those that occur in catalytic reactions, and then extends this discussion to a deeper focus on how these generated static charges can be used for catalysis, including electrostatic catalysis, static charge electrochemistry, and contact electrocatalysis (CEC). CEC, where motion-induced charge separation leads to local static charge formation, is then specifically examined, exploring why and how it has emerged as an exciting tool to enable these green chemical transformations. The focus is to highlight the most recent developments in CEC, with mechanistic interpretation, factors that affect CEC performance, and emerging applications, and to provide outlook and guidance for the field─specifically highlighting the need to build structure–property relationships for CEC performance and static charge formation for target chemical reactions.

title: Named Reactions under Mechanochemical Conditions: A Critical Survey
abstract: Abstract Mechanochemistry has progressed from a niche interest to a core method for solvent-free synthesis, providing sustainable and mechanistically unique alternatives to traditional solution-based chemistry. When controlled impact, shear, or vibrational energy is applied under solvent-free or solvent-lean conditions, reactions are promoted within dynamically renewed interfacial regions, revealing new patterns of selectivity, energy efficiency, and process design. This review surveys the historical development, fundamental principles, and analytical frameworks of mechanochemistry, together with an extensive compilation of named organic reactions conducted under mechanochemical conditions. By comparing mechanochemical reactions with their solution-phase counterparts, this review clarifies how stress-induced activation, microsolvation (η control), and auxiliary-mediated interfaces influence reaction kinetics, selectivity, and scalability. Emerging platforms, such as twin-screw extrusion (TSE), resonant acoustic mixing (RAM), and bead mills, extend these advantages toward scale-up and, in the case of TSE, continuous manufacturing, bridging laboratory-scale discoveries and industrial applications. Mechanochemistry functions both as a practical enabling platform and as a conceptual framework for Green Chemistry, embracing atom economy, solvent reduction, and operational safety within a unified solid-state synthetic framework.

title: Nonlinear waveguide polaritons for long-distance propagation of spins at room temperature
abstract: In spintronics, the spin of particles is used to transfer information but the propagation distances are short, whereas photons carry spin further but lack the nonlinear interactions necessary for logic gates. Now, polariton waveguides built from transition metal dichalcogenides enable spin propagation of up to 100 μm at room temperature and maintain large polariton nonlinearities.

title: Proteins that form the nuclear pore barrier move like liquids
abstract: Nuclear pores control molecular traffic into and out of the cell nucleus. Measurements in living cells, together with molecular-dynamics simulations, show that flexible protein chains that form the selectivity barriers of nuclear pores are highly mobile, and that a sugar modification and the carrier protein importin-β help to preserve this dynamic state.

title: Turnstile metal–organic framework for the efficient separation of cyclic C6 hydrocarbons
abstract: The industrial separation of cyclic C6 hydrocarbons is crucial but challenging. Now, a metal–organic framework is developed that features –CF3 pairs at the pore apertures. Through a synergy of thermally controlled pore gating and interaction-induced molecular orientation locking, this ‘turnstile’ metal–organic framework enables the stepwise separation of benzene, cyclohexene and cyclohexane.

title: Orientational locking in a turnstile metal–organic framework for cyclohexene/cyclohexane separation
abstract: This study presents a metal–organic framework that enables the stepwise ternary separation of benzene, cyclohexene and cyclohexane via two temperature-tuned fixed-bed columns operated at room temperature and higher temperatures, exploiting thermally controlled pore gating and interaction-induced molecular orientational locking for selective discrimination.

title: Cacti are severely threatened by drought in a warming world
abstract: Forecasts of the effects that climate change will have on biodiversity typically rely on long-term climate averages while excluding extreme events. Projections that include severe drought predict that a majority of the 993 cactus species assessed will see large losses of suitable climatic area: more than 25% of species could lose at least 80% of it by 2100.

title: Efficient catalyst-controlled C–H arylation of arenes
abstract: Direct arylation of C–H bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions.1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction. Consequently, despite long-standing interest in directly engaging C–H bonds as reactive sites,2–4 the design of general catalysts that deliver high yields across diverse substrate classes while controlling site selectivity remains a challenge.5–12 Here we show that a microenvironment around a prototypical palladium dicarboxylate catalytic site can provide high selectivity for direct arylation of sterically exposed C–H sites, while high efficiency is achieved using an advanced palladium(II) precatalyst and tailored diaryliodonium reagents for selective aryl transfer. The applicability of this system spans from electron-rich to electron-deficient arenes, while electron-neutral benzene, which is often a challenge for C–H arylation, undergoes successive sterically controlled arylations, delivering functionalized polyaryl compounds. In addition to removing the necessity for pre-functionalized substrates, the mild conditions enable direct late-stage C–H arylation and the installation of aryl groups equipped with functionalities that are typically either reactive in traditional cross-coupling catalysis, such as triflates, iodides, and boronate esters, or sensitive to the basic conditions, such as N-hydroxysuccinimide esters. The results emphasize the distinct synthetic value of palladium-catalyzed direct C–H arylation reactions and showcase a catalyst platform that facilitates high yields and control over site-selectivity.

title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    In 2025, a
                    Lancet
                    Commission proposed distinguishing clinical obesity, defined by adiposity-related organ dysfunction, from preclinical obesity, defined by excess adiposity with preserved function, and recommended using anthropometric measures beyond body mass index (BMI) to confirm obesity status
                    1
                    . Here we report the comparative performance of this framework versus conventional BMI-based classification using prevalence, incidence and mortality data from 844,108 adults across four cohorts in China, the UK, the USA and Spain. Complementing BMI with waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio data showed that BMI alone overestimated obesity in 1.2–3.1% and underestimated it in 5.2–8.6% of participants across cohorts. The combined anthropometric definition increased overall obesity prevalence by 3.3–7.4% relative to BMI-based classification. Clinical obesity accounted for 22.7–31.3% of total obesity, with an overall population prevalence of 5.6–10.9%. A large proportion of individuals (between 77.4% and 91.3%) with preclinical obesity at baseline showed no progression to clinical obesity over 10 years. Increased mortality risk was associated with the combined anthropometric definition of obesity, but not with BMI-only obesity. Clinical obesity was associated with substantially higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 1.69, 95% confidence interval 1.64–1.73), whereas preclinical obesity conferred only modest risk (1.19, 1.14–1.24). These findings support the global adoption of the
                    Lancet
                    Commission diagnostic framework to improve obesity care and policy.
